attested.verifiedBy: The gated half is done: the scale is emitted in absolute points with Japanese leading strictly greater than Latin at every step, lineBreakStrategyIOS and textBreakStrategy are passed for Japanese only, and scripts/verify-font-coverage.mjs parses cmap formats 4 and 12 with a --prove mode that builds a synthetic TTF to watch it discriminate. What remains is the ASSET: F-076 carries the Noto Sans JP subset, the subsetting pipeline, the NOTICE.md licence entry and the wiring into gate:content. Until then the app falls back to the platform face, the checker exits 1 rather than reporting a green run as coverage, and this stays outstanding.

features.notes: DONE. 11 increments, each committed with the gates green at its own boundary. THE FEATURE OPENED BY FINDING ITS OWN CONTRACT WRONG: the acceptance criteria said to build a Next.js 16 app with Server Components, axe and a `web-perf` gate, nine months after ADR-0051 retired the web surface and four features after apps/mobile shipped. Gate 0 was green throughout, because a criterion naming a surface that no longer exists is still a well-formed string — F-074 records that guard, and the sweep also found docs/PRD.md only HALF corrected after the rehaul. FOUR ADRs: 0054 React Native primitives (0034 superseded); 0055 the a11y gate under jest-expo, DECIDED BY RUNNING IT — the spike found that jest-expo@57 is built on Jest 29 internals and dies against jest@30 before a single test, and that RNTL@14 and jest-expo@57 are not aligned; 0056 the enumerated catalogue, because fallback is the core behaviour of every runtime i18n library; 0057 a bundled Noto Sans JP subset generated from the corpus, possible only because the corpus is an immutable signed bundle at a pinned version. WHAT THE CHECKS CAUGHT, mostly in my own work: the CSS line-height ratio would have rendered a 15pt line with 1.65 POINTS of leading; icon.check/alert/cross resolved to NOTHING, so NFR-9 was true of the type and unproven of the render; the conformance suite rejected my own Swatch for missing disabled/loading and for rendering focus and active identically; gate 9 rejected the home screen for five predicted foreground.3 findings AND nine unpredicted ones, because the screen read useColorScheme() itself and so rendered LIGHT when asked for dark; a11y-scope found Status and Icon in no registry, and had a bug of its own that skipped generic components; tsc rejected textBreakStrategy: high_quality (RN wants camelCase) and found ColorSchemeName includes "unspecified", which is exactly the no-preference case the theme fallback exists for; and the claims lint rejected a doc comment of mine that quoted two banned phrases as examples. MUTATION RUNS THAT CHANGED THE DESIGN rather than confirming it: deleting the RN text-inheritance model turned only ONE of two tests red, because the node then falls back to 14px which is ALSO below the large-text floor — the 22px counterpart fixture exists because that experiment was run. And one a11y proof case stayed green because RN DERIVES accessibilityState.disabled from the disabled prop, so the case was wrong, not the gate. GATE 8 ACTIVATED LAST, after being watched fire six times against real components, with ciStep:true and a real CI step whose removal was watched turning gate 0 red — it had been specified as ciStep:false with the mirror check skipping it, which would have made it read `active` while never executing. SPLIT OUT RATHER THAN LEFT AS NOTES: F-074 (gate 0 sees a retired-surface criterion), F-075 (motion may not animate a colour — not a lint, because knowing the node IS a sample needs composition static analysis cannot see), F-076 (the font asset). THREE CRITERIA ATTESTED: the Japanese being reviewed rather than machine-translated (blocked on OQ-5, as F-012 is), on-device kinsoku, and VoiceOver/TalkBack with text at 200 percent. `e2e` was removed from verification because `pnpm test:e2e` exits 1 by design while no surface declares the script — verified by running it.

features.title: Colour Atlas and colour detail
acceptance: Every corpus entry reachable in 3 interactions or fewer from the atlas root
Reads the signed corpus bundle at a pinned version with its digest verified at load, and renders with no network access
Browsing renders values read from the published bundle; the engine is called for derived answers, never to recompute a value the bundle already carries
Colour detail shows names in four forms, every coordinate system, provenance, relations, palettes and CVD appearance
Every swatch has an accessible name and its numeric value
features.notes: DONE. The corpus reaches a reader. THE ATLAS ROOT LISTS ALL 120 WITH NO FILTER, which is what makes criterion 1 checkable by walking the rendered tree rather than counting interactions by hand — a design where a family must be chosen first would make "reachable" depend on a filter set nobody enumerated. The detail screen carries all four names, every coordinate system, provenance, relations, palettes and colour vision, and it renders the FR-21 `unknowns` reason where a value is null, which is the only place those reasons mean anything. F-084’S ATTESTED CRITERION IS DISCHARGED HERE: a self-reviewed entry says "Checked by its own author" in words, asserted over the render. TWO DECISIONS IN ADR-0066. The digest function must be SYNCHRONOUS — expo-crypto is async only, and verification behind a promise can be outrun by the first render, at which point "verified at load" has become "verified shortly after we started drawing". @noble/hashes is audited and still not trusted on arrival: assertSha256 runs it against published vectors first, including 藍鼠, which catches a hasher encoding UTF-16. And the bundle ships as generated TEXT with the LEDGER’s digest beside it as two exports from two files, because a bundle checked against a checksum it carries verifies itself. WHAT THE CONFORMANCE SUITE CAUGHT WAS STRUCTURAL. The filter chips and the search box were a Pressable and a TextInput inside Atlas.tsx, where NOTHING checks them — the component suite covers the library, the screen suite covers screens as `static` subjects, and an interactive control in a screen file falls between the two. Chip and SearchField are now @irodora/ui components and the Atlas is `static`. The move immediately produced two more findings: the chips declared no minWidth (a chip is content-width, so "All" sits under 44px), and the suite’s OWN model of "interactive" was press-only, so a SearchField was reported as "nothing in the tree responds" — which would have pushed it to claim a kind it does not have. pressableNodes now counts onChangeText. That third one is the reusable lesson: when a check objects, ask whether its model is the thing that is wrong. TWO BUGS THE SOURCE CAUGHT BEFORE ANY TEST COULD. simulateDichromacy takes RGB, not XYZ — both are Triple, so passing entry.color.xyz type-checks and returns a plausible wrong colour, the same trap as handing OKLCh to ΔE00. And it THROWS for tritan by design, because VIENOT_1999 has no tritan entry and publishing one would invent a value the source does not. The block uses Machado’s simulateAnomalous at severity 1 over the bundle’s encoded sRGB, and the copy says "red-weak" rather than "protanopia" — different conditions, and the label has to match the model that produced the swatch. BOUNDARY #24 ENFORCES CRITERION 3: a screen may not import xyzTo* or gamutMap*, because recomputing a bundled value looks identical, passes every test, and returns TODAY’s engine’s answer for a version published under an older one (FR-10, E-001). srgbToHex is deliberately NOT banned — the CVD block encodes a simulated triple — and that distinction is a SILENT DECOY the rule must accept. verify-guards gained the concept and now reports overreach as its own failure with its own fix: 25 boundaries, 1 decoy. 93 NEW MESSAGE KEYS, and the existing i18n tests caught two design errors on the way in. `atlas.of` was an English sentence pattern forced onto Japanese and was DELETED rather than translated. And IDENTICAL_BY_DESIGN is capped at three deliberately, so the colour-space names became NOTATION_KEYS — a category governed by an anchored shape and a length cap instead of a longer list of favours; the ad-hoc list is now EMPTY, and its decoy caught the first shape admitting "Not recorded". E-017 FIRED A SECOND TIME, from the ja catalogue rather than the corpus: 105 uncovered codepoints of ordinary UI Japanese. The link is not only about rare kanji in colour names. E-022 IS NEW: the app reads a COPY of the bundle, so a publish without a regenerate ships a stale corpus with every gate green. Guarded by `--check` in gate 11, watched failing first. HOME NOW LINKS TO THE ATLAS. Without it the whole feature would have been the shape of a tested module nobody wired up — 120 colours, every gate green, and nothing on screen leading to any of them. F-090 (Japanese taxonomy vocabulary) and F-091 (the e2e harness) filed rather than left as comments; the Atlas shows `blue-grey` in both locales today and says so.

attested.criterion: Reads the signed corpus bundle at a pinned version with its digest verified at load, and renders with no network access
attested.verifiedBy: THE FIRST HALF IS DISCHARGED AND THE SECOND IS NOT. Verification at load is real and proven: loadPublishedVersion has no warn mode, the app is its single call site, the text comes from the generated module and the expected digest from the LEDGER, and five mutations over the real pinned bundle are watched being refused — an edited entry, an edited derived value, an entry removed where every survivor still hashes, and the right bundle against a wrong digest. THE NETWORK CLAIM IS NOT CHECKED ANYWHERE. "renders with no network access" is a statement about what the process does, and a render-tree assertion cannot see a socket. Gate 7 is `pending`, nothing declares a test:e2e task, and e2e-scope fails for want of a surface to run — so `e2e` was listed in this feature’s verification and could not be run. F-091 carries the harness; F-039 already carries the matching attested criterion for the offline journey. Nothing in F-018 makes the network half of this criterion true, and it is recorded here rather than allowed to pass on the strength of the half that is.

features.title: Colour Compare
acceptance: DeltaE00, per-axis differences, OKLCh delta, CVD separation and contrast, each with its units and computation space
Tabular numerals, aligned columns, copyable values

attested.criterion: Tabular numerals, aligned columns, copyable values
attested.verifiedBy: THE FIRST TWO ARE ASSERTED AND THE THIRD IS NOT FULLY. The rendered tree is checked for the font variant on more than twenty numeric nodes, with a decoy proving a Text without the prop carries none — so "tabular" reaches the node. What no render-tree assertion can reach: whether the FACE actually has equal-width figures at every weight, which is a property of the subset Noto Sans JP ships and needs a device or a glyph-metrics read; and whether `selectable` produces a usable copy affordance on iOS and Android, which is platform behaviour rather than a prop. `selectable: true` is asserted on every tabular value, so what is owed is the device leg, not the wiring.

features.notes: DONE. Compare shows ΔE00, the per-axis CIELAB and OKLCh deltas, CVD separation and both contrast readings — each with its unit AND the space it was computed in, which is what FR-48 actually asks for. "ΔE00 4.2" without "CIELAB (D65)" beside it is a different claim from the one the engine made, and this repository has already been bitten by exactly that. A TOKEN THAT HAD NEVER REACHED A PIXEL. `nativeNumericFeature` was emitted from the manifest, asserted against it by its own test, and consumed by NOTHING since F-017 — so C9 ("numbers are tabular", annotated mandatory) was true of a constant and false of every screen. `Text` gained a `numeric` prop reading the token, asserted over the rendered node with a decoy: a Text WITHOUT the prop must carry no font variant, or the assertion would pass for a component applying it unconditionally. Recorded as a lesson and filed as F-092, because the shape — a generated value whose only reader is its own emitter test — is not specific to this token. THE METRIC SET IS A MODULE, NOT A COMPONENT. A number a screen computes inline is a number no test can reach without rendering. `compare.ts` is asserted on PROPERTIES rather than by re-running the arithmetic: zero against itself, ΔE00 and WCAG symmetric, APCA deliberately NOT — swapping the pair swaps both readings, with a decoy proving the two are genuinely different numbers rather than one value returned twice. THE PINNED VALUE WAS A GUESS AND THE TEST CAUGHT IT. I wrote 76.86 ΔE00 for usu-gami to soko-zumi without computing it; the engine returned 89.73. That is the argument for pinning a number rather than describing a pair in words, and the comment now records which it was. It is also E-003’s destination end: a change to `deltaE00` now fails on a surface as well as in the golden set. NO COLOUR MATHS IS WRITTEN HERE. `hueDelta` already exists, and the hue axis is the one place subtracting two stored numbers is wrong — the mean of 350° and 10° is 0°, not 180°. Separation shows its DECOMPOSITION rather than only a score, because a number labelled "62" with nothing beside it is a grade nobody can check. THREE KEYS WERE DROPPED RATHER THAN TRANSLATED. `:1`, `°` and `/100` are fragments of a formatted number, not symbol names, and NOTATION_SHAPE rejected them — correctly. Keeping them meant widening the shape until a fragment of prose could qualify, or three more favours in a list capped at three. The words stayed in the catalogue; the punctuation moved into the value. E-017 fired a THIRD time, for 3 codepoints; three firings in three features is the shape of that link rather than bad luck. `e2e` IS IN THIS FEATURE’S VERIFICATION LIST AND WAS NOT RUN, for the same reason as F-018: gate 7 is pending and nothing declares a test:e2e task. F-091 carries it.

features.title: Palette Studio
acceptance: Build, edit, reorder and save palettes with anchor, neutral, light and accent roles
Palettes validate against the same schema as corpus palettes

attested.criterion: Build, edit, reorder and save palettes with anchor, neutral, light and accent roles
attested.verifiedBy: THE SAVE IS PROVEN AGAINST node:sqlite, NOT AGAINST THE DATABASE THAT SHIPS. packages/store/test/palette.test.ts writes a palette, REOPENS the database and reads it back with its members — real transactions, real foreign keys — and the shared conformance suite gained palette-durability and palette-atomicity so the device driver is judged by the same checks when F-041’s device attestation is run. What no CI run can reach: whether expo-sqlite commits the three-table write on a phone, whether SQLCipher encrypted it, and whether a save survives a force-quit. That is F-041’s standing attestation and this feature adds a table to it rather than a new kind of gap. The screen’s own save is proven against an in-memory port; the route wiring is proven by typecheck plus a source assertion, which is weak and is stated as weak.

features.notes: DONE. Palette Studio builds, edits, reorders and saves a palette to the encrypted database, and every saved palette is parsed by `parsePalette` — the same function content/palettes/*.json goes through — on the way in AND on the way back out. THAT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN: the two rules a palette EDITOR breaks are the two the schema already states (at least one anchor; ranks contiguous from 1), so a reorder bug fails at the boundary with a message that explains itself, instead of against a second copy of those rules in a screen. WHAT A DEVICE-BUILT PALETTE IS ENTITLED TO SAY ABOUT ITSELF is ADR-0067, not a decision made in passing: the corpus schema was written for provenanced editorial content and a palette built on a phone is not that, so every required field says what is actually the case — sourceId USER-LOCAL and authoredBy user-local (both RESERVED and enforced never to appear under content/), status draft so no reviewer can be recorded, versionId the corpus version it was built against, and name.en === name.ja because we do not translate user content. THE RESERVED-IDENTITY CHECK CARRIES ITS OWN DECOY, because both strings appear nowhere under content/ and a check over an empty set is indistinguishable from one that does nothing; it applies its rule to a planted record on every run, and was watched going red on a real palette before being trusted. WEIGHT IS DERIVED FROM RANK — 1.0, then a ladder from 0.9 to 0.6 — because FR-49 asks for roles and ordering and the schema requires a weight. That makes ORDER MEAN PROPORTION, which is the only reason a reorder control is worth having; it deliberately does NOT reproduce the seed palettes’ hand-authored weights, because a formula claiming to reproduce editorial judgement would be claiming something it cannot do. MIGRATION 2 adds the six columns F-041’s provisional tables could not carry, all NULLABLE WITH NO DEFAULT: a default would be a value nobody chose standing in for one somebody must, and NULL honestly means "written before this column existed" — refused by name, with the row planted through the driver because the write path cannot produce one. THE TESTS FOUND TWO REAL DEFECTS. Re-adding a removed member hit UNIQUE constraint failed, because the member lookup filtered to live rows and the derived member id collided with its own tombstone; re-adding is a RESURRECTION of that row, not a second one. And `no-role` demanded an accessibilityRole for TextInput that React Native has no name for — Role offers searchbox and no textbox, AccessibilityRole’s nearest is `text`, which means STATIC text. The checker’s model was what was wrong, so it now reads the host type, with a paired decoy proving a Pressable with no role is still reported AND that a TextInput with no NAME still is. A PRE-EXISTING RED GATE WAS FOUND AND FILED AS F-093: `pnpm test` printed 31/31 successful while --force was red in four tests. packages/store/test/key.test.ts scans apps/mobile/src for 64-hex literals and had been red since F-018 generated a bundle carrying 126 SHA-256 digests — turbo keys the task on its own package’s inputs, so a cached pass was replayed for two features. Fixed HERE, because it blocked this feature’s own verification: a 64-hex literal is an offender only if the corpus ledger does not record it, which keeps the check total instead of exempting a path, with a decoy proving a key literal is still caught. The three remaining failures are bitwise identity/golden tests failing by ULP on Node 22.16.0 against a repo pinning 24.19.0; reproduced at clean HEAD, in packages this feature does not touch, and carried by F-093. `e2e` IS IN THIS FEATURE’S VERIFICATION LIST AND WAS NOT RUN — the fourth feature to report it. Nothing declares a test:e2e task and F-091 carries it. E-017 fired a FOURTH time, for 11 codepoints; the subset was regenerated and gate 11 is green.

features.title: Colour Finder
acceptance: Search by English name, Japanese name, kanji, romaji, hex, or natural phrase
A hex query returns its nearest entries by DeltaE00
Natural phrases map deterministically to lightness/chroma/hue regions from a versioned lexicon in content/rules

attested.criterion: Search by English name, Japanese name, kanji, romaji, hex, or natural phrase
attested.verifiedBy: EVERY BRANCH IS ASSERTED OFF-DEVICE AND THE JAPANESE HALF IS NOT REVIEWED. The routing, the hex ranking, the phrase regions and the name forms are all asserted in finder.test.ts and over the rendered screen, in both themes. What no test here reaches: whether the Japanese TERMS mean what a Japanese speaker would expect — they are written by one editor and declared unreviewed in the lexicon’s own editorial notes (ADR-0060, OQ-5) — and whether typing them on a device produces the terms at all, which is an IME question no render-tree assertion can answer. The font coverage they need IS checked.

features.notes: DONE. One field routes three ways — hex, phrase, name — and the screen SAYS WHICH QUESTION IT ANSWERED, which is the feature rather than the polish: a single field that routes will sometimes route differently from what the person meant, and the difference between "these results are wrong" and "ah, it read that as a hex" is one sentence. THE HEX BRANCH IS NOT IMPLEMENTED HERE. `nameColor` from @irodora/color-naming (F-013) already returns candidates ranked by ΔE00 whose two-stage search is PROVABLY the ranking a full scan would give (E-015). Writing a second nearest-match would be a defect by definition. THE LEXICON IS VERSIONED RULE CONTENT with its own ledger (ADR-0069, ADR-0011): content/rules/phrase-lexicon.2026.08.1.json plus content/rules/index.json, two files because a record checked against a checksum it carries verifies itself. It is NOT in the corpus bundle — adding a key there would change every recorded digest and force a corpus mint for a change to vocabulary. F-029 is not built: no weights, no normalisation, no contexts, and E-009 is untouched. TWO RULES CAME FROM MEASURING THE CORPUS, NOT FROM TASTE. FIRST, every hue term carries a CHROMA FLOOR, enforced by the schema: charcoal spans hue 58°–268° and off-white 66°–246° because a colour with almost no chroma has no hue, so a hue-only term would answer "green" with greys. SECOND, "dark" is now defined twice — as a lexicon region and as an authored taxonomy band — so gate 11 asserts every authored band falls inside the region of the same name: 175 agreements over 28 terms, PRINTED, because a green check over zero entries reads identically to one over 175. THAT CHECK PAID BEFORE IT SHIPPED. The boundaries were first round numbers, chosen from a measurement printed to three decimals. 0.40 sits a MILLIONTH above the lowest entry filed as mid — do-ma at 0.3999990449505662 — so it would have been excluded from every query for a medium colour, silently and forever. Boundaries now sit in the measured GAP: 0.395, 0.725, 0.039, 0.100. TWO DECOYS CORRECTED THE DESIGN RATHER THAN CONFIRMING IT. (1) The first vocabulary made "dark muted green" — the phrase FR-47 ITSELF NAMES — resolve to a single point matching almost nothing, because "muted" had been given grey’s range; muted is low-to-MID chroma and must overlap the hue floor or no hue can ever be muted. (2) `beaded` IS a valid hex — six characters, every one a hex digit, and #BEADED is a real colour, as are decade and facade. No anchoring fixes that, so an unprefixed hex must contain a DIGIT and `#` is how a person says they meant the colour; the cost (ffffff searches names) is asserted so it is visible rather than discovered. MATCHING SCANS FOR TERMS RATHER THAN SPLITTING ON WHITESPACE, longest first — Japanese has no spaces, and a resolver that split on them would work in one language and not the other. A phrase needs EVERY part known; one unrecognised word sends the whole query to name search. E-017 FIRED A FIFTH TIME, and from a new direction: the lexicon’s Japanese terms are typed INTO the field and echoed there, so they render in the app’s own subset. Extending verify-font-coverage.mjs to read them immediately found two codepoints — 淡 and 鮮 — that nothing else in the repository required. A person typing 淡い would have seen a tofu box. `e2e` IS IN THIS FEATURE’S VERIFICATION LIST AND WAS NOT RUN — the fifth feature to report it. F-091 carries gate 7. AND `test` IS RED REPO-WIDE on this workstation for the Node 22 reason F-093 made visible and F-083 owns; every package this feature touches is green under a forced run.

features.title: Shareable colour cards
acceptance: A rendered card with name, kanji, hex, attribution and corpus version
Renders deterministically: the same entry at the same corpus version produces the same card on both platforms
Readable at thumbnail size

attested.criterion: Readable at thumbnail size
attested.verifiedBy: THE ARITHMETIC IS CHECKED; THE GLYPHS ARE NOT. Every type size scaled to a declared 96px thumbnail is compared against a floor, the sample block is asserted to occupy 62% of the card, and a decoy asserts the detail lines are BELOW the floor so the kanji claim means something rather than being one true statement among five vague ones. The screen shows the same document at that size beside the full one, so a person can disagree with the arithmetic. What no test reaches: whether a kanji at 9.6px is legible to a person on a real display — THUMBNAIL_MIN_PX is a DECLARED floor for CJK stroke separation, not a result from a legibility study, and must never be quoted as one.

features.notes: DONE. A colour as a card carrying kanji, kana, romaji, English name, hex, the entry’s own classification and the corpus version. THE CRITERION DECIDED THE DESIGN. "The same entry at the same corpus version renders the same card on both platforms" is unmeetable read as "the same pixels" — iOS and Android rasterise text differently and no application code changes that, so the criterion would have become an attested-forever item and then nothing. So the card is a DOCUMENT: cardSvg() is a pure function returning SVG text, byte-identical because nothing platform-shaped touches it, and CHECKABLE IN CI WITH NO DEVICE — asserted over every entry in both themes. The rasterisation is the platform’s and is not claimed. Same move archive.ts makes for FR-58’s "byte-identical database", and ADR-0070 records it for the same reason. TEXT DOES NOT SIT ON THE SAMPLE. Putting the hex over the colour needs a legible foreground chosen per entry against 120 backgrounds with no declared pairing — inventing the contrast decision the manifest exists to make. The sample is a block; the text sits on the card’s own ground where the pairing is declared and gate 9 already checks it. THE SAMPLE KEEPS SWATCH’S TWO-TONE KEYLINE, reusing swatch.hairline and its inverse rather than drawing a border: a near-white entry on a near-white card has no perceptible edge, and F-068 already measured that the worse of the two tones reaches 4.23 against the worst possible sample. Reusing the tokens inherits the proof; a border invented here would have inherited nothing. EVERY COLOUR IN THE DOCUMENT IS ACCOUNTED FOR — a token value or the entry’s own published hex, over all 120 entries in both themes, with a decoy proving a planted colour is reported. An SVG needs literal colours, which is what the colour-literal rule forbids in a component; the resolution is E-019’s, and E-027 records the part that is NEW: a stylesheet is rebuilt on every build and a card somebody sent last week is not. THE THUMBNAIL CLAIM IS NARROWED HONESTLY. At 96px no text on this card is comfortable. What survives is the COLOUR — the sample is 62% of the card — and the kanji, sized to clear the floor. A decoy asserts the hex and the attribution are BELOW it, because the alternative is five vague true statements instead of one sharp one. THE CONFORMANCE SUITE FOUND SOMETHING ON ITS FIRST RUN OVER THIS SCREEN: react-native-svg sets backgroundColor: transparent on its host view, and the colour-literal rule asked which token the ABSENCE of a colour is. `transparent` paints nothing, so it is now skipped — narrowly, one keyword, with a paired assertion proving a real hand-typed hex is still caught. It had gone unnoticed because Icon has set it on its triangle glyph since F-003 and the only registered subject rendering an Icon is Status with kind="bad", the CROSS glyph: that branch had never been rendered through the suite. CLASSIFICATION_KEYS IS NOW SHARED with the detail screen rather than copied. Two copies of the FR-23 vocabulary would drift, and the one that drifts would be the one on the artefact that leaves the app with none of its context. GETTING BYTES OUT IS FR-51 (R5) — no expo-sharing, no rasteriser, no device-only path — and the screen says so rather than leaving a person hunting for a share button. `e2e` IS IN THIS FEATURE’S VERIFICATION LIST AND WAS NOT RUN — the sixth feature to report it; F-091 carries gate 7. E-017 fired a sixth time, for 7 codepoints. `test` stays red repo-wide for the Node 22 reason F-093 made visible and F-083 owns; every package this feature touches is green under a forced run.

features.title: Claims copy lint
acceptance: Banned constructions fail lint across UI strings, marketing copy, documentation, code comments and identifiers
Permissible language is bound to Provenance.source
The allowlist is explicit, small, and each entry links to the measurement supporting it
A deliberately added banned phrase makes the gate fail
features.notes: DONE. DELIVERED: scripts/verify-claims.mjs inside gate 2, .harness/verification/claims.json holding the patterns as DATA, scripts/verify-claims-proof.mjs, and a clean fixture. Golden rule 11 is now a gate rather than a habit. THE PROBLEM THIS GATE HAS: the banned phrases must appear in this repository — ADR-0031 lists them, so do the governance doc, three skills and two rule files. A naive scan flags 18 files, most of them the policy. A blanket exemption for documents-discussing-the-policy would BE the gate, since every real claim in docs/ sits inside it. Answered with three exemption KINDS that are not interchangeable: policySource (an explicit file list, never a glob, 20 entries each with a reason), an inline claims-ok: marker scoped to ONE line and requiring a 12+ character reason, and `measured` requiring a link to a device-lab row. `measured` IS EMPTY and the count is printed every run — the device colour lab is F-063, and no number may exist without a row. FOUND ON ACTIVATION: the design system thesis was “soft chrome, exact colour”, a tagline asserting exactness in a product whose central commitment is that capture is an estimate. It meant the swatch carries no corner radius — rendering geometry, not accuracy — but a two-word thesis migrates into marketing faster than an identifier migrates into a field. Reworded to “unaltered colour”. Also corrected three “the true colour” comments in corpus/derive.ts to “specified”, which is more precise anyway. A FALSE POSITIVE I INTRODUCED AND FIXED BEFORE ACTIVATION: the actual-colour pattern had no determiner, so it fired on its own ADR-0052 (“covers actual colours” = real colours, ordinary English). Now requires the|its|their|your|a. PROVEN: 14 cases, each watched, baseline green either side — 12 red (one per construction plus a bare marker) and TWO green (a marker with a reason, and the clean fixture), with every red case also asserting the output NAMES the right construction. NOT DELIVERED, printed on every run: the provenance-conditional half of ADR-0031 §1. Deciding whether “measured” sits near an estimated value needs the render tree; it activates with F-017 and the table is already in claims.json.

features.title: Guided personal colour profile setup
acceptance: Swatch-comparison flow completes in 90 seconds median, with no camera
Produces lightness range, temperature tendency, chroma tolerance, contrast preference, neutrals, accents and avoid-list, each with its own confidence
The data model has no single skin-colour field, and a schema check rejects a migration adding one
Every dimension is editable, and a user correction is never overwritten by re-derivation

attested.criterion: Swatch-comparison flow completes in 90 seconds median, with no camera
attested.verifiedBy: THE CAMERA HALF IS GATED; THE 90 SECONDS IS NOT. "No camera" is checked over the source: no module under src/profile/ and no line of ProfileSetup.tsx matches vision-camera, expo-camera, ../lens/ or ImagePicker, with a decoy proving the scan can report one and a count proving it read the files it meant to. The DESIGN BUDGET is checked as arithmetic — 12 trials x 5 s + 20 s overhead = 80 s against FR-26 ceiling of 90 s, with a second assertion that the margin is finite so a per-trial budget of zero could not satisfy it. WHAT NO CHECK HERE REACHES: how long a real person takes. Nobody has been timed on this flow. TRIAL_BUDGET_SECONDS is a DECLARED design budget, never a measurement, and must not be quoted as one in copy or in a report (ADR-0031). Discharging this needs a moderated run with real participants across both locales, on a device, with the median reported alongside the spread — which is the first study this product has needed and is not a device-lab row.

features.notes: DONE. Twelve forced-choice swatch comparisons become seven dimensions, each with its own confidence and its own origin, editable, and stored. THE CRITERION DECIDED THE DESIGN, twice. "Each with its own confidence" covers all SEVEN dimensions including the three lists, which the data-model sketch did not — so the table carries seven confidence columns, and a list takes the MINIMUM of the dimensions it was derived from rather than a mean, because a mean launders a weak reading into a strong one and F-028 weights recommendations by this number. "A user correction is never overwritten by re-derivation" became origin_* as a COLUMN and one function, applyDerivation, that copies a fresh derivation only where the origin reads `derived` — a timestamp heuristic would have been usually right, which is not what ADR-0010 section 6 promised. CONFIDENCE IS AGREEMENT, CAPPED AT 0.75. Unanimous 0.75, split 0.5, unanswered 0, never 1 — and the same fact produces a WIDER range when the answers disagreed, so the range and the confidence agree because they have one source. ADR-0072 records it. THE TRIALS ARE DECLARED SLUGS AND THE CLAIM LIVES IN THE BUNDLE: each pair asserts it separates on its own axis and holds the others, and test/profile.test.ts checks that against the published OKLCh trial by trial, with a decoy asserting two off-whites FAIL the same bound. Filed as E-030 — a corpus publish that moved one entry would make a temperature question partly a lightness question, with every gate green and nothing different on screen. NFR-22 IS NOW A CHECK RATHER THAN A POLICY NOTE. prohibited.ts refuses a migration adding skin_*, complexion, ethnic*, rac(e|ial)*, attractive*/beauty*, body_* or bmi, AND refuses a database whose sqlite_master already carries one — the half no code review can substitute for. THE DECOY FOUND A REAL HOLE IN IT: the first pattern was \brac(e|es|ial)\b, which catches `race` and MISSES `racial_group`, because _ is a word character and there is no boundary before it. A rule that refuses the obvious name and accepts the one somebody would actually type reads as coverage. WHAT IS NOT PROVEN: gate 7 (e2e) could not run — it is pending and F-091 is blocked on the environment — so no assertion here covers a cold start, real navigation, or a real gesture. And nobody has been timed on the flow; that is the attested criterion above.

features.title: Photo-assisted profile setup
acceptance: Ranges derived on-device; the image is discarded and never transmitted
Every derived dimension presented as editable with its confidence
The profile is never finalised without explicit user confirmation
Bias validation across every ITA-degree band with a stated minimum sample per band

attested.criterion: Ranges derived on-device; the image is discarded and never transmitted
attested.verifiedBy: TWO OF THREE CLAUSES ARE GATED AND THE THIRD IS NOT. "Ranges derived" and "the image is discarded" are structural: the derivation takes a `LensReading`, which has NO field a frame, buffer, path or URI could be assigned to (F-040), asserted here with `ts-expect-error` so the test stops compiling if that ever becomes false — the image cannot be retained because it cannot be received. "NEVER TRANSMITTED" IS NOT PROVEN HERE. It is a claim about sockets during a real journey, it is F-039’s attested criterion and gate 7’s subject, and gate 7 is pending because F-091 is blocked on the environment. Discharging it needs the e2e offline suite asserting no socket opens during capture on a device — not a source scan, which is what would be tempting and would prove nothing about runtime.

attested.criterion: Bias validation across every ITA-degree band with a stated minimum sample per band
attested.verifiedBy: A HELD-OUT VALIDATION RUN OVER AN ITA-STRATIFIED SAMPLE OF REAL PEOPLE, with the minimum per band stated in advance and per-band accuracy published internally. NOT DISCHARGEABLE BY ANY CHECK IN THIS REPOSITORY — it needs participants, not a fixture, and "hard to test" is explicitly not the bar for attestation; "requires a system we do not control" is, and a cohort of people is one. THE SAME CRITERION IS F-037’s THIRD, AND F-037 IS `blockedBy: [F-027]` — so the study sits downstream of the feature that creates the need for it. That ordering is recorded rather than quietly resolved: it is legitimate (build the estimator, then validate it) but it means the validation debt must be visible from HERE, on the feature that ships the camera path, and not only from the feature that will eventually discharge it. WHAT PROTECTS THE PRODUCT MEANWHILE is not this attestation — it is `PHOTO_CEILING = 0.5`, which holds every photo-derived dimension at or below a split guided answer precisely because nobody has measured this path.

features.notes: DONE, with two of four criteria attested and both stated up front in the plan rather than discovered at the end — the same shape F-040 used, and for the same reason: the half that can be gated is gated and the half that needs a device or a cohort is named. WHAT A SINGLE READING CAN HONESTLY SUPPORT DECIDED THE SCOPE. Lightness from the reading’s own L, temperature from its hue, chroma from its own C — and CONTRAST ABSTAINS AT CONFIDENCE 0, because a contrast preference is the separation between two garments and one region has no second colour in it. The row reads "not asked yet", the same words a guided run uses for an unanswered trial, while every other row IS answered — which is what makes the abstention legible as a decision. A photo path that answered all seven would have invented exactly the dimension nobody would check. PHOTO_CEILING IS 0.5 AND THAT IS NOT A TUNING KNOB. It sits at or below CONFIDENCE_MAJORITY so an estimate from one reading never outranks a guided answer two of three people disagreed on, and the reason is NFR-23: nobody has measured this path across ITA° bands, so a higher number would be a claim with nothing behind it. ADR-0072 §5 records it and names the day it can move — the day F-037 publishes per-band accuracy. THE F-026 NO-CAMERA CHECK WAS RE-SCOPED, AND THE GUARANTEE IS STRONGER. `photo.ts` names `LensReading` on purpose, so the original directory-wide scan would have failed on the feature it was meant to coexist with, and the tempting repair — an exclusion — would have quietly changed what is guaranteed. What FR-26 protects is that the GUIDED FLOW does not depend on a camera, so the check now asserts that directly: no guided module matches a camera pattern AND none imports `./photo`; `photo.ts` reaches the lens by `import type` only, so nothing camera-shaped is in the runtime graph at all; and the roster is asserted against the directory so a new module is a failure rather than a file nothing scans. GATE 11 CAUGHT THE COMMENT THAT EXPLAINED IT. The Japanese note saying a particular kanji is absent from the bundled face contained that kanji, so the font-coverage gate reported 441 required and one missing — the same class as the app-imports gate reading a decoy comment as an import during F-026. Both gates read source text; a note ABOUT an artefact is an instance of it. WHAT IS NOT WIRED: nothing produces a `LensReading` in the app yet. F-040 shipped the seam and the four modes and attested every device criterion; there is no viewfinder. So the photo path is reachable only by passing a reading in, and that gap is filed as F-097 rather than narrated — a tested module nobody wired up passes every test it has.

features.title: Personal compatibility engine
acceptance: Score in [0,100] as a pure function of profile and colour, given the rule version
Explanation objects are data: factor, contribution, direction, and an i18n message key
Per-dimension confidence weights the contribution of uncertain dimensions
No prose is generated at scoring time
features.notes: DONE, and every criterion is gated — no attestation, which is rare here and worth saying: this feature renders nothing, ships no content and touches no device, so there is no half that needs a phone or a cohort. THE SCORE IS IN [0,100] BY CONSTRUCTION RATHER THAN BY CLAMPING. It is 100 x the weighted sum of fits in [0,1], so if the weights sum to 1 the range follows — which is why `parseRuleSet` REFUSES anything else instead of the engine clamping. A clamp would turn a defect in the weights into a plausible number at the boundary, which is the same failure shape as an accuracy claim with nothing behind it. The tolerance is 1e-9 because 0.4+0.3+0.2+0.1 is 0.9999999999999999 and a validator that rejected the most obvious weight set anybody would write is a validator somebody deletes. CRITERION 3 IS THE RENORMALISATION, AND THE DECOY IS WHAT PROVES IT. effective weight = weight x confidence, DIVIDED BY THEIR TOTAL. Without the division an uncertain profile simply scores every colour lower — which reads as "this suits you less" when the truth is "we know less about you", and those are different claims. The test halves every confidence and asserts THE SCORE DOES NOT MOVE, and separately that silencing a dimension the colour MISSES on raises the score while silencing one it MATCHES on lowers it. A single direction would also be produced by an implementation that just scaled everything down. NO PROSE, AND NO DEFAULT RULE SET. The engine emits `explain.<factor>.<direction>` keys and holds no catalogue, locale or formatter — a sentence produced at scoring time has to be translated at scoring time, and a stored recommendation becomes a stored English string. And there is deliberately NO `DEFAULT_RULES` export: a default would be a weight living in code, in the one place F-029 would have to find it, and E-009 would be false the day it was written. `scoreColor` requires a RuleSet; the tests build their own. FIFTY IS AN ANSWER, NOT A FALLBACK. With every confidence at zero there is nothing to renormalise, so the engine returns 50 with confidence 0 and all four contributions at zero — legibly "nothing to go on". Not equal weights, which would assert certainty the profile does not have. F-027 makes this reachable rather than theoretical: a photo estimate abstains on contrast at confidence 0. THE PROFILE ARRIVES STRUCTURALLY. `PersonalProfile` is a shape `NewPersonalProfile` satisfies, so the engine never imports `@irodora/store` — and because the two meet NOWHERE in the product yet, `test/profile.test.ts` is currently the only place a column removed in the store would fail. It is a devDependency import for exactly that reason. THE LOCKFILE GATE F-098 BUILT PAID FOR ITSELF WITHIN THE HOUR. Adding @irodora/color-spaces and @irodora/store to this package’s manifest failed gate 0 immediately, naming both packages and both sections, BEFORE any install — which is what it was built to do for somebody who cannot run pnpm at all. The matching three-line importer entries were written by hand and gate 0 confirmed the pair agrees. WHAT IS NOT PROVEN AND IS RECORDED AS E-032: `hueBias` here and `biasFromHue` in apps/mobile/src/profile/photo.ts are two implementations of one colour rule, carried with `guard: none` because the app cannot depend on this package until pnpm install can run. Two guards were considered and rejected as models that would report green while the algorithms drifted. F-099 deletes the duplicate. NOTHING CONSUMES THIS ENGINE YET — F-030 is what will, and it is blocked on F-029.

features.title: Rule and weight content system
acceptance: Weights and harmony rules are versioned, immutable content in content/rules
Every rule carries a rationale; a weight without one cannot be published
Weights sum to 1.0, validated at publish time
Changing a weight changes rankings with no deployment
Occasion contexts are deterministic weighting profiles
features.notes: DONE, and it CLOSES E-009 — the longest-standing owed check in the graph, carried with `guard: none` since 2026-08-13. Every criterion is gated; no attestation. THE WORD THAT MATTERED IN E-009 WAS "SILENTLY". A weight file that does not sum to 1 still parses as JSON, still carries five occasions, and still produces a number for every colour — one that cannot be compared with a number from any other context. Nothing downstream throws, so nothing downstream could ever have been the guard. THE GATE DOES NOT RE-IMPLEMENT THE RULE. `verify-content.mjs` loads the BUILT @irodora/recommendation and calls `parseWeightContent`, which wraps F-028’s own `parseRuleSet` — so "these weights normalise" is decided by the code that SCORES with them rather than by a copy in a script that would agree on the day it was written (E-013). A `loadRecommendationPackage` sits beside `loadCorpusPackage` for exactly that reason, and criterion 3 was therefore already half-built before this feature started. WATCHED FAILING IN BOTH HALVES, ON THE REAL PUBLISHED FILE. A weight moved from 0.35 to 0.9 reports "occasions.default: weights sum to 1.5499999999999998, not 1". A SINGLE WORD changed in a rationale — a file that still parses perfectly, and which the sum check cannot see — reports a digest that does not match the ledger. The second is the immutability half of ADR-0011 and it needed its own mutation, because the first throw short-circuits the rest of the block. Restored byte-exactly afterwards, proven by the digest passing again rather than by reading a diff. AN OCCASION IS A WEIGHT SET, which is why FR-34 cost almost nothing. `scoreColor` already took a RuleSet, so choosing a context is choosing which one to pass. The alternative — an occasion as a modifier applied AFTER scoring — would have put a second set of numbers between the weights and the answer, and the weights would have stopped being the thing that decides. CRITERION 4 IS THE ONE A TEST CAN MOST EASILY FAKE. "Changing a weight changes rankings" is satisfied by asserting two numbers differ, which would pass on an engine that read no weights and returned noise. It is asserted as a REORDERING of the same colours through an engine that is byte-identical between the two calls, plus a check that the same occasion always produces the same order — and a third that connects the numbers to the PROSE: the japanese-inspired rationale claims restraint is a chroma property, so a colour outside the chroma tolerance must score worse there than under casual and better under formal, which carries the lowest chroma weight. Without that a rationale could say anything at all. THE FIRST DRAFT OF THAT TEST WAS WRONG AND THE FAILURE WAS INSTRUCTIVE: it asserted rank POSITION, and the vivid colour sits third under both occasions because the colours above it move too. Rank is a comparison against whichever candidates happen to be in the list; the SCORE is what the weight acts on and what the rationale is a claim about. A SECOND FAILURE IMPROVED THE PARSER. The per-factor count reported only the first mismatch, so retyping `contrast` as `chroma` said "chroma appears 2" and never mentioned the factor that had gone missing — my test asserted the other half. The realistic edit produces both at once, so the message now names every mismatch. ADR-0011 GOT A NOTE RATHER THAN A REWRITE. It was written on 2026-08-13 when there was a server tier; ADR-0051 removed it. "A weight change requires no deployment" and "publication only through the admin application" do not survive — in a local-first app new content ships in a new build, the pull request IS the publish path, and the two-file diff is the audit log. FR-67’s own wording is the one that holds and the one the gate checks: without a CODE change. Sections 1, 4 and 6 survive unchanged and are now enforced. THE WEIGHTS ARE EDITORIAL AND NOBODY EDITORIAL SET THEM — Irodora’s own first draft, self-reviewed like every other record here (ADR-0060, OQ-5). The provenance block says so in its own words, and the derivation states plainly that NO WEIGHT IS SUPPORTED BY A STUDY. The editorial notes name the weight a second editor would most likely argue with first.

features.title: Outfit colour engine
acceptance: Given a garment colour and slot, returns 5 or more ranked trouser and 4 or more ranked shoe candidates
At least three alternatives per recommendation, each labelled with the dimension it moves along
Candidate generation is bounded before scoring
Recommendation p95 within NFR-4

attested.criterion: Recommendation p95 within NFR-4
attested.verifiedBy: A MEASURED RUN ON THE SLOWEST DEVICE IN THE SUPPORT MATRIX, which is what NFR-4 asks for in those words. GATE 12 IS THE PLACE IT BELONGS AND IT CANNOT RUN HERE: `perf` is `pending` and `activatesWith: F-038` — and F-038 is blockedBy F-030, so the gate that would check this arrives after the feature that produces it. WHAT WAS MEASURED, and what it is not: `recommendOutfit` over the 120-entry published corpus, 200 runs, Node 22.16.0 on a desktop — median 0.35 ms, p95 0.87 ms. That is roughly two hundred times under the 200 ms budget, which is a useful design signal and is NOT the NFR-4 claim: it is the fastest hardware available rather than the slowest supported, the corpus is already in memory, and Hermes is not V8. The number is PRINTED by the test rather than asserted, deliberately — gate 12’s own description says a latency assertion on a shared runner flakes until somebody disables it, and a threshold that passes trivially reads like coverage. WHAT IS ASSERTED ABOUT COST instead is the bound: `scored` never exceeds SHORTLIST_LIMIT however large the pool, which is a number the engine reports rather than a duration the machine decides.

features.notes: DONE. "What goes with this" returns ranked colours for the other slots, each with its score and the four contributions behind it, plus alternatives labelled with the dimension they move along. Three of four criteria gated; the latency one is attested and says exactly why. A RANK IS TWO QUESTIONS, NOT ONE. `scoreColor` answers "does this suit me" and says nothing about the garment in hand — built on it alone this would have returned the same five colours whatever you were holding, which is a personal-colour list wearing a different name. So the rank is the mean of personal fit and PAIRING fit, and there is a test that earns that half: two very different garments must produce different orders for the same person and pool. THE 50/50 BLEND IS THE ONE NUMBER HERE THAT IS NOT CONTENT, and it is said out loud in the module header, the plan and this note. FR-32’s six-factor model is F-031; inventing a weight the week after F-029 finished proving weights belong in content/rules would have been exactly the wrong lesson to draw. Equal weight asserts no preference, which is the honest position while there is no basis for one. Everything else — falloff, poles, CONTRAST_TARGET — comes from the published rule set, so no axis is defined twice. THE BOUND IS REPORTED, NOT JUST APPLIED. `considered` and `scored` are on the result, so the test asserts a pool of 10 000 was scored at most 64 times — a bound that HELD — rather than asserting that a constant exists. The baseline half is there too: a pool of ten is scored entirely, so "scored <= 64" is distinguishable from "scored nothing". AN AXIS WITH NO CANDIDATE IS OMITTED, NEVER FILLED. FR-38 asks for at least three labelled alternatives; four where one is mislabelled is not an answer. A pool of two near-identical off-whites is asserted to produce FEWER alternatives rather than duplicates. MY OWN TEST WAS WRONG AND THE ENGINE WAS RIGHT, and it is worth keeping. The first draft asserted that somebody who wants high contrast prefers the FURTHEST colour available. It failed: against a near-black top, an off-white overshoots the high target (0.776 separation against 0.50) by more than a mid grey undershoots it (0.314). A contrast preference is a TARGET, not a floor — somebody who asked for strong contrast did not ask for the maximum. That property is now asserted explicitly, and E-033 records the table that two different questions read. THE CACHE-SCOPE GATE CAUGHT SOMETHING SUBTLE: a shared `CONTENT` constant reduced what the static scan could see to the directory name, which turbo.json does not declare. Spelling each path out in full is what lets the check match `content/versions` against globalDependencies — a readability habit that happens to be load-bearing. STILL OWED: ADR-0011 section 2, `envelope.rules` as an indexed column on a stored recommendation. Nothing stores one yet; this engine returns the rule version on every result so the storing feature has it to record.

features.title: Outfit scoring and explainability
acceptance: Colour harmony, personal fit, contrast, Japanese aesthetic, versatility and CVD accessibility scored separately, plus an overall
All component scores are shown; the overall never replaces them
Every score returns its factor decomposition with direction and magnitude
features.notes: DONE. Six component scores and an overall, each with its direction, its message key and numeric evidence. All three criteria gated; `e2e` is in the verification list and could not run — gate 7 is pending and F-091 is blocked on the environment — so nothing here proves a person ever SEES six numbers. "JAPANESE AESTHETIC" IS CALLED `corpusAffinity`, AND THE RENAME IS THE FEATURE. FR-32 names the component and it has to exist; a number claiming how JAPANESE an outfit is would be an unmeasurable cultural claim shipped out of 100, which is a larger version of exactly what the claims lint bans phrases for. What is measurable is dE00 to the nearest published corpus entry — a real distance, a real unit, reproducible from the corpus version. ADR-0073 records it INCLUDING the cost: the component measures OUR corpus, not the tradition, and our corpus is 120 entries chosen by one editor. THE OUTFIT WEIGHTS ARE CONTENT, AND THAT MEANT PUBLISHING A VERSION. Six numbers summing to 1 is precisely the shape F-029 made content, so folding them in as constants would have repeated what F-030 explicitly refused. `weights.2026.08.2.json` supersedes 2026.08.1, changes NOTHING that was in it, and adds an `outfit` block with a rationale per component. THE PARSER MADE THE BLOCK OPTIONAL RATHER THAN REQUIRED, and that is not a soft default: 2026.08.1 is published and immutable, so a required field would have turned gate 11 red on a file nobody is allowed to edit. `null` means "this version predates the feature", and `outfitWeights` THROWS naming the version rather than substituting numbers nobody published. GATE 11 NOW DISCOVERS EVERY WEIGHT FILE instead of naming one. F-029 hard-coded 2026.08.1 — correct while there was one, and stale within the day. An old version still has to pass: it is immutable, the app may pin it, and a file nobody checks is a file nobody would notice going wrong. 46 rationales over 2 versions, 10 fixtures. E-005 STOPPED BEING A PREDICTION. It was written naming "the recommendation engine’s separation factor" before one existed; `cvdAccessibility` now imports `separationScore` and defines no separation of its own. It takes the WORST pair across all three deficiencies, not the mean — an outfit where one pair vanishes for a deutan is not rescued by two that survive. TWO OF MY TESTS FAILED AND BOTH FOUND REAL DEFECTS, one of them serious. (1) The CVD test assumed a red and a green would collapse under deutan; both scored 100, because they differ in LIGHTNESS and separationScore weights that. Asking the model which corpus pair it actually finds hardest returned kawaki-suna/usu-shiba at 0.68 of 100 — measured rather than assumed. (2) THE BIG ONE: `versatility` ranked mi-aka, the most saturated red in the corpus, as the MOST versatile colour — 73.3% against 61.7% for a warm grey. Two stacked defects. The component was built on `pairingFit`, whose separation term dominated, so it was measuring lightness centrality AND scoring the same property `contrast` already scored. Removing separation made the gap WIDER in the wrong direction, which exposed the second: `hueBias` calls `hai-suna`, a grey at C=0.012, 0.867 WARM — more strongly warm than that vivid red at 0.644. A hue angle on a near-neutral is a rounding artefact. `temperatureOf` scales the bias by chroma against the published lexicon’s own 0.039 boundary for "grey". E-034 records it, and records that `scoreColor` and the app’s copy still carry the same blind spot — fixed where it was demonstrated, filed as F-101 where it was not. A TEST WRITTEN AGAINST WHAT THE CODE COMPUTES WOULD HAVE PASSED. The only reason any of this surfaced is that the assertions were written against what the WORDS mean.

features.title: CVD outfit mode
acceptance: Flags reduced separation and proposes an alternative with the measured improvement
The improvement is reproducible from the stored envelope
Reads as an observation about the outfit, not as a diagnosis of the user
Permanently available in the free tier

attested.criterion: The improvement is reproducible from the stored envelope
attested.verifiedBy: THE REPRODUCIBILITY IS GATED; THE STORING IS NOT, BECAUSE NOTHING STORES ONE. `reproduceImprovement` recomputes the identical number from the envelope and the three colours, and REFUSES when the envelope records a severity this build does not check — both asserted. What does not exist is a `recommendation` row to store the envelope IN: the table is in data-model.md and unbuilt, and ADR-0011 section 2 (`envelope.rules` as an indexed column) is owed by whatever first persists a recommendation. Discharging this needs that feature plus a test that reads a finding back OUT of the database and reproduces its number — a round trip, not a recomputation in memory.

features.notes: DONE, with one criterion attested, one recorded as NOT APPLICABLE, and a surface deviation stated rather than quietly taken. SCORING, NOT RENDERING. There is no simulation preview anywhere in this feature, and a test asserts the module calls neither `simulateAnomalous` nor `simulateDichromacy` — not because simulation is wrong (`separationScore` does it internally) but because a colour simulated FOR DISPLAY is the industry-default filter that shows a person what their palette looks like TO SOMEONE ELSE. [[cvd-is-scoring-not-rendering]] is explicit that this helps designers and does close to nothing for the person it names. What is drawn is a sentence about a pair, a number, and a swap. E-005 GAINED THE CONSUMER IT NAMED, and it is the one where a second definition would have done the most damage: this flag proposes a swap with a MEASURED improvement, a number a person is invited to act on. If the Studio flagged by one definition and the engine ranked by another, the product would say a swap gained 99 points and then rank the result as though it had not. THE SURFACE IS PALETTE STUDIO, NOT AN OUTFIT, AND THAT IS A DEVIATION. FR-35 says "outfit mode"; there is no outfit surface — the builder is F-033 and it is R4. Building against nothing would have been [[a-tested-module-nobody-wired-up-passes-every-test-it-has]] for the third time this release. A palette is a set of colours somebody assembled by hand, which is exactly this check’s input, and the computation is identical when an outfit surface arrives. IT WORKS END TO END ON REAL DATA: kawaki-suna and usu-shiba separate at 1 of 100 — the hardest pair in the corpus, found by ASKING the model rather than reasoning about hue, which is the mistake F-031 made — and the Studio proposes Autumn Field at 100, a gain of +99. CRITERION 3 IS COPY, AND IT IS CHECKED. Every string is an observation about the colours: "These two are hard to tell apart", never "you may not be able to distinguish these". The product knows nothing about the reader’s vision and must not imply it does — NFR-22’s discipline arriving from a different direction, where the failure is not a stored field but a sentence that diagnoses somebody. A decoy proves the check fires on English AND Japanese second-person vision language, and a positive assertion proves the copy says the right thing rather than merely avoiding the wrong one. CRITERION 4 IS NOT APPLICABLE AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH RATHER THAN TICKED. "Permanently available in the free tier" describes a world ADR-0051 removed: no server, no account, no billing provider, and the PRD says there is no team tier with OQ-2 void. THERE ARE NO TIERS, so there is nothing to gate this behind and nothing to check — the same treatment ADR-0011’s "no deployment" got in F-029. Ticking it would have been claiming a check that could not exist. NOT RUN: `e2e` is in this feature’s verification list and gate 7 is pending with F-091 blocked on the environment, so nothing proves the flag is reachable by a real gesture.

features.title: Backup, export and import — the durability story
acceptance: An export contains every record, tombstones included, and re-imports to an identical canonical digest of every row of every table
Erasure is immediate and local: every table hard-deleted, change_log included, and the key destroyed so bytes already on disk stay unreadable
A re-query against each store returns nothing; the return value of the erase call is not the proof
The app offers an export before any destructive action, and erases nothing if a requested export fails
The export and import journeys complete on a device, writing to and reading from a file the person chose

attested.criterion: The export and import journeys complete on a device, writing to and reading from a file the person chose
attested.verifiedBy: A device run of the export and import flows against a real file, on iOS and Android. The MECHANISM is gated here — the round trip, every refusal, and the ordering are all tested in Node against the node:sqlite driver — but file access is behind the ArchiveSink interface precisely so the package needs no platform to be tested, which means the platform binding itself is what a device confirms. FR-58 says "asserted in e2e"; pnpm test:e2e exits 1 by design while no surface declares the script, and gate 7 activates with F-018/F-040.

features.notes: DONE. With no server this is the entire durability story (ADR-0051 section 5), which is why it is a first-release feature and not a follow-up. 27 tests in @irodora/store. "BYTE-IDENTICAL" IS INTERPRETED, IN THE OPEN. Taken literally FR-58 is unmeetable: a SQLite FILE differs in page layout, freelist state and AUTOINCREMENT sequence after an identical sequence of writes, so no import could ever satisfy it and the criterion would eventually be softened quietly instead of deliberately. The claim worth making is that the DATA round-trips, so digest() is a canonical serialisation — every table in a declared order, every row INCLUDING TOMBSTONES, every column sorted — and that is compared byte for byte, against the ORIGINAL database rather than against the archive it came from. Comparing an export to an export is an echo that passes on an exporter dropping the same column twice. THE ARCHIVE IS JSON, NOT A FILE COPY: a copy of an encrypted database is useless without the key, and shipping the key with the backup makes the encryption theatre. The stated cost is that the archive is plaintext — readable by the user, which is the point, and by anyone who obtains it, which is the price. Recorded as a decision rather than discovered later. THE LINT FOUND A DESIGN FLAW: importArchive typed its parameter as Archive, and no-unnecessary-condition flagged the format check as always-false — which is exactly the type asserting a fact about data nobody had checked. An archive arrives from a FILE the user chose. It now takes `unknown` and validates every field, and distinguishes a MISSING table (an older archive, accepted as empty) from one present but not an array (corruption, refused) — treating them alike would import garbage as emptiness. TWO REFUSALS THAT SEPARATE A RESTORE FROM A DISASTER: a NEWER schemaVersion is refused rather than guessed at, the same rule migrate() applies; and a non-empty database is refused rather than merged, because a silent merge duplicates everything a user owns and looks like it worked. ERASURE IS PROVEN BY RE-QUERY, and eraseEverything RETURNS VOID so the test FR-58 warns against cannot be written. Its decoy is the one that matters: a "wipe" that only tombstoned would leave every row on disk while every list came back empty — soft delete exists so a sync can tell "deleted" from "never existed", and erasure exists so nothing remains to tell anything about. Destroying the key is what makes it true of bytes already written; a file delete leaves recoverable blocks and a row-by-row delete leaves them too. THE ORDER IS THE WHOLE FEATURE. eraseWithBackupPrompt enforces offer -> write -> confirm -> erase in code, so a caller cannot get it wrong by writing the calls in the order that reads more naturally, and the test asserts the ORDER rather than the outcome — a test checking only "a backup exists and the data is gone" passes on an implementation that erased first and backed up an empty database. AND THE CASE THAT MATTERS MOST: if a requested export FAILS, nothing is erased. Losing the data and the backup in one action is the worst outcome available here, and it is exactly what a try/catch that carries on produces.

features.title: Ethical guardrails and bias validation
acceptance: A schema check rejects any migration adding a skin-colour, ethnicity, age or health field
No code path infers a protected characteristic
Held-out validation set stratified by ITA-degree band, every band above its minimum sample
Per-band accuracy published internally; a band that underperforms blocks release of the profile feature
features.notes: DONE. Two guarantees of different kinds, and the feature treats them differently on purpose. NFR-22 IS STRUCTURAL AND WAS BUILDABLE, so it was built. The prohibition gained AGE and HEALTH — F-026 had covered skin, complexion, ethnicity, race, attractiveness and body — and more importantly it LEFT SQL. `packages/store/src/prohibited.ts` refuses a column; it cannot see a function called `inferEthnicity` that never touches the database, and "no code path infers a protected characteristic" is a claim about CODE. `scripts/verify-no-inference.mjs` scans 308 shipped source files, reusing the store’s own vocabulary from the BUILT package rather than keeping a second list (E-013). THE PROOF FOUND TWO REAL HOLES IN MY FIRST VERSION, and they are the same hole: the patterns were written for snake_case SQL and TypeScript is camelCase. `\bethnic\w*\b` does not match inside `inferEthnicity` — the word is not at a boundary — and `\bages?\b` does not match `ageBand`, because the `\b` after "age" fails against a capital B. BOTH SLIPPED THROUGH SILENTLY. The fix is not a looser regex, which would flag `average`, `percentage`, `storage`, `language` and `usage`: it is TOKENISATION. Identifiers are split into words — `inferEthnicity` into infer+ethnicity, `ageBand` into age+band — and stems are matched by prefix per token, which is safe precisely because `percentage` is ONE word that does not begin with "age". One vocabulary, two representations: `pattern` for SQL and `stems` for source, each suited to its input, in one list. THE SCAN THEN FOUND FOUR FALSE POSITIVES IN THE REPOSITORY, and every one changed the rule rather than the exemption list. `diagnos\w*` caught `verify-guards.mjs`’s `diagnose()` helper and a test constant — the ORDINARY engineering sense — so the family now matches the noun `diagnosis`/`diagnoses`, which is what a FIELD is called. `body` caught `verify-state.mjs`’s markdown `body` and `bodyIndent`, so the source stems are multi-word: `body shape`, `body type`, `body fat`, `body mass`. A check that fires on honest code is one somebody switches off, and the real protection goes with it. THE EXEMPTION LIST IS FOUR FILES, each made of the vocabulary by necessity, and the proof is what stops it growing: a violation planted in a NON-exempt file must be caught while the exempt files stay green, so silencing a real finding by widening the exemption fails the proof. Five cases — three red, TWO GREEN. The green ones are the load-bearing half: a doc comment discussing skin colour and ethnicity (this repository is full of them) and identifiers containing "age" and "race". IT RUNS IN GATE 15, NOT GATE 2, FOR A MECHANICAL REASON WORTH RECORDING: the scan reads the vocabulary from the BUILT store, and CI runs lint (gate 2) BEFORE build (gate 6). Putting it in `pnpm lint` would have passed locally — where dist exists — and failed on the first push, which is the F-098 shape exactly. It belongs beside the key-material scan anyway: both are about what the product must never do with personal data. NFR-23 CANNOT BE DONE HERE AT ALL, and both its criteria are attested, blocking release. What this feature could do is make the absence a CONDITION rather than a note: a test asserts PHOTO_CEILING stays at or below CONFIDENCE_MAJORITY while the study is outstanding, so raising it produces a failing test asking what changed. That is the only guard NFR-23 can have before participants exist, and the attestation now names the shape of the study so whoever runs it has something to run. THIS FEATURE CANNOT MAKE THE PRODUCT SAFE. It makes one class of failure structurally impossible and leaves the other clearly outstanding, which is the honest division.

attested.criterion: Held-out validation set stratified by ITA-degree band, every band above its minimum sample
attested.verifiedBy: A HELD-OUT SET OF PHOTOGRAPHS OF REAL PEOPLE, stratified by ITA° band, with the minimum per band stated in advance. NOT DISCHARGEABLE BY ANY CHECK IN THIS REPOSITORY — it needs participants and consent, not a fixture, and "requires a system we do not control" is the bar for attestation rather than "hard to test". THE SHAPE IT WOULD TAKE, so the attestation is actionable rather than a shrug: ITA° computed from a calibrated reference capture per participant; bands at the conventional boundaries; a minimum per band chosen BEFORE collection so it cannot be fitted to what arrived; the guided profile and the photo estimate both run per participant; agreement measured against the participant’s own corrected profile, which is the only ground truth this product has. WHAT PROTECTS THE PRODUCT MEANWHILE is not this attestation — it is PHOTO_CEILING = 0.5, and F-037 turned that from a constant into a CONDITION: a test now asserts it stays at or below CONFIDENCE_MAJORITY while this criterion is outstanding, so raising it produces a failing test asking what changed rather than a green run.

attested.criterion: Per-band accuracy published internally; a band that underperforms blocks release of the profile feature
attested.verifiedBy: A held-out validation run over an ITA-stratified sample, published internally. A release blocker on an ethical guarantee (NFR-23). Depends on the criterion above: there is nothing to publish until there is a set to measure over.

features.title: Performance budgets and gates
acceptance: Absolute committed thresholds, never baseline deltas
Backend bench boots the real runtime over a versioned deterministic corpus
Frontend measured over the wire, gzipped, at the load event, under prefers-reduced-motion with CPU throttling, median of 3
Each gate self-tests its own arithmetic every run
Gate perf activates
features.notes: DONE, WITH ONE CRITERION RECORDED NOT APPLICABLE AND THE REASON. WHAT SHIPPED: tests/bench/budgets.json holds seven ABSOLUTE ceilings, each with a rationale and a `scope`; tests/bench/src/bench.mjs measures the three that are measurable here and PRINTS the four that are not; tests/bench/src/bench-proof.mjs plants ten cases against it. Gate 12 is active and unconditional in CI. CRITERION 1 (absolute, never deltas) — met: every ceiling is a committed number, and the bench reads no previous run at all, so a delta is not merely discouraged but unimplementable. CRITERION 2 ("Backend bench boots the real runtime over a versioned deterministic corpus") — met in substance; the word "backend" is retired-world and there is no backend. The bench imports the BUILT @irodora/recommendation and @irodora/color-core rather than sources or mocks, and runs over published corpus 2026.08.1 (120 entries) and weights 2026.08.2 — the files that ship, pinned by version, so a measurement is reproducible. CRITERION 3 (frontend over the wire, gzipped, at the load event, CPU-throttled, median of 3) — NOT APPLICABLE, and recorded rather than ticked. That is NFR-5, withdrawn by ADR-0051; the PRD's own withdrawal table says "There is no web surface". Nothing is served over a wire and there is no load event. Same treatment as F-032 gave the free tier and F-029 gave "no deployment". CRITERION 4 (each gate self-tests its arithmetic every run) — met, and it is the interesting one. A p95 computed wrongly produces a plausible number and a green gate for ever, with no downstream symptom ever. The percentile is checked against known arrays with known answers AND against the question those cannot ask — is p95 different from p5. The proof plants a percentile hardcoded to satisfy the known answers and constant otherwise; only the second half catches it. Zero self-tests is a refusal, not a pass. CRITERION 5 (gate perf activates) — met, and the ACTIVATION WAS THE HAZARD. The CI step carried `if: github.event_name == 'push' && hashFiles('tests/bench/package.json') != ''`, and that file has existed since F-001 — so the guard’s surviving effect was to skip the gate on every pull request. Gate 0 was WATCHED FAILING with the status flipped and the guard still in place ("Active gate \"perf\" has a CI step guarded by `if: ...`"), then the line came off in the same change. No step in ci.yml carries an `if:` any more, and the file now says why. TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY MEASURING RATHER THAN ASSUMING. (1) The first draft budgeted score-outfit at 40 ms "because corpusAffinity is the most expensive thing the engine does". It is not: scoreOutfit p95 is 0.45–0.67 ms against recommendOutfit at 0.76–1.06 ms, because two slots of shortlist-plus-score outweigh one corpus-wide dE00 sweep. The rationale was wrong in the direction that flatters the code, and it was rewritten from the numbers. (2) A per-call ceiling on scoreColor reported p95 0.00 ms — the work is cheaper than performance.now() can resolve, so the budget could not be exceeded by any regression. That is a check that passes because it does nothing, in the one form that looks like good news. Fixed by measuring 1000-call batches, and the bench now REFUSES any node-reference p95 of exactly zero so the next one cannot be added quietly. WHAT THIS GATE DOES NOT PROVE, printed on every run: NFR-4 is measured on the slowest device in the support matrix. A CI runner is neither slowest nor a device. All four device budgets are NOT RUN and stay attested on F-030, F-040 and R4. The node-reference ceilings are CHOSEN at roughly twenty times the observation, not derived from the device numbers — nobody has measured the ratio between this workstation and a four-year-old Android, and inventing one would turn a desktop number into a claim about a phone. E-035 records the link. GATES RUN ON THIS WORKSTATION: state (green), perf (green, 3 measured / 4 NOT RUN), the gate 12 proof (10 cases, 9 red 1 green), the gate-CI mirror proof (14 active gates, both halves), eslint and prettier over tests/bench, and tsc --noEmit for the package. NOT RUN HERE and said plainly: any gate needing pnpm, because Node 22.16.0 / pnpm 9.3.0 cannot satisfy engines >=24.19.0 / >=11.
