features.notes: DONE. The first feature that produces something a person could hold — apps/mobile is a real Expo app: SDK 57.0.14, React Native 0.86.2, React 19.2.3, Expo Router, development client rather than Expo Go because VisionCamera is a native module and F-040 needs frame processors. Versions verified with expo install --check rather than guessed; it flagged one (react-native-screens 4.20 -> ~4.26) and now reports Dependencies are up to date. THE ENGINE IS WIRED AND EXECUTING, not merely listed: apps/mobile/src/engine.ts is the single import site, the screen computes every hex and the dE00 figure at render time, and nothing on it is a typed colour value. A dependency nobody imports passes every gate and ships nothing, which this repository has already lost six increments to. FOUND WHILE WIRING IT: @irodora/design-tokens GENERATED a React Native target and never re-exported it — nativeColors was unreachable from outside the package. Byte-compared by its own test the whole time, and importable by nobody. F-039 is its first consumer, which is why it surfaced now. A DECOY THAT MATTERS: dE00 is defined on CIELAB, and OKLCh triples are the SAME TYPE, so handing them straight to deltaE00 typechecks and returns a plausible meaningless number. The first draft of engine.ts did exactly that. The test now pins the Lab route AND asserts the wrong route differs by more than 1 dE00, so the assertion discriminates. NFR-12 AS A BUILD-TIME FACT: app.config.ts requests no network permission on either platform and BLOCKS android.permission.INTERNET, because a library that declares it would otherwise have it merged in silently. Adding it back would falsify a requirement and needs an ADR. There is no newArchEnabled flag and its absence is correct — the New Architecture has been mandatory with no opt-out since SDK 55, so the field is not part of ExpoConfig. A LINT SUPPRESSION I KEPT RATHER THAN OBEYED: no-unnecessary-condition flags the ?? guard on useColorScheme(). react-native types it as null | undefined | ColorSchemeName and tsc agrees the guard is needed — assigning null to its ReturnType compiles. The rule resolves the module differently. The guard stays, with the evidence in the comment: deleting a guard because a linter overruled a measurement is the wrong way round. THREE OF SIX CRITERIA ARE ATTESTED, and the plan says so in its own section rather than leaving a reader to work out which half is checked. The Hermes execution, the airplane-mode journey and the no-socket assertion all need a device — and the last two also need journeys, which arrive with F-018/F-040. Gates e2e and a11y stay PENDING for exactly that reason: their subject is a journey and this feature ships a floor. F-080 replaced the EAS assumption with a GitHub Actions lane (ADR-0058) and reworded the build acceptance criterion accordingly — recorded here because ADR-0038 forbids quietly rewording an attested criterion, and this one WAS reworded.

features.title: Colour Lens: live pick, garment scan, precision pick
acceptance: Capture colour space is read, never assumed; an unrecognised space is unknown and caps the confidence rather than falling back to sRGB
Only a bounded numeric sample crosses the bridge; the frame is disposed on the worklet thread and never written to a file
All four capture modes, each calling the engine and computing no colour of its own, enforced by a lint rather than by review
VisionCamera frame processors run on a worklet thread and the UI thread never blocks on colour maths
yuv pixel format with conversion in the processor; every frame explicitly disposed and the pipeline does not stall
Live pick sustains at least 15 updates per second on the reference device set
No socket opens during a scan
features.notes: SCOPE CORRECTED WHILE SELECTING IT AFTER F-035. F-040 conflated two features with different verification stories: the SAMPLING MATHS (robust statistics, rejection rules, illumination and quality classification, the confidence rules) and the CAMERA PLUMBING. The maths is fully gateable and belongs in the engine — apps/mobile/AGENTS.md: "The engine is imported, never ported. Sampling logic, rejection rules and averaging live there" — and E-008 records that a mobile-only re-implementation makes the same fabric measure differently on two surfaces, which NO single-platform test can see. Building the camera half first would have forced the maths into the app or stubbed it. Split to F-077, which this now depends on. ALSO CORRECTED: docs/PRD.md scheduled FR-13, FR-14 and FR-15 as "R1 web · R3 mobile" — a retired surface AND a release that disagreed with this feature being R2 and must. The feature list is the scope authority (AGENTS.md section 1), so the PRD columns were the stale half. F-074 could not catch this: it matches vocabulary, and a release column is neither a banned word nor a gate id. DONE, with four of seven criteria attested — a property of the feature, not a shortcoming of the work, and stated up front in the plan rather than discovered at the end. THE GATED CORE IS THE PART THAT COULD OTHERWISE ROT: only numbers cross the bridge, enforced by the TYPE (LensReading has no field a frame, buffer, path or URI could be assigned to, asserted with ts-expect-error so it fails on the unused directive if that stops being true); the colour space is read and an unrecognised value is unknown rather than sRGB; all four modes call the engine, proven by recomputing the value independently through @irodora/color-sampling and requiring an exact match. TWO LINTS DO WHAT NO TEST HERE COULD. Colour maths may not drift into the app — E-008 records that a mobile-only re-implementation makes the same fabric measure differently on two surfaces, both pass their own tests, and nothing runs both. And a frame may not reach disk: a debug write during development is how "nothing is stored" stops being true, and it survives review as a one-line change. Both planted and watched firing; 17 boundaries. THE OPEN QUESTION IS RECORDED AT THE SEAM rather than left to whoever first has a phone: can the engine run inside a worklet? Sampling in the worklet and aggregating on the JS thread is what ships; compiling the engine for the worklet runtime is strictly better if it works. Both share this seam. Reimplementing the arithmetic there is forbidden and lint-enforced. A FIXTURE LESSON WORTH KEEPING: three separate tests in this feature initially failed because the ILLUMINATION ceiling for `unknown` (0.6) bound before the thing under test. A region with no highlights classifies unknown, and 0.6 is low enough to mask a mode ceiling of 0.7 and equal to the unknown-space ceiling. Every one of those was the classifier being right and the fixture being wrong — but it also shows that `unknown` illumination is a strong default cap doing real work.

attested.criterion: VisionCamera frame processors run on a worklet thread and the UI thread never blocks on colour maths
attested.verifiedBy: A device run with the frame processor active, watching the UI thread stay responsive under load. THE OPEN QUESTION THIS SETTLES: a worklet cannot call arbitrary JavaScript, so it may not be able to reach @irodora/color-sampling. Two honest answers — sample in the worklet and aggregate on the JS thread (what src/lens/camera.ts does now), or compile the engine for the worklet runtime (strictly better, and it needs a device to find out). Both share the same seam, so choosing the second later is an optimisation rather than a rewrite. The third option — reimplementing the arithmetic in the worklet — is forbidden and there is a lint that fails the build on it.

attested.criterion: yuv pixel format with conversion in the processor; every frame explicitly disposed and the pipeline does not stall
attested.verifiedBy: A device run. A retained frame stalls the pipeline within a second or two, so the symptom is obvious once a camera exists and is invisible until then. yuv is roughly 2.6x less bandwidth than rgb, which is why it is the negotiated format rather than a preference.

attested.criterion: Live pick sustains at least 15 updates per second on the reference device set
attested.verifiedBy: Measured on the reference device set (FR-13). Nothing off-device can measure it, and it is the criterion most likely to force a design change once measured — it is what would push the aggregation into the worklet.

attested.criterion: No socket opens during a scan
attested.verifiedBy: The e2e offline suite on a device (NFR-12). The BUILD-TIME half is already gated and has been since F-039: app.config.ts requests no network permission on either platform and explicitly blocks android.permission.INTERNET, so the app cannot open a socket even if a dependency tried. Gate 7 activates with this feature and F-018.

features.title: @irodora/store — SQLite, SQLCipher, migrations, sync-shaped schema
acceptance: SQLite behind one repository interface with a conformance suite that both drivers run — node:sqlite in CI, expo-sqlite on the device
Writes succeed offline and survive a reopen; reads never block on a network
The SQLCipher key lives in SecureStore, never in the app database and never in the bundle
The database is actually encrypted at rest, and a write survives a force-quit mid-transaction
features.notes: DONE, with the device half attested rather than assumed. THE DECISION IT TURNED ON: the database cannot be tested on the thing it ships on — expo-sqlite needs a device and CI is a Windows runner with none. One repository interface, TWO drivers, ONE conformance suite run against both: node:sqlite in CI (built into Node 24, SQLite 3.53.3, zero dependencies — better-sqlite3 would have to compile on every runner) and expo-sqlite+SQLCipher on the device. The limit is carried as DATA, not as a comment: the Node driver reports encryptsAtRest:false, the suite prints which driver it ran, and a test asserts it, so a green CI run cannot be read as a statement about encryption. PRAGMA foreign_keys IS THE SUBJECT OF THE SUITE. SQLite defaults it OFF and it is PER CONNECTION, so a schema full of REFERENCES enforces nothing unless it runs every time — it looks right in the DDL and accumulates orphans in silence. The check watches a bad write FAIL rather than reading the pragma back, and writing that test found the trap underneath it: PRAGMA foreign_keys IS A NO-OP INSIDE A TRANSACTION, so the first mutation (turning it off after the user_version bump, inside the migration transaction) changed nothing and the test failed for an unrelated reason. THREE ASSERTIONS WRITTEN AGAINST TESTS THAT LOOK RIGHT AND PROVE NOTHING: durability REOPENS the database, and the driver refuses reopen() on :memory: with a message saying why, because a round-trip without a reopen tests the cache; the change log is checked for WHICH row and op in WHICH order, never for a count; and a rolled-back transaction must leave NO change-log row, because a log entry describing a write that did not happen would be applied confidently by a future reconciler. THE KEY LIFECYCLE IS BEHIND AN INTERFACE BECAUSE IT IS THE PART NO DEVICE WOULD REVEAL: a key regenerated on every launch encrypts a database nobody can open again, which presents as "the app lost my data" — reported once, months later, unreproducible. It is a two-line test here. Its decoy is the one that matters: a CONSTANT key would satisfy "same on second call" perfectly and would be a key every user shares. keyPragma refuses anything that is not 64 hex characters, because PRAGMA takes no bound parameter and the key is interpolated. A test scans shipped source for a 64-hex literal, excluding test files by path. THE GUARD NO TEST COULD REPLACE: apps/mobile bundles this package, so a node:sqlite import reachable from src/index.ts is a crash on a phone and is invisible to every gate — the tests run in Node, where it resolves perfectly. The Node driver is behind @irodora/store/node and src/drivers/node.ts is exempted by explicit path, never by glob. Guard 15, planted and watched firing. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: Drizzle, which ADR-0051 section 2 names — it is a query builder over a driver, and adding it before the repository interface existed would have settled the interface by accident. Recorded as a follow-up rather than a silent omission. And change_log is written and read by NOTHING: ADR-0051 section 6 is explicit that it is not an outbox, because an outbox implies a destination and a delivery guarantee.

attested.criterion: The database is actually encrypted at rest, and a write survives a force-quit mid-transaction
attested.verifiedBy: Running apps/mobile/src/store/conformance.ts on a physical device, then inspecting the database file for SQLite header bytes — an unencrypted file begins with "SQLite format 3", an encrypted one does not. SQLCipher is not in node:sqlite, so NOTHING in CI says anything about encryption at rest; the Node driver reports encryptsAtRest:false and a test asserts it, so a green CI run cannot be mistaken for this. The force-quit case needs a real process kill mid-transaction, which is why PRAGMA synchronous is FULL rather than NORMAL. The attestation is one call rather than a day of work because the same checkStore the CI driver runs is already wired to the device driver.

attested.criterion: SQLite behind one repository interface with a conformance suite that both drivers run — node:sqlite in CI, expo-sqlite on the device
attested.verifiedBy: The CI half is gated: node:sqlite runs all seven checks every build. The DEVICE half needs a phone, and it is the half that matters — the two drivers are not the same SQLite, and a green CI run is a claim about the device driver only as far as the shared suite reaches. runDeviceStoreConformance() returns its report rather than logging it, so the evidence can be pasted into progress.md.

features.title: Wardrobe model and encrypted local storage
acceptance: Only colour and type required at creation; every other field progressively enriched
Colour grouping uses perceptual distance, not hex string sorting
Wardrobe images are encrypted with a device key held in the platform keystore; key rotation is exercised in a test
EXIF stripped on ingest; images decoded on the device under explicit byte and pixel limits read before decoding
No documentation or copy describes this as end-to-end encryption

attested.criterion: Wardrobe images are encrypted with a device key held in the platform keystore; key rotation is exercised in a test
attested.verifiedBy: A device run. TWO HALVES ARE GATED AND ONE IS NOT. Gated: the rotation LIFECYCLE — that a new key is generated through the CSPRNG port, that the database is rekeyed BEFORE the keystore is written, and that a driver refusing the rekey leaves the old key in place, which is the ordering whose failure presents months later as "the app lost my photographs". Also gated: that the bytes round-trip through a real SQLite BLOB inside the database rather than beside it. NOT GATED, and it cannot be: node:sqlite has no SQLCipher, so PRAGMA rekey cannot execute in CI at all. What the device run confirms is that a rotated database opens under the NEW key and REFUSES the old one — the same wall F-041 recorded as encryptsAtRest:false, now also covering the image bytes because they are in that file. DriverInfo.supportsRekey is carried as data and the Node driver reports false AND THROWS, so a green CI run cannot be mistaken for this.

features.notes: DONE, AND THE FIRST THING IT HAD TO DO WAS RESOLVE A CONTRADICTION BETWEEN THREE DOCUMENTS. NFR-13 says the database AND ANY STORED IMAGERY are encrypted WITH SQLCIPHER; criterion 3 says images are encrypted with a device key in the platform keystore; and data-model.md §5 said there is no image_encrypted column because "the whole database and the image directory are covered by the device’s own protection plus SQLCipher". THE THIRD WAS FACTUALLY WRONG. SQLCipher encrypts a database file; it does not reach a directory of images sitting beside it. Those would be covered by iOS Data Protection and Android FBE — real protection, and neither SQLCipher nor a key we hold. So an image_path column would have made NFR-13 FALSE WHILE APPEARING TO SATISFY IT. That is golden rule 11 one level in from the UI, and it is harder to catch because nobody reads an architecture document hunting for a claim. THE DECISION WAS PUT TO THE USER BECAUSE IT CHANGED THE DEPENDENCY FOOTPRINT, and it closed as ADR-0078: images are BLOBs in the SQLCipher database. The two rejected options are recorded with why they lost. Encrypted files on disk matches criterion 3 most literally and needs TWO NEW RUNTIME DEPENDENCIES plus a crash-safe re-encrypt loop of our own, whose recovery path is exercised on exactly the day it is needed and never before. Plain files under OS protection is what data-model.md intended and would require AMENDING NFR-13 and criterion 3 to promise less — a requirement owner’s call, not an implementer’s, and state/README.md is explicit that criteria are not edited to match what was built. The accepted option costs two things, both stated in the ADR rather than discovered: a blob read is all-or-nothing (which is why garment_image is its own table and why byte_length and the dimensions are columns beside the bytes), and archive.ts reads SELECT * so photographs join the backup and its digest. CRITERION 1 IS ENFORCED BY THE TYPE, NOT BY THE NULLABLE COLUMNS. A NewGarment carrying twelve optional fields satisfies every constraint in migration 4 and still puts twelve decisions in front of somebody adding a jumper; the requirement is about what a person is ASKED for. `NewGarment` has exactly three fields and three ts-expect-error directives prove the compiler refuses a brand at creation, a missing colour and a missing type. THE FIRST VERSION OF THAT PROVED NOTHING: NewGarment was not exported from index.ts, so the annotation resolved to `any`, all three directives went unused, and tsc said so — WHILE VITEST REPORTED 78/78 GREEN. A type assertion that never bound is indistinguishable from one that holds, and only the separate typecheck gate could tell. CRITERION 2’S DECOYS ARE THE CRITERION. A grouping test using well-separated colours passes against a hex sort, a Lab sort and a random shuffle alike, so the fixtures are adversarial to the wrong implementation specifically: #800000 and #800080 are one hex digit apart, sort adjacently, and are ΔE00 ≈ 39 apart; #FF0000 and #FE0102 differ in all three bytes and are the same red. Mutating groupByColor to a hex-distance grouping fails exactly those cases and the threshold-extremes case, and nothing else. The metric is IMPORTED from @irodora/color-difference and never re-derived — E-008’s rule — and the Lab values in the fixture are computed through the engine rather than typed in, because a hand-copied triple is a number nobody can check. CRITERION 4 NAMES SOMETHING THAT DOES NOT EXIST, AND THAT IS REPORTED RATHER THAN REINTERPRETED. "Images decoded only in THE WORKER under hard limits" — ADR-0051 retired the server tier, and .harness/rules/security/security.md still describes one ("never in the API process", "the worker runs non-root, read-only filesystem, no network egress"). CRITERION 4 WAS WRITTEN FROM THAT RULE, so the rot propagated from a rules file into the scope file. What survives is the reason: hostile bytes must not reach a decoder unbounded. On a server you contain that with a process; here there is no process to spend, so the containment happens BEFORE the decode instead of around it — byte cap, magic-byte type check, and a pixel bound read from the header, with this module never decoding anything. The "in the worker" half is not implementable and is not claimed. THE BRAND IS THE ENFORCEMENT FOR EXIF. putGarmentImage accepts only a SanitisedImage, which carries a unique symbol nothing outside image.ts can produce — so forgetting to ingest does not compile. Two ts-expect-error directives prove it, and the second plants a hand-made object with the RIGHT SHAPE, because a plain marker field would let any literal claim it and the brand would be decoration. E-041 records the link and its limit: the brand says a function ran, not what it did, so the stripping itself is gate:test with a decoy on every assertion — the metadata went AND the image is still an image. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY KEPT IS THE ICC PROFILE (APP2 / iCCP): a strip-all-metadata implementation is the obvious one and it is wrong in a colour product, because without the profile a Display P3 photograph is silently reinterpreted as sRGB and comes back muted. THOSE TWO DIRECTIVES ALSO SHIPPED BROKEN ONCE. @ts-expect-error suppresses the compile error and DOES NOT STOP THE STATEMENT RUNNING: written inline they type-checked as intended and then executed, passing a raw buffer into a SQL bind and failing the suite for a reason unrelated to what they assert. They now live in a declared-and-never-called function, where the compiler reads them and the runtime does not. WIDENING THE DRIVER INTERFACE BROKE THE APP, EXACTLY AS E-023 PREDICTED. That link’s `to` names apps/mobile/src/store, and adding rekey to Driver made the device driver an incomplete implementation — the link named the dependent BEFORE it broke, which is the whole return on keeping the graph. Fixed in the same change: the device driver implements rekey through SQLCipher’s pragma, reports supportsRekey: true, and the conformance report carries it so a device run is evidence for the attestation. It also produced a correction worth keeping — the driver first called keyPragma(newKey).replace("PRAGMA key", "PRAGMA rekey"), string surgery on a validated statement that works and is one careless edit from not. rekeyPragma now shares the hex validation, because both statements interpolate a key into SQL that takes no bound parameter. E-023 ALSO PREDICTED THE ARCHIVE, AND NO DUPLICATE LINK WAS ADDED. ARCHIVE_TABLES derives from SYNC_TABLES, so garment_image joined the backup format and its canonical digest with nobody editing archive.ts. E-023 covers exactly that and a second link would be noise; what was added is the ASSERTION, so the behaviour is a decision rather than something a user discovers from an export that grew. GATE 0’S RETIRED-VOCABULARY CHECK CANNOT SEE THIS CLASS OF ROT, and the proof is that it missed its own vocabulary. It builds its subject list from acceptance entries, attested criteria and PRD rows — architecture, ADR and rule documents are entirely outside its corpus. docs/architecture/security/privacy-design.md §4 contained "per-tenant data key", one of the check’s own seven terms, and gate 0 was green over it for months. §4 also still described TLS 1.3, HSTS, certificate pinning and a KMS master key, and justified not claiming end-to-end encryption with "the server can decrypt wardrobe images" — a reason that depends on a server ADR-0051 retired. REWRITTEN: the phrase is still wrong, now because THERE IS ONE END, and what the encryption protects against is a lost or stolen phone. Two more places denied it for the retired reason — .harness/rules/security/privacy.md and the security-review skill — and were corrected here rather than filed, deliberately and narrowly, because a rules file is read as binding and the sentence was false about the product’s security posture in the exact subject this feature was building. The remainder is F-107. AN INVENTED COLUMN WAS REMOVED BEFORE IT SHIPPED. A sha256 on garment_image was drafted for an archive comparison nothing asked for; implementing it honestly meant either a hash port to install at startup or a hand-rolled SHA-256 in a package that carries no runtime dependency. Neither is F-042’s business. Extra scope is as much a failure as missing scope. GATES RUN, all green on the pinned toolchain: state, the effect-id and state-id proofs, the mirror and lockfile proofs, typecheck, lint, format, test (109 in @irodora/store), build, security and content. E2E IS IN THIS FEATURE’S VERIFICATION LIST AND COULD NOT RUN — gate 7 is pending and F-091 is blocked on an emulator this workstation has no JDK for. Nothing here proves a person ever adds a garment through a screen, because there is no screen; that is F-043. NOT APPLICABLE: color-golden (the metric is imported, no engine maths moved), cvd, contrast, a11y, perf, artifact. TWO FILTERS THAT REPORTED SUCCESS WITHOUT RUNNING, both caught by reading the output rather than the exit code. `pnpm --filter irodora-mobile typecheck` matched no package and exited 0 — the package is @irodora/mobile — so the app was briefly believed to compile against the widened Driver interface when nothing had checked. And a hard-coded `expect(applied).toBe(1)` in F-026’s migration test broke on migration 4; it is now derived from MIGRATIONS, because the number it asserted was "the migrations that did not exist when this was written".

features.title: Add-garment flows
acceptance: Camera, Lens scan, manual colour and image upload
Median time to add an item 20 seconds or less, measured on device
Never more than two required fields

attested.criterion: Median time to add an item 20 seconds or less, measured on device
attested.verifiedBy: Timed runs on physical devices from the reference matrix, recorded with the device and OS version

features.notes: DONE. F-042 made the wardrobe storable; this is the screen that makes it reachable. Four entry paths (criterion 1) — a Lens reading, a corpus colour, a photo from the library and one from the camera — with the two photo paths behind an injected `ImageSource` port so all four are exercised off-device. CRITERION 3 IS HELD BY A TYPE, NOT BY THE SCREEN. `NewGarment` has three properties, one of them generated, so a caller supplies two — and a third requirement would mean editing a type `@irodora/store` owns and F-042’s ts-expect-error guards. `draftProblem` only picks which sentence to show. THE TEST IS THE INVERSE OF THE OBVIOUS ONE: a test that saves a fully-populated draft proves nothing about "never more than two required fields", so the assertion sweeps the twelve other fields ONE AT A TIME. A single "the minimal draft saves" test would keep passing while somebody added a mandatory brand, because the minimal draft would still be minimal. THE BUG THAT ONLY APPEARS WHEN A SECOND READER ARRIVES, AND THE REASON IT NEEDED ITS OWN LINK. `handoff.ts` is a one-slot mailbox: offerReading writes and takeReading CONSUMES, which is right for one reader and F-097 built it with profile setup as the only one. Make the wardrobe a second reader and somebody who scans a garment and passes through profile setup on the way has the reading EATEN THERE — the wardrobe finds an empty slot and asks them to scan again, and the profile has been offered an estimate built from a jumper. BOTH SCREENS SEE `null` AND NEITHER CAN TELL THAT FROM NOBODY HAVING SCANNED. No type catches it (both readers want a LensReading and both get one, or do not) and no existing test catches it (each screen plants an offer and reads it back, and the two never run in the same process in the order that breaks). The offer gained a destination, still one slot, and a MISMATCHED TAKE LEAVES THE OFFER STANDING — consuming it and returning null would be the original bug wearing a parameter. THE GUARD IS A PAIR AND EITHER HALF ALONE PROVES NOTHING. A takeReading that ignored its argument passes every other assertion in that describe block: the offer is written, read back, null on the second read, and replaced by a second offer — all still true. Watched failing, twice: dropping only the destination comparison turns exactly those two red and leaves the other 379 green, before and after the optional-chain rewrite lint asked for. Recorded as E-042. E-037 WAS NOT EXTENDED: that link is about a privacy claim on the profile screen, and this is a different failure with a different tell. THE LINT THAT ALREADY ANTICIPATED THIS FEATURE. Two of the four paths need a picker and apps/mobile had none. eslint.config.mjs bans expo-file-system, expo-media-library, node:fs and fs from the Lens AND from every route — "a camera frame may never be written to a file" (NFR-12, ADR-0026) — and its own message says "if a surface here genuinely needs the filesystem, it is not the Lens". IT DOES NOT NEED IT: expo-image-picker is asked for `base64`, the bytes go through ingestImage, and they become a BLOB in the SQLCipher database (ADR-0078). The photograph is never a file this app manages, so NOTHING HERE ASKS FOR AN EXEMPTION and the rule stays exactly as strict as it is. EXPECTED_PERMISSIONS WAS DELIBERATELY NOT WIDENED. READ_MEDIA_IMAGES may appear in the shipped APK on Android 13+, and gate 16 asserts the artefact’s permission set EQUALS the expected list in both directions. F-085 records that the first genuinely signed artefact failed that check on three permissions no dependency and no source file named — which is exactly why the gate reads the artefact rather than the config. A red gate naming a permission is the correct outcome here; the list moves in response to a build rather than in anticipation of one. The picker’s compatibility with Expo 57 was checked BEFORE the manifest was edited (57.0.14, peer `expo: *`), because "both are latest" is not evidence. THREE CHECKS CAUGHT THREE REAL THINGS. (1) The a11y check found TWELVE UNNAMED BUTTONS — each corpus swatch wrapped in a Pressable with a role and no accessible name, which is a screen reader announcing "button" twelve times and looks perfect in a screenshot. swatchAccessibleName composes the name, the hex AND the provenance. (2) The token-reach check refused `display.1`: its declaration says "no screen leads with a display size; every one of them opens at title", which is a DESIGN CONVENTION — so the honest fix was to follow it rather than edit the declaration, because the check was right and the screen was the new thing. (3) The i18n check refused twenty keys with no renderer, which forced the correct order: the screen first, then the copy it uses. THE JAPANESE IS UNREVIEWED AND THE COUNT SAYS SO. Twenty new keys, none added to JA_REVIEWED, and the suite prints 0/278 reviewed, 278 OUTSTANDING. OQ-5 is closed as a DECISION (ADR-0060, one editor) rather than answered, so the reviewer this waits for is not engaged. What must never happen is "a missing translation fails the build" quietly becoming "an unreviewed translation passes silently", and the count is the mechanism that stops it. ONE CLAIM THE SCREEN MUST NEVER MAKE. A Lens capture is stored with source `estimated` and the reading’s own confidence, and ITS NAME IS THE HEX. Naming it after the corpus entry it lands closest to would be an assertion of identity — exactly what FR-13 forbids and what the claims lint bans phrases for. The button offering the reading says it is an estimate, and nothing offers to name it. GATES RUN, all green on the pinned toolchain: state, typecheck, lint, format, test (381 in the app), build, a11y, contrast, perf, security, and both id proofs. E2E IS IN THIS FEATURE’S VERIFICATION LIST AND COULD NOT RUN — gate 7 is pending, F-091 is blocked on an emulator with no JDK here, and this is the feature e2e was most for: nothing here proves the four paths work as a JOURNEY, only that each reaches the store through a port. ARTIFACT could not run either; it needs an APK from CI, and it is where the permission question above gets answered. NOT APPLICABLE: color-golden (no engine maths — the conversions are imported), cvd, content. THE ATTESTED CRITERION WAS ALREADY DECLARED AND STAYS OUTSTANDING. "Median time to add an item 20 seconds or less, measured on device." The screen is built for it — two fields at the top, the four colour paths beside them, everything else under a heading that says out loud it is optional — but a layout argument is not a measurement, and this one needs devices from the reference matrix.

features.title: Outfit builder
acceptance: Compose slots, lock items, swap colours, regenerate
The same locked set and versions always regenerate the same candidates
features.notes: DONE. THE ENGINE ALREADY HAD THE MULTI-LOCK ANSWER AND FINDING IT IS THE FEATURE. `recommendOutfit` takes ONE anchor garment and fills every other slot; FR-33 wants N LOCKED SLOTS constraining generation, and no engine call does that. The tempting fix — score candidates against each locked garment in the app and combine — is NEW COLOUR ARITHMETIC IN THE APP, which E-008 is precisely about: a second implementation makes the same outfit rank differently on two surfaces, both pass their own tests, and nothing runs both. `scoreOutfit` ALREADY TAKES THE WHOLE COMPOSED OUTFIT, so generation is "for each unlocked slot, for each candidate, compose locks+candidate and ask the engine". Every judgement is the engine’s; the only arithmetic in builder.ts is a comparison. That is why this stayed a mobile feature rather than becoming an engine change. CRITERION 2 NEEDED THE TEST THAT CAN FAIL. "Call it twice and compare" passes for an implementation that is entirely order-dependent AND for one that caches — it checks the function is not actively random, which was never in doubt because the engine is pure. THE THREAT IS THE APP’S ORDERING: `sort` is stable, so two equally-scored garments come back in WARDROBE ORDER, and that order changes the day somebody adds a jumper. So the assertions are the same locks over a REVERSED wardrobe, and a tie broken on garment id (a UUIDv7, stable and unique). BOTH MUTATIONS FAILED EXACTLY ONE TEST EACH, AND THEY WERE DIFFERENT TESTS. Dropping the id tie-break failed only "breaks a tie on id, not on arrival". Scoring the candidate alone with the locks ignored failed only "scores the candidate WITH the locked garments". WORTH NOTING: the reversed-wardrobe test did NOT catch the missing tie-break, because no two garments in that fixture tie. Two assertions, two properties, neither redundant — which is the opposite of the F-003 evaluation’s finding, where one mutation broke two assertions at once and hid a hole. THIS IS WHERE SIX NUMBERS FINALLY REACH A PERSON. F-031 built the component scores and its own note said the quiet part — "nothing here proves a person ever SEES six numbers", because e2e was in its list and could not run. This screen renders them, and F-031’s criterion 2 is honoured at the surface it was written for: THE OVERALL APPEARS BESIDE ITS COMPONENTS, NEVER INSTEAD OF THEM. The builder ranks on the score OBJECT rather than a number precisely so that stays possible one layer up. F-108 HAD TO LAND FIRST AND THAT IS WHY THIS FEATURE WAS PARKED. Turning a stored garment into an OutfitPiece needs its colour as a `Color`, and ADR-0005 will not produce one without complete provenance — a Lens-captured garment could not supply it until F-108 stored the capture conditions. The builder was drafted, deleted rather than left half-written in the tree, and rebuilt from the plan afterwards; it COMPILED FIRST TRY on the second attempt, which is what a real blocker looks like once it is actually removed. THE FONT SUBSET WAS A TRACING STEP THIS TIME. F-043 shipped with gate 11 red because new Japanese copy introduced kanji outside the bundled subset. Here the eleven new ja keys were followed straight to generate-font-subset.mjs IN THE SAME CHANGE — 642,136 to 645,176 bytes — and gate 11 was run before anything was committed. The lesson from one feature earlier, applied rather than recorded a second time. AN UNRECOGNISED GARMENT TYPE FILLS NO SLOT. `garment.type` is free text because FR-39 asks for two fields and not a taxonomy, so `slotFor` maps the words people actually type and returns null for anything else. NOT DEFAULTED TO `top`: a belt silently proposed as a shirt is worse than one the builder does not offer, because the second is visible and the first is not. Widening the vocabulary is a content question — the taxonomy is content/’s — and guessing at it here would be the second place garment vocabulary is defined. GATES RUN, all green: state, typecheck, lint, format, test (398 in the app), build, a11y, contrast, content and security. E2E IS IN THIS FEATURE’S VERIFICATION LIST AND COULD NOT RUN — gate 7 is pending on F-091, and nothing here proves the compose/lock/regenerate loop works as a JOURNEY, only that each step is correct in isolation. That is the third feature in a row owing the same thing, and it is now worth reading as one item rather than three. NOT APPLICABLE: color-golden (no engine maths — every judgement is an imported call), cvd (the CVD component lives inside scoreOutfit, unchanged), perf, artifact. DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT, so the absences are decisions rather than omissions. PERSISTING AN OUTFIT: `outfit` and `outfit_item` are in the data-model sketch and in no migration; no criterion asks for a saved outfit, and adding a table nothing reads is the shape F-041 refused with change_log. OCCASION WEIGHTING (FR-34) and CVD OUTFIT MODE (FR-35): separate requirements this feature does not claim. SWAPPING A COLOUR INDEPENDENTLY OF A GARMENT: FR-33 says "swap colours", and in a wardrobe a colour arrives attached to a garment — so swapping the garment is how a colour changes, and the alternative is recolouring a jumper somebody owns.

features.title: Preference feedback loop
acceptance: Repeated selection shifts a stored, inspectable per-user weight
The user can see and reset it
No model training; feedback affects only the submitting user, never global ranking
features.notes: DONE. THE DECISION THE REST DEPENDS ON: the table stores COUNTS and never a weight. The obvious shape is one `weight REAL` column nudged on each observation, and it is wrong in a way that is invisible until it bites — a running float depends on the ORDER the updates arrived in and on the HISTORY of the update function, so changing the step size in a later release silently changes what every stored row means with nothing able to detect it. `accepted` and `rejected` are facts about what somebody did; `preferenceWeight()` is a pure function of them. FR-37’s "deterministic" and "inspectable" are then true BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by discipline, and the formula can be corrected later without corrupting stored state because the state is not the formula’s output. FAMILIES, NOT INDIVIDUAL COLOURS, OR NOTHING EVER LEARNS. Keyed on published entries the space is 120 x 120 and a person would have to pick the same two entries repeatedly for anything to move — the loop would be correct and INERT. The corpus carries taxonomy.family: 25 families over 120 entries, COUNTED rather than assumed, which is 325 unordered pairs and generalises across a wardrobe. Unordered and enforced twice: the writer sorts, and CHECK (family_a <= family_b) with UNIQUE makes a second row impossible. A rule enforced only by the writer holds until somebody writes a second writer, so a test plants a mis-ordered row directly and watches the database refuse it. THE LINE THIS FEATURE EXISTS TO HOLD: preference multiplies `harmony` AND NOTHING ELSE. If it reached `cvdAccessibility`, somebody who repeatedly chose a pairing a deutan cannot separate would GRADUALLY STOP BEING TOLD SO — golden rule 13 defeated not by removing the channel but by teaching the system to stop using it. The same shape applies to `contrast`: a floor that erodes with use is not a floor. And `personalFit` is what the person SAID about themselves while preference is what they DID; letting one write the other makes the profile unfalsifiable. ASSERTED PER COMPONENT in a loop over OUTFIT_COMPONENTS with harmony skipped, because "the overall moved" passes for an implementation that moved the WRONG one — which is the entire failure. Recorded as E-043. TWO MUTATIONS, TWO DISTINCT FAILURES. Applying the multiplier to `contrast` as well failed exactly one test of 121 — "MOVES NOTHING BUT HARMONY". Setting PREFERENCE_NEUTRAL to 0.999 failed FIVE, led by "multiplies by EXACTLY one". The second is what protects every existing caller: `scoreOutfit` gained an OPTIONAL argument and every call site written before it passes nothing, so neutral must be EXACTLY 1 rather than approximately — 0.999 would silently re-rank the whole product while every other assertion in the file stayed green. THE BOUND IS PART OF THE GUARANTEE RATHER THAN TUNING. Plus or minus 25% around 1, saturating at eight net observations. Unbounded, preference eventually promotes a pairing the engine scored badly, and at that point the six component scores are decoration because the answer is the person’s habit wearing the engine’s clothes. FR-11 promises a decomposition somebody can argue with, and nobody can argue with a number that is mostly their own past behaviour reflected back. The constants are JUDGEMENTS and are labelled as such: eight is "a habit shows within a week of ordinary use, and one stray tap moves it 3% and is undone by one tap back". THE WEIGHT IS A FUNCTION OF THE NET, DELIBERATELY. A pairing accepted twelve times and rejected ten is one somebody keeps RECONSIDERING, not one they like — using the totals would let it outrank a pairing chosen cleanly three times, which is the opposite of what the person expressed. Asserted directly. RESET IS A HARD DELETE, ALONE AMONG THE DELETES HERE. Every other delete is a tombstone because a sync reconciler must tell "deleted" from "never existed". A tombstone here would be A RECORD OF WHAT SOMEBODY ASKED TO HAVE FORGOTTEN, and a change-log row saying "pairing_preference rust/charcoal was updated" is the same record wearing another name — so the rows and their log entries both go. WITH A DECOY: another test asserts the OTHER tables’ history survives, because a reset implemented as DELETE FROM change_log would pass the first assertion and erase everything. CRITERION 2 IS HALF MET AND SAYS SO. "The user can see and reset it" — `listPreferences()` returns every pairing with its counts and `resetPreferences()` removes them, so the data IS inspectable and IS resettable. NOTHING RENDERS IT, so no person can currently see anything. This feature is `service: packages` with `verification: [state, test]` and no a11y, so a screen was not claimed and was not built. FILED AS F-109 rather than counted as met — the same shape as F-031, which built six component scores and said in its own notes that nothing proved a person ever saw them, with F-045 finally showing them two releases later. Recording it as a gap is the difference between a gap and a claim. THE CLAIMS LINT CAUGHT ME WRITING A BANNED PHRASE, THREE TIMES. `exact colou?r` is one of the eleven banned constructions (ADR-0031, NFR-21) and I had written it in a plan heading, a plan sentence and a migration comment — meaning GRANULARITY rather than accuracy. The lint does not distinguish and should not: ADR-0031 bans the construction because a phrase migrates, from a heading to a sentence to a field name to copy. REWORDED rather than exempted, because an inline marker would have spent an exemption on prose that had no need of the phrase, and exemptions are for lines that must name the thing in order to forbid it. A RED GATE THAT WAS NOT, AND ONE THAT WAS. Lint reported red in two CONCURRENT sweeps before this, which is exactly the collision F-108 recorded — verify-guards writes fixtures at fixed paths and overlapping runs clobber each other. This time the ISOLATED run was red too, for a real reason. The F-108 lesson held in the useful direction: it says a concurrent red is evidence about the sweep rather than that a red is always noise, and running it alone is what told the two apart. GATES RUN, all green: state, typecheck, lint, format, test (121 engine, 124 store), build, content and security. This feature’s own list is state and test; the rest were run because a migration and a new engine input touch them. NOT APPLICABLE: color-golden (no colour maths — the multiplier scales a component and derives no colour), cvd, contrast, a11y, perf, artifact, e2e.

features.title: Wardrobe coverage and gap analysis
acceptance: Reports valid outfit count and outfits per garment; recomputes incrementally on change
Gaps named in product language with the outfits they would unlock
features.notes: DONE. "VALID" CANNOT MEAN "ONE GARMENT PER SLOT". tops x trousers x shoes is a multiplication wearing the name of a score: it says nothing about colour and RISES WHEN YOU BUY A SECOND BLACK JUMPER, which is the opposite of what somebody asking "how much does my wardrobe give me" wants to know. A valid outfit clears COVERAGE_THRESHOLD; scoreOutfit produces the number and coverage.ts counts without judging. The threshold is EXPORTED because "34 outfits" is a measurement with no units unless the bar is stated beside it. The first assertion is that an impossible threshold gives 0 rather than t x r x s, with a floor-level threshold as its decoy — a coverage that always returned 0 would pass the first one alone. CRITERION 1 IS CHECKED OVER A SEQUENCE, NOT A CHANGE. An incremental cache that drifts is worse than no cache: it is confidently wrong and nothing looks broken. So applyChange is compared with a full recompute AT EVERY STEP of a sequence of adds and removes — one change proves one path, and the failure mode is state that ACCUMULATES. Counts are rebuilt from the surviving combination set rather than decremented, because decrementing is faster and is exactly how such a cache drifts: one missed decrement is invisible for months and then the numbers are simply wrong with nothing to point at. TWO MUTATIONS, EACH HITTING ITS OWN PAIR: keeping stale combinations on removal failed the REMOVE and SEQUENCE tests; ignoring the threshold failed the counts-nothing test and the zero-count garment. THE GAP VOCABULARY ALREADY EXISTED, AND FINDING THAT WAS THE FEATURE. FR-43 wants gaps "named in product language" and its own example is "no warm light neutral" — and content/rules/phrase-lexicon.*.json ALREADY PUBLISHES EXACTLY THAT: 18 English terms, each constraining OKLCh axes, each with a rationale an editor wrote, at a version, parsed by @irodora/corpus and already read by the Finder. Inventing a second vocabulary in the engine would have been E-013’s shape. THE DECOY THAT PROVES THE WORDS ARE CONTENT: removing a term from the fixture lexicon must remove the gap names that used it — hard-coding two term names fails exactly that one test of 139. THE CONSEQUENCE IS STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED: the gaps this can name are exactly the ones the lexicon can express, and publishing no term for a region means none is reported there. THE HONEST LIMIT IS A LIMIT AND NOT A LOOP BOUND. A lightness-and-chroma region HAS NO HUE, so a representative colour needs one chosen — and choosing one would be this file inventing the most consequential part of the answer. Below NEUTRAL_CHROMA the problem does not exist, because F-101 established that a hue angle on a near-neutral is a rounding artefact, and the lexicon’s own `neutral` term ends at EXACTLY 0.039, the same number. So the hue is arbitrary AND DEMONSTRABLY DOES NOT MATTER, which is the only condition under which picking one is honest. Above it, "light vivid" without a hue is unactionable and a claim this file cannot support, so the hue-bearing half is FILED rather than guessed. THE TWO 0.039s ARE DELIBERATELY NOT COLLAPSED INTO ONE CONSTANT: one is a CONTENT boundary an editor chose for a word, the other an ENGINE boundary F-101 measured for when hue stops meaning anything. They agree today and are free to diverge, and if an editor widened `neutral`, gaps should still refuse to invent a hue above where the engine says hue is real. THE UNLOCK COUNT IS A PROJECTION AND THE TYPE SAYS SO. "How many outfits would this unlock" needs a garment that does not exist, so every Gap carries the `representative` colour it projected from — the number is reproducible and its basis is visible. Golden rule 11 applies to our own reports as much as to the UI, and carrying the evidence makes reporting the number without it inconvenient rather than impossible. E-044 RECORDS THAT THE LEXICON HAS TWO READERS NOW AND THEY FAIL DIFFERENTLY. When an editor removes a term the Finder stops matching a typed phrase — visible and self-reporting, because somebody searches and gets nothing. `gaps` loses the ability to NAME a region, so none is reported there, AND SILENCE IS EXACTLY WHAT "YOU HAVE NO GAPS" LOOKS LIKE. Recorded with its limit: nothing checks that the lexicon can still express every region a wardrobe might lack, because that would require knowing every wardrobe. THE PERF BUDGET, AND A MEASUREMENT TAKEN UNDER THE WRONG CONDITIONS. `perf` is in this feature’s verification list, and running gate 12 without adding a budget would have been running a gate that says nothing about the change. THE FIRST CEILING WAS WRONG AND THE WAY IT WAS WRONG IS THE USEFUL PART: a scratch script measured the increment at 4.79 ms and the ceiling was set to 25 ms, then the harness reported 22.66 ms — five times my number. The scratch script used a 12-ENTRY reference set while the bench uses the FULL 120-ENTRY published corpus, and corpusAffinity and versatility scan that set. THAT IS THE SAME ERROR AS QUOTING A BENCHMARK FROM A DIFFERENT MACHINE, and it nearly shipped as a rationale citing numbers that did not apply. Re-measured THROUGH THE HARNESS so the conditions are identical by construction: whole recompute p95 216.8 ms, incremental p95 23.0 ms, a 9.4x ratio matching the theoretical 10x. The ceiling is 60 ms — about 2.6x the observation so GC and a loaded workstation survive it, and about a quarter of the full recompute so an applyChange that quietly called coverage() lands near 217 ms and fails loudly. The rejected 25 ms had nine per cent of headroom, and a gate that flakes gets disabled. GATES RUN ONE AT A TIME, all green: state, typecheck, lint, format, test (139 engine, 124 store, 398 app), build, bench and the bench proof. NOT APPLICABLE: color-golden (no colour maths — every judgement is scoreOutfit’s), cvd, contrast, a11y, content (nothing published changed; the lexicon is only read), security, artifact, e2e. AND I BROKE THE ONE-AT-A-TIME RULE WHILE RUNNING THEM, one feature after recording it: `test` was launched while `lint` was still going, and both were re-run alone before anything was written down. The rule is easy to state and easy to forget under momentum, which is the argument for it being a rule rather than a habit. DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT: the surface — service is packages and a11y is not in the verification list, so nothing renders a coverage number or a gap and that is filed rather than counted, as F-046’s was. Also not built: hue-bearing gaps above NEUTRAL_CHROMA; capsule optimisation (F-050), which this unblocks; and any recommendation of a PURCHASE, because a gap is a region rather than a product.

features.title: Duplicate detection
acceptance: Flags items within DeltaE00 5 in the same category, showing the measured difference
features.notes: DONE. DELIVERED: packages/optimization/src/duplicates.ts — findDuplicates(items, threshold) returning every same-category pair closer than DUPLICATE_DELTA_E, each carrying its measured DeltaE00, closest first with an id tie-break so the ordering is total. 10 tests. BUILT IN THE WRONG PACKAGE FIRST: the plan header said @irodora/recommendation, carried forward from F-046 without checking. This record said @irodora/optimization all along, and ARCHITECTURE.md draws the line — recommendation is rules, weights, scoring and explanation objects; optimization is capsule and coverage solvers. Duplicate detection asks about the wardrobe as a SET, so it belongs in optimization. Moved before this feature closed, and @irodora/optimization gained color-difference and color-spaces as workspace dependencies. EVERY GATE WAS GREEN WITH THE CODE IN THE WRONG PACKAGE — gate 0 does not check that a feature landed in the package its record names, so nothing was ever going to say so. Found by reading this record while waiting for a gate. F-110 files the same defect for F-048, which is already committed. THE OPTIMISATION SOMEBODY WILL REACH FOR IS WRONG, NOT SLOW: DeltaE00 violates the triangle inequality, so no spatial index over it prunes correctly. Pairwise within a category, and said so in the file. CATEGORY IS THE GARMENT TYPE, NOT THE SLOT: a jumper and a coat are both top and are not duplicates; the decoy is two identical colours on different types. THE THRESHOLD IS THE REQUIREMENT S, NOT A JUDGEMENT: 5 from FR-44, unlike F-048 s COVERAGE_THRESHOLD which had to be chosen. Strict, per the PRD s "< 5" against the criterion s ambiguous "within 5", asserted at the boundary. THE MEASURED DIFFERENCE IS RETURNED, NEVER A BOOLEAN — half the criterion, and the test recomputes deltaE00 independently rather than comparing against the number the function produced. MUTATIONS WATCHED FAILING: category check removed -> the cross-category test failed alone; >= threshold -> > threshold -> the boundary test failed alone. GATES: state, typecheck, lint, format, test, build all PASS, run one at a time, and all re-run after the move because a green gate on code in the wrong package proves nothing. NOT APPLICABLE: color-golden — no colour maths is added or changed, deltaE00 is called and not defined; also cvd, contrast, a11y, content, perf, security, artifact, e2e. NO NEW EFFECT LINK: no shared contract, no behaviour changed. NOT DELIVERED: the surface. service is packages and a11y is not in the verification list, so nothing renders the warning. Third feature running (F-046, F-048, F-049) that computes something no person can see yet.

features.title: Capsule optimiser
acceptance: Solves at least N outfits from at most M garments for a 40-item wardrobe within NFR-4
Branch-and-bound with a heuristic seed and a hard time budget
Returns best-so-far on expiry; the result is deterministic and reproducible
features.notes: DONE. DELIVERED: packages/optimization/src/capsule.ts — solveCapsule(coverage, {targetOutfits, maxGarments, nodeBudget, deadlineMs, now}) returning the smallest garment set reaching N outfits under M garments, with meetsTarget, stoppedBy, reproducible and nodesExplored. 18 tests. N and M are the QUESTION, not constants — FR-45 asks "at least N from at most M". THE TWO CRITERIA CONTRADICT EACH OTHER AS WRITTEN. Criterion 2 wants a hard time budget; criterion 3 wants the result deterministic and reproducible. A wall clock plus best-so-far is NOT reproducible — a faster machine explores more in 3s and returns a better subset. Put to the user, who chose: TWO LIMITS. A deterministic nodeBudget is the primary stop (same input, same nodes, same answer, anywhere) and the wall clock is a backstop carrying NFR-4 s 3s. stoppedBy reports which fired and reproducible is exactly stoppedBy !== deadline, so when the clock does fire the caller is TOLD rather than handed a machine-dependent answer claiming to be reproducible. AT 40 ITEMS EVERY SOLVE STOPS ON nodes, so the clock is never what ends it and results are identical everywhere; the honest cost is that optimality is NOT PROVEN at that size. NO COLOUR MATHS AT ALL: coverage() already decided which outfits are valid, so this reduces to a max-coverage-shaped subset selection over Coverage.combinations. NP-hard, which is why the criterion names branch-and-bound. F-110 s payoff — coverage() is in this package now. THREE DEFECTS THE MUTATIONS FOUND. (1) THE OPTIMALITY TEST WAS NOT DISCRIMINATING: weakening the bound to over-prune went GREEN, because the symmetric GRID fixture is already solved by the greedy seed so the search never had to work. Replaced with a fixed-seed LCG generating 40 lopsided instances, each compared against exhaustive search at every target. (2) THE HEURISTIC SEED WAS A NO-OP: an outfit is three garments, so the first garment completes nothing, every candidate scored gain 0, bestGain started at 0, and the loop returned an EMPTY seed for every wardrobe there is. Criterion 2 asks for a heuristic seed and there was not one. Fixed by ranking on POTENTIAL — combinations a garment could still reach — with gain primary. (3) THE GREEDY-TRAP FIXTURE DID NOT TRAP GREEDY: a1 and a2 sorted first AND were a compatible pair, so index order stumbled into the right answer. Rebuilt so the alphabetically-first garments sit in different combinations. FOUR MUTATIONS WATCHED FAILING: bound over-prunes (1 test), never search (7), seed ignores potential (1), the original no-op seed (3). 46 GREEN TESTS SAID NOTHING ABOUT THE TYPE ERROR: noUncheckedIndexedAccess makes typed-array reads number|undefined and four compound assignments were errors under it, but vitest transpiles without typechecking so the suite was green while build was red. Surfaced through the BENCH, which resolves via dist/ and died on "does not provide an export named solveCapsule" — the stale-dist hazard F-110 s plan listed as a risk, one feature later. THE DEVICE BUDGET STAYED PUT. capsule-solve-p95 (3000ms, device) was committed in F-038 BEFORE this feature existed precisely so it could not be chosen to fit; untouched and still NOT RUN. New capsule-solve-node-p95 is node-reference scoped: p95 166.42ms, median 135.30ms, ceiling 400ms, 30 runs, 40 garments and 2366 combinations. Its rationale records that the number is flat across queries because every solve exhausts the node budget, so the gate watches cost per node and raising CAPSULE_NODE_BUDGET would push straight through it. EFFECT E-046 (high): Coverage.combinations joins sorted ids on a pipe, which was a private encoding while applyChange only compared whole keys. solveCapsule SPLITS them, so the encoding is a contract no type describes. Changing the separator fails loudly; an id CONTAINING one parses into the wrong number of wrong ids and returns a capsule naming garments that do not exist. Not live — ids are UUIDv7 — and recorded because the constraint is written nowhere else. GATES one at a time: state, typecheck, lint, format, test (optimization 46), build, perf — all PASS. NOT APPLICABLE: color-golden (no colour maths added, changed or called), cvd, contrast, a11y, content, security, artifact, e2e. NOT DELIVERED: the surface, for the fifth feature running (F-046, F-048, F-049, F-110, F-050 all compute what nobody can see). Also not delivered: proof of optimality at 40 items, and any evidence about a phone.

features.title: Cost-per-wear
acceptance: Computed from cost and recorded wears; absent data yields unknown, never an invented estimate
features.notes: DONE. THE COLUMNS EXISTED AND NOTHING HAD EVER WRITTEN THEM. `cost_minor`, `currency` and `wear_count` have been on `garment` since F-042's migration 4, and no code path in the app had ever set one — so cost per wear was a division whose denominator could only ever be zero. A module built and tested against that schema alone would have passed every test it had by answering "unknown" forever, on every garment that could exist, because the fixtures were the missing writer. That is the session's lesson and it is recorded as [[a-column-nothing-writes-makes-its-own-feature-unfalsifiable]]. FR-46 therefore had three parts, not one: the division, a way for a price to arrive, and a way for a wear to be recorded. Any one alone is inert. THE REFUSAL IS THE REQUIREMENT, AND IT HAS THREE NAMES. `costPerWear` returns a discriminated union, never `number | null`: `noCost`, `noCurrency` and `neverWorn` are three different situations with three different things to do about them, and one silent "unknown" for all three is the ambiguity F-119 removed from the Lens one level down. THREE MUTATIONS WERE RUN AND EACH FAILED ITS OWN CASE AND ONLY ITS OWN. `if (!garment.costMinor)` failed exactly "a garment that genuinely cost nothing is known, at zero" — a gift has a price and it is zero, and falsiness cannot tell that from a column nobody filled in. Dropping the `wearCount <= 0` check failed exactly the Infinity cases; `4550 / 0` is a number, of type number, that renders as a word. A fixed exponent of 2 failed six cases including yen. The baseline was re-run green after each. THE EXPONENT TABLE IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE WORLD AND IS NOW AN EFFECT LINK. `cost_minor` is stored at a scale the row does not record: the exponent comes from ISO 4217 at write time and from the same table at read time. Change one entry and every price already stored for that currency is silently reinterpreted, in the plausible direction, with no error anywhere — the E-001 shape applied to money. Filed as E-052 with a guard that pins ALL twenty-six non-default entries by value, proven by changing CLP from 0 to 2 and watching the suite name it. An illustrative test over JPY and KWD would have let that through. A `minor_unit_digits` column is the right answer the day a price crosses a boundary; none exists, and adding it now is the shape F-042 refused twice in one migration. COST PER WEAR LIVES IN THE OUTFIT BUILDER BECAUSE FR-41 HAS NO SCREEN. The outfit builder is the only surface where a garment somebody owns is on screen, and the only moment at which a person says they are wearing something. That is correct for this feature and the wrong long-term home, so the missing browse-and-edit surface is filed as F-122 — along with the coverage-map row that reports FR-41 as delivered by a `packages` feature whose service cannot satisfy the e2e and a11y gates named beside it. THE FIGURE IS SHOWN BESIDE THE NUMBERS IT CAME FROM. `Per wear: 119.74 GBP` alone asks to be believed; with `Price and wears: 45.50 GBP / 38` under it, it can be checked — which is why `costPerWear` carries its inputs back rather than returning a scalar. E-017 FIRED FOR REAL AND WAS RESOLVED IN THE SAME CHANGE. Ten codepoints from the new Japanese copy were missing from the bundled subset — 購 価 例 通 貨 額 両 桁 超 費 — and the subset was regenerated (655,468 to 661,088 bytes, 520 required, 851 in the face) before any gate was declared. F-045's lesson applied rather than recorded a second time. GATES RUN, all green: 0 state (18 checks), 1 typecheck, 2 lint, 3 format, 4 test (mobile 446, up from 414), 5 build, 8 a11y (130), 9 contrast (130), 11 content, color-golden, cvd, security:keys. NOT RUN: e2e (gate 7 is still pending on F-091), perf (no budget claimed here), artifact. NOT APPLICABLE: color-golden has nothing to judge — this is integer division and a table, and a golden dataset for a division would be theatre. DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT. A wear LOG: `wear_count` is a counter and *when* something was worn is a different question with a different table, which no criterion asks. Currency CONVERSION: two prices in two currencies have two figures and no common one, and a rate would be the invented estimate the requirement names with a feed attached. A VALUE JUDGEMENT: there is no "good value" threshold, because whether £1.20 a wear is worth it is not a question this repository can answer about somebody else's coat. A COMMA as a decimal separator: it is a decimal point in much of Europe and a thousands separator in both of this app's locales, so `1,500` means two amounts a factor of a thousand apart with nothing in the string to say which — refused, at the cost of a re-type.

features.title: Shopping check
acceptance: Outfits unlocked, personal compatibility and duplicate warning, computed against the local wardrobe offline
features.notes: DONE. THREE ANSWERS, THREE ENGINE CALLS, AND ONE SUBTRACTION. `coverage`/`applyChange` count outfits (F-048), `scoreColor` scores a colour against a person (F-026), `findDuplicates` measures how close two garments in a category are (F-049). This feature composes them and performs no colour arithmetic of its own — the same line F-045's builder holds, and the reason both stayed mobile features instead of becoming engine changes (E-008). THE THREE REFUSALS ARE AS MUCH THE FEATURE AS THE THREE ANSWERS. A type that fills no slot returns `outfits: null`, NEVER `unlocked: 0` — zero is an answer, and "your scarf adds nothing" on the authority of a nine-word vocabulary list is not that answer. No profile returns `compatibility: null` rather than a score about nobody. Neither refusal is wholesale: a scarf can still suit you, and a person with no profile can still be told they already own something almost identical, which is arguably the most useful thing this screen says. THREE MUTATIONS, EACH FAILING ITS OWN CASE. Returning `after.valid` instead of the difference failed exactly one test — and only because the fixture wardrobe ALREADY PRODUCES OUTFITS. On an empty wardrobe a total and a difference are the same number and that test would have passed against the bug it exists for, so the fixture's own properties are asserted in their own describe block before anything depends on them. Reporting zero for an unplaceable type failed exactly the refusal test; dropping the duplicate filter failed five. FIRST CONSUMER OF `scoreColor` IN THE APP, AND THAT TURNED UP E-053. Its twelve `explain.<factor>.<direction>` keys have been emitted since R3 and NONE was in either catalogue: the engine holds no catalogue by design (FR-11, ADR-0056), `messageKey` is a plain `string` on its side of the boundary, and nothing had ever checked the other end. FR-29 asks for a per-factor explanation and the engine had been producing one for two releases into a catalogue with no word for it. The guard pins the set in BOTH directions, which is what makes it safe to exclude these keys from the existing unused-key scan — they are rendered through a computed lookup, so no source literal exists for that scan to find. Proven by mutation both ways: deleting a key failed two assertions, adding an `explain.sparkle.supports` the engine never emits failed four. THE SCREEN NARROWS RATHER THAN CASTS: `t(key as MessageKey)` would compile and render a blank line, so a miss shows the raw key instead — visible and reportable. THE PLAN MISSED AN EFFECT AND THE COMPILER FOUND IT. `@irodora/optimization` was not a dependency of apps/mobile; the plan named the package five times without noticing that importing it changes a workspace manifest, which is E-032 — CI installs with --frozen-lockfile and install is step nine of seventeen, so a missing lockfile entry reads as a total build outage (it happened in F-020, 9ce0926). Recorded as a plan revision rather than quietly fixed. Two things worth keeping: it was the first real `pnpm install` in this tree, and `packages/corpus` — reached through a hand-made junction — survived it intact, which progress.md had flagged as a risk since F-092. E-017 FIRED AGAIN, nine codepoints this time (買 効 妨 照 答 有 持 先 手), regenerated to 665,020 bytes before any gate was declared. THREE FINDINGS FILED RATHER THAN LEFT UNRECORDED. F-123: the investment signal is FR-52's fourth item, used once in the PRD and defined nowhere, and the obvious implementation — a projected cost per wear — picks its denominator out of the air, so it takes an ADR first; REQUIREMENTS-COVERAGE.md's FR-52 row now names both features. F-124: `OUTFIT_MESSAGE_KEYS` are in neither catalogue and OutfitBuilder renders the raw component name in both locales; declared as an exact gap in the test rather than filtered out, so a NEW unrenderable key still fails. F-125: `offerReading` is called exactly once in the whole app, always with 'profile' — so `takeReading('wardrobe')` can only ever return null and AddGarment's Lens control is unreachable on a device. A consumer with no producer, which is F-051's lesson a second time, one boundary over. GATES RUN, all green: state (18 checks), typecheck, lint, format, test (mobile 469, up from 446), build, a11y (133), contrast (133), content, color-golden, cvd, security:keys. NOT RUN: e2e — it is in this feature's verification list and gate 7 is still pending on F-091, so nothing proves choose-a-colour, name-it, read-three-answers works as a JOURNEY, only that each step is correct in isolation. That is the fifth feature owing the same thing. NOT APPLICABLE: color-golden and cvd — every judgement is an imported call and the only arithmetic is a subtraction; perf — no budget is claimed, though `coverage` is t×r×s engine calls and the baseline is memoised per wardrobe so that changing the CANDIDATE costs only applyChange's cross-product, which is the saving F-048 exists for. DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT. A VERDICT: no "buy it" or "do not buy it". Three measurements shown with what they were measured against; turning them into one word would hide the parts that matter behind the part that does not. THE LENS PATH INTO THIS SCREEN: the criterion does not ask for it, and F-040's first attestation is still outstanding — no reading has been observed reaching the app on a device — so a third consumer of that path would be a second dead route, which is F-125. STORING THE CHECK: nothing is written, because the premise is a garment nobody has bought.

Mean DeltaE00 improves by 50 percent or more against uncalibrated on the device matrix
