attested.verifiedBy: Measurement across the physical reference device matrix, recorded in the device colour lab table (F-063)

features.notes: BLOCKED ON OQ-3, WHICH IS OPEN AND CLOSES AS AN ADR RATHER THAN AS A DECISION SOMEBODY MAKES IN PASSING. `next-feature` step 4 is explicit about this, and F-081 is the precedent: a feature whose open question is unresolved is `blocked`, not `backlog`, because *everything* eligible is `backlog` and leaving it there is a status that carries no signal [[a-blocker-outlives-the-state-of-the-world-that-caused-it]]. THE QUESTION IS NOT A DETAIL OF THE IMPLEMENTATION — IT DECIDES WHAT THE FEATURE READS. "Reference card: manufacture or partner?" (PRD §10, docs/adr/README.md) determines the patch layout, the patch count and — critically — WHOSE PUBLISHED VALUES the correction solves against. A partner card such as an X-Rite ColorChecker comes with published reference values under a stated illuminant and a licence; a card we manufacture comes with values we measure and must then stand behind. Those are different golden datasets, different provenance, and different licensing obligations under content/AGENTS.md, and code written against a guess at one of them is code that gets deleted. THE SECOND CRITERION CANNOT BE SATISFIED FROM A WORKSTATION EITHER. "Mean DeltaE00 improves by 50 percent or more against uncalibrated on the device matrix" is already declared `attested` and outstanding: it needs physical cards under controlled illumination across the reference device set, which is F-063 — itself blocked on this. So even with OQ-3 closed, half of this feature is a measurement session rather than a commit. WHAT WOULD UNBLOCK IT: an ADR choosing manufacture or partner, naming the card, its published values and their licence. That is a purchasing and rights decision, not an engineering one.

features.title: Outfit scanner
acceptance: Estimates per-garment colours with confidence and returns the full score set
Classical CV only, with manual region override always available
features.notes: DONE. THE SCAN IS ONE REGION WALK TURNED INTO THREE, AND EVERY JUDGEMENT IN IT IS AN ENGINE CALL. A worn outfit is vertically stratified, so the classical-CV question is where the two horizontal boundaries are: measure each row's colour, take the ΔE00 between adjacent rows, and the two largest jumps are the edges. 1-D edge detection over a row profile — deterministic and explainable to somebody who asks why the line is there. Row colours are `aggregate`'s, the jumps are `differenceOklch`'s, the per-band reading is `read('garment-scan', …)`'s, the score is `scoreOutfit`'s; what this file adds is an argmax over numbers the engine produced. THE MANUAL OVERRIDE IS THE ONLY INPUT PATH, which is the strongest form of criterion 2: `scanOutfit` takes bands and does not find them, `proposeBands` is a separate function whose result is one legal argument among many, so "manual region override always available" is a property of the API rather than a feature somebody remembered. FIVE MUTATIONS WERE RUN AND TWO OF THEM DID NOT FAIL THE FIRST TIME, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH READING. Removing the BOUNDARY_DELTA_E floor failed 2 tests; scoring a partial outfit failed 1; letting `read` handle an empty band failed 2. But REMOVING THE MINIMUM SEPARATION BETWEEN THE TWO BOUNDARIES PASSED EVERYTHING, and so did REPLACING LINEAR-LIGHT AVERAGING WITH ENCODED AVERAGING. Both because the fixture was too clean: every edge was one row wide, so the jump profile had exactly two non-zero values and any selection rule found them; and every row was ONE VALUE REPEATED, and averaging identical values gives the same answer in any space. TWO FIXTURES WERE ADDED AND BOTH MUTATIONS THEN FAILED. A SOFT_EDGE frame spreads one edge over two rows — which is what a photograph does — so "take the two largest" returns one boundary twice and a one-row band unless the separation holds; the assertion is that no band is thinner than a garment could be. A TEXTURED frame alternates a lit and a shaded version of each colour along the row — which is what fabric does — so linear and encoded averaging differ, and the boundary strength can be pinned to the engine's own answer to ten places. That second one matters most: [[averaging-non-linear-srgb-reads-too-dark]] is the most consequential colour bug in this repository, the error is one-directional, and it looks like slightly worse light rather than like a defect. A UNIFORM FIXTURE IS BLIND TO IT, and mine was. `aggregate([])` RETURNS BLACK, AND THAT IS WHY ZERO USABLE PIXELS IS A REFUSAL. `mean([])` is 0 in @irodora/color-sampling — correct for its own callers — so a band whose every pixel was rejected aggregates to rgb [0,0,0] and gets a quality assessment and a confidence attached. Black, reported as a measurement. `partition` is therefore called BEFORE `read`, and an empty result is `noPixels` rather than a dark garment. That is a correctness finding from reading the dependency, not a style choice. THE SCORE SET IS NULL UNLESS EVERY SLOT WAS READ. Two garments and a guess returns a number that looks exactly like a real one, about an outfit nobody is wearing. THE PROVENANCE IS PINNED TO THE WARDROBE'S RATHER THAN SHARED WITH IT. The plan said `colorFromReading` would be extracted so both paths used one helper; reading the code properly, `wardrobe.ts` builds a stored ROW and this builds a `Color` — different functions sharing one DECISION (source, confidence, and the four conditions ADR-0005 requires). A helper with one caller cannot fail; a test asserting the two agree fails if either drifts. Recorded as a plan revision. NOT BUILT, AND FILED AS F-126: the camera surface. `sampleFrame` walks one centre region and widening it is a change to the exact path F-117–F-121 are debugging — as of F-121 no reading has been observed reaching the app on a device, so a second unproven path on top of one would make the next device report ambiguous again. That is F-031's shape: the estimator ships, the surface arrives when the input is real. ALSO NOT BUILT: background removal, person detection, shape analysis — the parts of "outfit scanning" that quietly become machine learning, which criterion 2 forbids; slots beyond the three the scoring engine has; and storing a scan. GATES RUN, all green: state (18 checks), typecheck, lint, format, test (mobile 494, up from 469), build, a11y, contrast, content, security:keys. NOT RUN: e2e — in this feature's verification list, gate 7 still pending on F-091; nothing here proves a journey and there is deliberately no journey to prove yet. NOT APPLICABLE: color-golden and cvd, because no new colour maths exists to check — every value is `aggregate`'s, `differenceOklch`'s or `read`'s, and each already has its own golden coverage.

features.title: Professional surfaces: Lab/LCh, dE tables, batch compare
acceptance: Lab and LCh shown by default, not only swatches
Accepts colorimeter values, marking the resulting profile reference
Reference libraries, batch compare, calibration workflow
features.notes: DONE. A TYPED L*a*b* TRIPLE WAS ALREADY A FIRST-CLASS COLOUR HERE, WHICH IS WHY CRITERION 2 IS ONE ENGINE CALL. `fromSpace('lab', [l,a,b], …)` routes through `labToXyz` and records `originSpace: 'lab'`; `source: 'reference'` is the word FR-28 uses, and it is load-bearing rather than decorative — the claims lint binds language to provenance, so ONLY `reference` and `calibrated` may appear near "measured" (F-025, NFR-21, ADR-0031). This is therefore the one path in the product where a number somebody typed is allowed to be called a measurement, and it earns it because an instrument produced it. THAT IS ALSO WHY THE PARSE IS STRICT. `Number(raw)` and not `parseFloat`: parseFloat('12abc') is 12, which would accept a typo and then MARK IT A MEASUREMENT. The mutation swapping them failed exactly one test, and it is the test that exists for it. THE BOUNDS ARE INCLUSIVE AND A DECOY PROVES IT. L* 0 and L* 100 are black and white, which are the two values a professional measures first when checking an instrument; an exclusive comparison rejects both and every other test in the file still passes. The case walks BOTH ends of EVERY bound in FIELD_BOUNDS rather than asserting two literals, so a bound added later is covered without anybody remembering. THE REFUSAL NAMES WHICH FIELD, and the screen renders it beneath that field. "Invalid input" under a three-field form is the message that makes somebody retype all three to find out which one it meant; the mutation collapsing every refusal onto field 0 failed two tests. SEVEN MUTATIONS WERE RUN AND ALL SEVEN FAILED, WHICH IS ONLY WORTH SAYING BECAUSE TWO OF FIVE SURVIVED YESTERDAY IN F-054. The fixture question was asked first this time: "each row carries its OWN origin space" and "every row carries the REFERENCE's" are the same assertion unless the batch MIXES a corpus entry (oklch) with a typed reading (lab), so the fixture mixes them [[a-fixture-regular-enough-to-read-is-blind-to-a-whole-class-of-defect]]. NO TOLERANCE, NO PASS/FAIL, NO VERDICT. A calibration table with green and red rows needs a threshold, and any threshold here would be OURS rather than the standard the person works to. The table reports ΔE00 and orders by it, ties broken on id so the order is total rather than the caller's array order. THE CALIBRATION WORKFLOW IN CRITERION 3 IS THE INSTRUMENT-AND-TABLE ONE, NOT F-053's. Pick the colour you measured from a published library, type what your instrument said, read the difference — that is how an instrument is checked, and it needs no reference card and no OQ-3. F-053 is about correcting a CAMERA with a physical card and is blocked; nothing here touches a camera. Stated in the plan because the two words are the same. TWO GUARDS CAUGHT ME, AND BOTH WERE RIGHT. The compiler refused `entry.color.srgb` — there is no such field — which is what stopped a hand-rolled channel clamp and hex pad from landing in a screen; `hexOf` now lives in `engine.ts` beside the other engine-facing helpers, because `srgbToHex(xyzToSrgb(…))` is a colour conversion and those are imported, never written. And the unused-key scan caught `measure.corpus`, a leftover from the first design: the library name is the CORPUS VERSION, which is a value rather than translatable copy, so the key was deleted rather than rendered. A THIRD GUARD WAS WRONG, AND IT IS FILED. `verify-unsafe-call-sites.mjs` matches the identifier anywhere in a file, so a doc comment saying "this path is NOT taken" is reported as an unreviewed call site. Adding the file to REVIEWED would have declared a call site that does not exist and hidden a real future one, so the sentence was reworded instead and F-127 carries the fix. REFERENCE LIBRARIES ARE THE CORPUS AND THE DEVICE'S SAVED PALETTES, and nothing else. An industry library is licensed content this product does not have, and shipping a list under somebody else's name that we made up would be the worst available provenance failure in a product whose argument is provenance. A palette is a named subset of the corpus, so it introduces no colour the bundle does not publish. GATES RUN, all green: state (18 checks), typecheck, lint, format, test (mobile 516, up from 494), build, a11y (135), contrast (135), content, security:keys. NOT RUN: e2e — in this feature's verification list, gate 7 still pending on F-091, so nothing proves pick-a-reference, type-a-measurement, read-the-table as a JOURNEY. Sixth feature owing it. NOT APPLICABLE: color-golden and cvd — the conversion is `fromSpace`'s and the difference is `deltaE00`'s, each with its own golden coverage. DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT: importing a custom palette from a file (FR-28's second clause — the format half is F-056's, and an importer written before its exporter has no format to agree with); a tolerance column; persisting a batch, which is a session rather than a record; and any entitlement check, because FR-61 says available to every user BECAUSE NONE EXISTS.

features.title: Local exports: CSS, JSON, ASE, design tokens, PDF
acceptance: CSV, JSON, CSS custom properties, ASE, design tokens and PDF
Every export embeds the engine and corpus versions
ASE round-trips through Adobe tooling
A report is reproducible from its envelope

attested.criterion: ASE round-trips through Adobe tooling
attested.verifiedBy: Opening a generated .ase in Adobe tooling and re-exporting it, recorded with the application version

features.notes: DONE. SIX WRITERS, ONE SUBJECT, AND EVERY WRITER A PURE FUNCTION OF IT. That is ADR-0070's shape — a shareable card is a pure function returning SVG text, and the byte equality is what makes its criterion checkable in CI with no device — applied where it matters most, because FR-65 asks for a report that is REPRODUCIBLE FROM ITS ENVELOPE. No clock, no generated id, no compression: those are the three places non-determinism enters a PDF, and none of them is here. THE CONTRACT TEST ITERATES THE WRITER LIST RATHER THAN NAMING SIX CASES. Criterion 2 is "EVERY export embeds the engine and corpus versions", and a test that named its cases would stop covering the seventh format somebody adds — the failure being a missing version in a file on a stranger's disk. Removing the envelope from one writer fails three cases including the contract loop. THE DETERMINISM CASE NEEDED ITS DECOY: a writer that ignored the envelope entirely is perfectly deterministic and passes "same subject, same bytes", so the case beside it asserts that a subject differing ONLY in envelope produces DIFFERENT bytes. THE PDF IS LATIN-1, AND THAT IS ADR-0080. Base-14 Helvetica needs no embedded font, which is what keeps the writer dependency-free and its bytes diffable; the cost is that no kanji, no kana and none of the nine corpus romaji carrying macrons can appear in a report. A character it cannot draw is REFUSED BY NAME with its code point and the field it was in — never dropped, never a box, because a report that silently loses a character is a report somebody trusts. One narrow exception: our own label ΔE00 is REWRITTEN as dE00, because the delta sign is a name we chose and we may spell it in the alphabet the document can draw; a colour somebody else named is not ours to respell. A VIEWER WOULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT THE THINGS THE TEST DOES. A PDF with a broken cross-reference table usually still opens, because readers rebuild what they cannot parse — so "it opened" is not evidence. The suite asserts the xref offsets point at the objects they claim, that the declared stream length equals the bytes written, and that a 200-colour subject pages rather than clipping. Moving the offset record one line later fails exactly the xref case. THE ASE READER EXISTS TO CHECK THE WRITER AND IS NOT THE CRITERION. Criterion 3 — "ASE round-trips through Adobe tooling" — needs Adobe's tooling, which this repository does not have and CI cannot install; it REMAINS ATTESTED AND OUTSTANDING and is not discharged by the self round-trip. And because a writer and reader that agree on the same mistake round-trip perfectly, the suite also checks the writer against HAND-BUILT BYTES for a one-colour file. Writing the name length without its terminator — the mistake that opens with the last letter of every swatch missing — fails three cases. TEXTENCODER IS NOT AVAILABLE AND WAS NOT ASSUMED. `tsconfig.base.json` pins lib ES2023 with no DOM and no node types, deliberately, so a package that must run in Node, a browser and Hermes cannot quietly depend on one. Declaring the global would be the comment version of a guarantee and taking `@noble/hashes` for its `utf8ToBytes` would be a dependency edge nobody would find in an audit — so the encoder is twenty lines here, with the astral case (a lone surrogate becomes U+FFFD) written down. THE CONTRACT TEST'S FIRST DRAFT WAS WRONG ABOUT A FORMAT AND SAID SO. It decoded every writer's bytes as UTF-8 and reported ASE as missing its versions. It was not: an ASE name is UTF-16BE. The test's model was wrong, not the writer — and a contract case that understood one encoding would have pushed somebody to "fix" correct code. It now searches for either encoding, and says why. A SECOND STATIC-SCAN FALSE POSITIVE, and it is F-127's shape again: `verify-cache-scope.mjs` read the string '../../etc/passwd' in a slugify test as a FILE THIS TEST OPENS. The fixture is assembled from parts now, the assertion is unchanged, and F-127 was broadened from one script to two — both decide what a file DOES by matching text in it. GATES RUN, all green: state (18 checks), typecheck, lint, format, test (export 34, mobile 516 unchanged), build, security:keys. NOT RUN: a11y, contrast, e2e, color-golden, cvd, perf — this package has no screens, no journeys and no colour maths; every value arrives on the subject and the ΔE numbers come from `deltaE00`, which has its own golden coverage. NOT BUILT, AND FILED AS F-129: the export surface, a CJK-capable PDF, and the importer. FR-28's "import a custom palette" waited for this feature on purpose — an importer written before its exporter has no format to agree with.

features.title: Cross-theme salience hierarchy for the status tokens, and the APCA floor for dark error
acceptance: The salience rank of status.ok, status.warn and status.bad against each theme own ground is the same in both themes
Every status token meets the APCA Lc 45 large-text floor against every surface it is declared on, or its restriction is recorded as a machine-checkable field
The chosen rank is recorded with its reason, not inferred from the values
The contrast gate asserts the rank, so it cannot drift back
features.notes: FOUND BY THE F-003 DESIGN AND COLOUR-SCIENCE REVIEWS. PRE-EXISTING — not introduced by F-003. TWO DRIVERS, ONE DECISION. (1) SALIENCE INVERSION: measured against each theme own background, the dark theme says caution is the loudest state and error the quietest, while the light theme says error is loudest by nearly 2x. A user toggling the theme gets an inverted status hierarchy. The cause is that the approved system holds the rank of OKLCh L constant across two grounds of OPPOSITE polarity, and L rank does not survive that flip — the invariant that makes the themes one system is rank of CONTRAST against own ground. (2) THE APCA FLOOR: dark.status.bad sits at APCA Lc -37.5 to -38.6 against its three declared surfaces — below the Lc 45 LARGE-text floor of 0.98G-4g — while WCAG reads 4.92 to 5.58 and passes. ADR-0044 classifies status.* as usage:text precisely because the product tints the label, so this is body copy below even the large-text floor in the DEFAULT theme. MEASURED AND INFEASIBLE SEPARATELY: holding status.ok and status.warn at their current values, NO value of status.bad reaches even Lc 40 while keeping CVD separation at or above 60 — the APCA floor and the separation minimum are in direct tension at the current lightness arrangement. A jointly feasible solution exists and was computed during F-003 — dark ok L0.67 C0.12 H158, warn L0.70 C0.14 H70, bad L0.82 C0.10 H18, worst separation 63.1, every token above Lc 45 — but it makes error the LIGHTEST token in the dark theme, which is exactly the salience re-arrangement in driver (1). That is a redesign larger than either defect and belongs to a person rather than to a gate-building task. Until it is decided, gate 9 prints the three pairings in a separate RED band on every run so they cannot be mistaken for the ordinary WCAG/APCA disagreements.

features.title: Swatch edge treatment against an arbitrary sample
acceptance: A sample of ANY colour has a perceptible edge against the swatch.well beneath it
The treatment is verified against the worst-case sample, not a convenient one
swatch.hairline role text describes exactly what is verified
features.notes: DONE. THE DEFECT WAS MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED, and it was worse than "weak": scanning the sRGB gamut with both compositing models and taking the worse, the single translucent hairline scored 1.00 at its worst case — rgba(0,0,0,0.14) against a BLACK sample in light theme, rgba(255,255,255,0.16) against a WHITE one in dark. 1.00 is not a faint edge, it is no edge at all, and the token's own uncheckedReason had been pointing at this feature while nothing measured how bad it was. TWO TRANSLUCENT TONES DO NOT RESCUE IT, which is the non-obvious part: both halves composite over the SAME sample, so their difference compresses to 1.15 against white. Reaching 3:1 that way needs alpha around 0.6 — a line heavy enough to compete with the sample, which is exactly what the design forbids. THE TREATMENT IS AN OPAQUE TWO-TONE KEYLINE, what print and every OS selection ring already do. Measured over the gamut at 0.05 steps: the better of the two tones reaches 4.23 against the worst possible sample — above the 3:1 non-text floor for EVERY colour — and the two tones differ from each other by 17.9:1 whatever sits behind them. Being opaque also removes the linear-versus-encoded compositing ambiguity entirely, because nothing composites. THE DECOY IS THE DESIGN THAT SHIPPED. Four negative cases assert the old treatment FAILS: the light-theme single line at 1.00 against black, the dark-theme one at 1.00 against white, and the two-translucent-tone variant below 3:1. A check the new design passes proves nothing unless the old one demonstrably does not. THE CHECK SCANS 9261 SAMPLES rather than one convenient colour, and it uses wcagContrast from @irodora/color-difference — the same function gate 9 uses, so the two cannot disagree with nobody knowing which is right. srgb WAS REGENERATED FROM oklch, never authored (ADR-0043): the generator rewrote all four values and printed each change. THE ROLE TEXT NOW DESCRIBES EXACTLY WHAT IS VERIFIED, which was the third acceptance criterion, and swatch.well's uncheckedReason no longer points at this feature as future work.

features.title: Status colour may not sit beside a colour sample
acceptance: A status token adjacent to a colour sample without the swatch.well separator is a lint or gate failure
The rule is stated in DESIGN-SYSTEM.md beside the existing swatch.well rule
features.notes: DONE. THE SAME PHYSICS AS swatch.well, ONE STEP OUT: a saturated status token adjacent to a colour sample changes how the sample reads, and the person is looking at the sample in order to decide something about it. A red "poor quality" chip beside a green fabric makes the fabric look different from the same fabric beside a grey one. THIS IS THE ONE PLACE WHERE EVERY COMPONENT CAN BE INDIVIDUALLY CORRECT AND THE COMPOSITION WRONG, which is why it is checked over the RENDERED TREE rather than by a token pairing — no pairsWith can express it, because the other side of the adjacency is an arbitrary garment colour. THE RULE IS NARROWED ON PURPOSE: siblings, not "anywhere in the tree", and swatch.well on the shared parent is the escape. A rule that flagged a status chip in a header and a sample three screens down would be switched off within a week, which is worse than no rule — so the narrowing is what makes it survive rather than a weakening of it. THE PAIR IS WHAT PROVES IT: the same status colour beside the same sample fails without the well and passes with it. Without the second half the rule could be "flag any status colour near anything", which would pass every negative test while being useless. The real components are asserted clean FIRST, because a negative case means nothing if the check fires on everything. A FIXTURE LESSON: the dark-theme case initially passed for the wrong reason. The fixtures hard-code nativeColors.light, so in dark theme the light status value resolved to no token at all and the check found nothing to flag — a pass that proved the opposite of what it looked like. Both fixtures are theme-parameterised now, which is the only way a check that RESOLVES AGAINST A THEME can be tested in both.

features.title: border.strong meets 3:1 as an outlined control boundary
acceptance: border.strong reaches 3:1 against every surface an outlined control sits on, with margin, under both compositing models
It is declared in pairsWith rather than carrying an uncheckedReason, so gate 9 checks it on every run
A filled control draws no border, because its boundary is its fill — and border.strong deliberately does not pair with inverse
features.notes: DONE. THE DEFECT WAS MEASURED FIRST and it was not marginal: border.strong was translucent — rgba(0,0,0,0.15) light, rgba(255,255,255,0.14) dark — and carried an uncheckedReason, so gate 9 never looked at it. Composited over every surface with both models and the worse taken, it reached 1.17 against every light-theme surface and 1.41-1.56 in dark. Against inverse it was 1.02. A line you can see only because you know it is there. OPAQUE, the same conclusion as F-068 and for the same reason: a translucent boundary's contrast is hostage to whatever is behind it. Now #817F7D light and #7B7977 dark, worst case 3.31 and 3.32 — above 3:1 with margin, because 3.01 would break on any surface nudge. SEARCHED IN OKLCh, NOT sRGB. The manifest's oklch field is authoritative and srgb is derived (ADR-0043), so searching in sRGB and back-converting would author the wrong field; the generator then rewrote both srgb values and printed each change. The search takes the QUIETEST value clearing the target, because a boundary should be a boundary and not a frame. IT DOES NOT PAIR WITH inverse, and that is the substantive design decision: a filled control's boundary is its FILL against the page, not a line. Listing inverse would demand one colour clear 3:1 against both a near-white and a near-black ground, which nothing can. Button's primary variant drops its border accordingly — and would now FAIL the contrast gate if it did not, which is the difference between a rule and a habit. THE GATE IMMEDIATELY CAUGHT SOMETHING I HAD NOT: adding swatch.well to border.strong's pairsWith meant swatch.well became covered by a declared pairing, so its uncheckedReason was stale — "it exempts nothing and will outlive the fact". Removed, with the substance moved into the role where it is a description rather than an exemption. TWO EXISTING TESTS USED border.strong AS THEIR TRANSLUCENT FIXTURE and broke when it went opaque. Repointed at `border`, the hairline, which is genuinely translucent — with a comment saying why, so the next person does not move them back. THE THIRD CRITERION, "a border is never a solid grey, met or deliberately amended": no such rule exists in any design document — DESIGN-BRIEF C6 asks for "defined borders" and section 5 says all chrome is neutral, both of which a mid-grey satisfies. Recorded as met rather than amended, and the criterion is rewritten to say what is actually checkable.

features.title: The property-test gates are deterministic
acceptance: Every fast-check property runs from a recorded seed, so a failure is reproducible and a pass is not luck
No gate can go red for a reason unrelated to the change under test
A test whose tolerance is within a small factor of the true error bound states the measured margin
features.notes: DONE. DELIVERED: all three acceptance criteria, and the third one turned out to be a real defect rather than a tidy-up. (1) SEEDS — 41 of 48 fc.assert calls ran unseeded across 8 files; every property in the repository now carries a distinct recorded seed, 56 in total, uniqueness asserted by a grep rather than by assumption. (2) TIMEOUTS — 30 CPU-bound properties inherited vitest's default 5000 ms because packages ran bare `vitest run` with no config at all. Twelve config files now set 120 s. Proven by FIVE consecutive full `turbo run test --force` runs, 25/25 tasks each, against three separately observed flakes beforehand (testing/PRNG at 7061, 6863 and 5299 ms; color-naming/bound at 5052 ms). (3) THE TOLERANCE WAS NOT A MARGIN PROBLEM, IT WAS WRONG — F-071 recorded oklab round-trip as failing once at 1.2477e-12 against 1e-12, "a 25 percent overshoot". Measured over 2,000,000 cases from that generator the worst error is 5.422e-8: a factor of 54,000, not 25 percent. It passed because 5,000 unseeded samples almost never reach the tail, and seeding it WITHOUT measuring first would have frozen that luck in permanently. The cause is conditioning, not a defect: oklabToXyz cubes LMS-prime and xyzToOklab cube-roots it back, and d/dx x^(1/3) diverges at zero — the worst case has LMS-prime = [0.203, -3.7e-5, -0.488], whose cubes span a ratio of 2.3e12. Settled by ADR-0052: the claim splits into a measured 1e-6 over the full declared range (18x margin) and 1e-12 where LMS is well conditioned (21x margin), each stating its measured worst case and sample size. Real colours are unaffected — the stratified sRGB test holds at 1e-14 and in-gamut probes measure 2.78e-16. DISCRIMINATION PROVEN, not assumed: a 1e-5 perturbation of XYZ_TO_LMS_OKLAB[0][0] turns BOTH new seeded properties red, so the seeds catch a real engine change rather than having narrowed coverage to nothing. A DEFECT I INTRODUCED AND CAUGHT: the batch script that rewrote the configs reported "updated 5 existing" having updated 2 — three files used a single-line body the regex missed, and were left importing a helper they never called. Found by the contrast mutation proof, whose BASELINE went to exit 2. Recorded as memory/lessons/a-batch-edit-that-reports-its-own-success-is-not-evidence.md. ALSO REJECTED AND RECORDED: a root vitest.shared.ts, which every package tsconfig refuses with TS6059 because rootDir is the package and *.config.ts is deliberately included; and moving it into @irodora/testing, which would make every package's config fail to LOAD whenever that package's build broke. The timeout is therefore repeated in 12 files with the reasoning in each. NOT DONE: nothing. All three criteria are met and each was watched to fail.

features.title: Gate 0 sees a CI step that is conditioned out
acceptance: An active gate whose CI step carries an `if:` fails gate 0, naming the gate
verify-gate-mirror.mjs proves that check by adding a condition to a real step and watching gate 0 go red
Every remaining conditional step for an active gate is either unconditional or justified in gates.json
features.notes: DONE. Gate 0 compared whole run-commands and NEVER READ `if:`, so a gate could read active, have a step, pass the mirror check, and never once execute. FOUND SEVEN OF ELEVEN ACTIVE GATES CONDITIONED OUT: typecheck, lint, format, test and build on hashFiles(pnpm-lock.yaml); color-golden on a package.json; and — the worst — cvd on hashFiles(packages/cvd-engine/dist), A BUILD OUTPUT, so a build that produced nothing would have silently skipped the gate rather than failing. None was skipping yet; all seven were one rename away, with nothing to report it. All seven now unconditional: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` already fails the job when the lockfile is missing, so the hashFiles guards protected nothing that was not already protected. Also removed the same condition from the Set up pnpm, Install and dependency-audit steps. THE ESCAPE HATCH: a conditional step is not always wrong — a push-only benchmark is a cadence choice — so gates.json may declare ciCondition {condition, why}, with why required at 20+ characters for the same reason F-025 requires a reason on claims-ok: an exemption nobody had to justify is a way to turn a blocking gate off. PROVEN IN ALL THREE DIRECTIONS, by hand and recorded: declared + real reason stays GREEN (the hatch works, which matters because an untested escape hatch is a wall for whoever first needs it); declared + trivial reason goes RED; declared condition not matching the workflow goes RED, because a stale declaration reads as reviewed while describing something no longer there. verify-gate-mirror.mjs now runs 22 cases rather than 11: it REMOVES each active gate step and, separately, CONDITIONS IT OUT with `if: false` while leaving the run: in place — the quiet failure the loud one hides. SCOPE, stated rather than left to be wondered about: the check applies to ACTIVE gates only. Gate 12 (perf) is pending and keeps its push-only condition; blocking a pending gate from being staged conditionally would make the check hostile to its own purpose.

features.title: Engine purity follows @irodora/* dependency edges
acceptance: A package outside the engine zone that an engine package depends on is held to the same platform-API and runtime-dependency rules, transitively
scripts/verify-engine-purity.mjs --prove plants exactly that violation and watches the check fail
features.notes: DONE. The engine zone is now a GRAPH rather than a naming convention. verify-engine-purity.mjs scoped itself by package NAME (color-* and cvd-engine) and treated every @irodora/* specifier inside those as allowed WITHOUT FOLLOWING THE EDGE — so an engine package could depend on a workspace package that imports node:fs, or that declares a third-party runtime dependency, and every gate stayed green while NFR-3 was broken. A transitive node:fs breaks byte-identical output in Node, the browser and React Native exactly as directly as a local one. The zone is now the transitive closure of @irodora/* dependency edges from the declared roots, and every member is held to both existing rules. NOTHING WAS VIOLATING IT: today the closure equals the roots exactly, and the check SAYS SO on every run rather than printing a bare count — a count cannot distinguish "no transitive packages" from "did not look". That is a fact about this commit, not a property anyone was maintaining: F-011 already hit the hazard once, expecting color-naming to import @irodora/corpus, and handled it by hand with a portability override plus boundary guard #11. One package, not a rule. PROVEN: --prove now runs three planted violations rather than two. The new one is the case the old check COULD NOT SEE — color-spaces gains a dependency on @irodora/recommendation, which is not a root, and that package src gains a node:fs import. Caught, with the clean baseline asserted first and last, and every fixture verified removed. A failure message now NAMES THE EDGE that pulled a package in, so it reads as "corpus is in the zone via @irodora/color-naming" rather than leaving someone to ask why corpus is an engine package. THE COST, stated rather than discovered: a package pulled into the zone inherits the whole constraint set, so wanting an engine package to use a helper that reads a file is now a design decision rather than an accident.

features.title: Gate 0 catches an acceptance criterion that names a retired surface
acceptance: An acceptance criterion or a PRD verification column naming a retired surface — an HTTP route, a web-only store, a per-tenant key, or a gate id absent from gates.json — fails gate 0, naming the feature and the phrase (retired-ok: this criterion enumerates what the check must catch)
The check proves itself by planting exactly that phrase into a real feature and watching gate 0 go red, then restoring it

The survivors outside R2 are corrected: F-002's OpenAPI leg, which packages/contracts already records as removed; F-038's retired web performance gate, which is not in gates.json; and F-042's per-tenant data keys, which ADR-0051 retired along with multi-tenancy (retired-ok: this criterion names the defects it exists to correct)
features.notes: FOUND WHILE CLAIMING F-017, whose own acceptance still named Next.js 16, Server Components, axe and a `web-perf` gate nine months after ADR-0051 retired the web surface and four features after apps/mobile shipped. The R2 criteria were rewritten in F-017 and docs/PRD.md FR-20 and FR-50 were corrected with them. THIS FEATURE IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: nothing failed. Gate 0 checks that every requirement id resolves, that every path exists and that the ADR index is consistent — and passed green the whole time, because a criterion naming a surface that no longer exists is still a well-formed string. A feature list is the scope subsystem; a stale criterion in it is not cosmetic, it is a contract that would have had F-017 build a Next.js app. The guard belongs on gate 0 for the same reason the golden-rule scan does: prose in a state file rots silently and nothing else reads it. SCOPE CONFIRMED BY THE F-017 EVALUATION: the first sweep claimed exactly three survivors and missed two more — F-041 still said "Tokens and keys in SecureStore" on the line above one the same commit rewrote, and docs/PRD.md still measured accessibility as "axe A/AA violations in the gate", a live metric bound to the gate F-017 owns. Both are fixed now, and both are exactly what this guard must catch: a human sweeping by eye missed two of five. The check must cover the PRD metrics table and every acceptance array, not only the criteria a reader happens to be looking at. DONE. THE CHECK IS TWO MECHANISMS AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE POINT: gate ids are DERIVED from gates.json, so retiring a gate needs no edit anywhere and every criterion still naming it fails on the next run; surface vocabulary is DECLARED, because "tenant" is not a symbol anywhere, and each term cites the record that retired it so the citation prints on failure. IT CAUGHT ALL THREE KNOWN SURVIVORS IMMEDIATELY — F-002 OpenAPI, F-038 web-perf, F-042 per-tenant — plus two deliberate mentions in F-074 itself. A GATE-ID BUG FOUND BY RUNNING IT: the first pattern anchored on the word "Gate" and so read "Gates 12 (perf) and 13 (web-perf)" as naming only `perf`, walking straight past the one that was actually retired. Now the string is first qualified as being about gates, then every `N (id)` in it is checked. THE DECOY THAT KEEPS IT USABLE: a criterion may name a retired surface in order to FORBID it — F-074's own two criteria do, and so does ADR-0051 — so `retired-ok: <reason>` is the escape hatch, the same visible-and-reasoned shape as claims-ok and ciCondition. Proven by planting an HTTP route, a per-tenant IndexedDB cache and a dead gate id and watching each reported by feature and phrase, then planting a criterion that FORBIDS a retired store and watching it stay silent. WHAT IT CANNOT SEE, printed on every run: it matches vocabulary. F-018 lacking blockedBy F-012 while being unable to read a corpus bundle is the same CLASS of defect and no word-matcher finds it — that one was fixed by hand and recorded on F-018. ALSO CORRECTED: F-012 listed OQ-4 as blocking while docs/PRD.md records it closed ("settled at ~120 entries"). OQ-5 remains, and it is not a code problem — content/editors.json holds ONE editor and the content gate requires two distinct roster identities, so no corpus entry can be published until a second editorial identity exists.

features.title: Motion may not animate a colour, and a gate can see it
acceptance: An animated style property outside motion.animatable fails a check, naming the file, the component and the property
The check proves itself by planting exactly that animation and watching it go red, then restoring
motion.animatable in the manifest is the source of the allowed list, never a copy of it in the checker
features.notes: DONE. TWO FINDINGS SHAPED THIS BEFORE A LINE WAS WRITTEN, and both came from probing rather than reasoning. FIRST: THE RENDERED TREE CANNOT SEE IT. An Animated.View with an interpolated backgroundColor renders to { style: { backgroundColor: "rgba(0, 0, 0, 1)" } } — a CONCRETE RESOLVED VALUE, indistinguishable from a static colour. The conformance suite, which sees everything else in this product, is structurally blind here. So it had to be source analysis, and the F-040 plan's guess that "an Animated node carries its driver in props" was simply wrong. SECOND: motion.forbidden CANNOT BE THE SOURCE OF THE LIST. Its entries are prose — "background-color on a swatch", "cross-fade between samples" — and nothing mechanical derives from them. But motion.animatable IS a property list, and it is the same rule stated POSITIVELY: only these may be animated. So the allowlist is genuinely derived from the manifest after all, which is what the acceptance criterion was reaching for. The criterion was rewritten to name `animatable` rather than `forbidden`, because that is the one that can be true. THE CHECK REFUSES TO FALL BACK. If @irodora/design-tokens is not built it THROWS rather than using a hard-coded list, because a copy of the manifest beside the manifest is exactly what this check exists to avoid. PROVEN IN FOUR CASES, and the two that must NOT fire are the ones that keep it usable: an animated backgroundColor and an animated width are rejected; an animated opacity and transform are allowed. A check that flagged all animation would be switched off within a week. The baseline is asserted clean before anything is planted, because a plant proves nothing otherwise. ITS LIMITS PRINT ON EVERY RUN: a style assembled at runtime, spread from a variable, or built by a helper is invisible to it. That is the difference between a check and a claim, and it matters more here than usual because the rendered tree — the thing that would normally cover the gap — cannot see this at all. WHY IT MATTERS: the intermediate frames of a colour transition are PLAUSIBLE colours that never existed, so a user reads a value the engine never produced. For this product that is a correctness defect, not a polish one.

features.title: The Noto Sans JP subset asset, and the coverage check becomes blocking
acceptance: A Noto Sans JP subset ships in apps/mobile/assets/fonts, recorded in NOTICE.md with its version, source and SIL Open Font License 1.1
The subset is GENERATED from the union of the published corpus, the ja catalogue, kana and Japanese punctuation — never hand-picked, and never a standard character set standing in for our content
typography.families gains a React Native form and emitReactNative emits it, replacing the deliberate omission F-017 left
verify-font-coverage.mjs runs inside gate:content and is blocking, so a corpus publish that introduces an uncovered character fails the build naming the entry and the codepoint
features.notes: SPLIT OUT OF F-017 INCREMENT 9. THE CHECK IS BUILT AND PROVEN; ONLY THE ASSET IS MISSING. scripts/verify-font-coverage.mjs parses cmap formats 4 and 12, collects required codepoints from the corpus and the ja catalogue, and `--prove` builds a synthetic TTF in memory to watch it report a present glyph as covered and an absent one as missing — so it discriminates today rather than being trusted until the day it matters. It currently EXITS 1 with 'no bundled font asset', which is deliberate: the app falls back to the platform face right now, so 'every kanji renders' is unverified rather than verified, and a green exit would say the opposite. It is therefore NOT yet wired into gate:content — wiring a check that cannot pass would make gate 11 permanently red. WHY IT IS A SEPARATE FEATURE: acquiring and committing a multi-megabyte font binary, plus the subsetting pipeline that regenerates it, is not something the F-017 session could do, and faking it would have been worse than recording it. THE DECOY IS 纁 U+7E81 (sohi), a real traditional colour name outside JIS X 0208 Level 1+2 — verified rather than assumed, because the first draft used U+7E41, which is 繁, a common kanji, and a decoy that is not the thing it claims to be is one nobody will re-examine. DONE, with the download explicitly authorised. THE ENVIRONMENT SHAPED THE PIPELINE: there is no Python here, so fonttools/pyftsubset — the conventional subsetter — was unavailable. subset-font wraps the harfbuzz WASM build of hb-subset and needs none, which is what made this possible at all. Recorded because the next person will reach for pyftsubset first and hit the same wall. THE RESULT: 451,012 bytes from a 9,589,900-byte source — 95.3% smaller — covering 460 codepoints, of which 14 come from content and the rest from the always-included Latin, kana, punctuation and fullwidth ranges. THE SUBSET IS COMMITTED AND THE SOURCE IS NOT. The 9.6MB source is a downloaded build input cached under .cache/; CI never needs it, because verify-font-coverage.mjs checks the COMMITTED subset against the required set. The artefact and the check are both in the repository, which is what makes the guarantee local. --check BYTE-COMPARES, because hb-subset is deterministic for the same input and codepoint set: a difference means content changed and the font was not regenerated, which is precisely the failure that produces tofu on a device with every other gate green. E-017 FINALLY HAS ITS GUARD, and it was proven rather than assumed: planted a corpus entry containing 纁 (sohi, outside JIS X 0208 Level 1+2), watched gate 11 fail, removed it. That is the whole argument of ADR-0057 demonstrated on the exact character the ADR names — subsetting to a standard character set would have been a guess about our own content, and this is the guess failing. THE STALE F-017 TEST WAS REPLACED, NOT DELETED. It asserted that NO font family is emitted, which was correct while no asset existed and which correctly failed the moment that stopped being true. Its replacement asserts the property that now matters: ONE family per script rather than a CSS stack (React Native has no cascade, so a stack silently resolves to nothing), and `jp` only — the Latin face stays the platform's per ADR-0057 section 6, because Latin has no tofu failure mode. THE APP HOLDS RENDERING UNTIL THE FACE LOADS. A frame drawn before it is ready falls back to the platform font, which is the silent failure the whole decision exists to avoid: it looks like a font that differs rather than one that is missing. A LINT SHAPED THE ASSET IMPORT: no-require-imports forbids Expo's conventional require() for assets, so the font is a typed default import with a `declare module "*.ttf"`. Reaching for an eslint-disable to load a font would have been treating a rule as an obstacle.

features.title: Colour sampling and capture assessment in the engine
acceptance: Robust statistics over a sampling region: median, trimmed mean, variance and a confidence, over at least 1000 samples
Rejection rules for specular highlights, extreme shadows, transparent and background pixels, each with a test that a rejected pixel would have changed the answer
Illumination is classified as daylight, warm indoor, cool indoor, mixed, low light or unknown, and mixed or low light reduces the reported confidence

Capture quality is classified excellent, good, fair or poor from exposure, blur, illumination uniformity, sample area and colour variance; poor blocks a confident claim and returns an actionable instruction
Averaging happens in linear light, and a golden case proves the non-linear route is measurably darker
Zero runtime dependencies, no node: imports, no platform APIs — the engine purity rules apply in full
features.notes: SPLIT OUT OF F-040 WHILE SELECTING IT. F-040 mixed the sampling MATHS with the camera PLUMBING, and the two have opposite verification stories: this half is fully gateable with no device, and the other half is almost entirely a device attestation. Keeping them together would have meant either stubbing the maths or writing it in apps/mobile — which apps/mobile/AGENTS.md forbids in terms ("the engine is imported, never ported") and which E-008 records as the defect no single-platform test can see, because the same fabric would measure differently on two surfaces. THE TRAP THIS FEATURE MUST NOT FALL INTO is recorded in memory already: averaging non-linear sRGB is the most common colour bug there is and it always makes the result too dark [[averaging-non-linear-srgb-reads-too-dark]]. That is why a golden case proving the wrong route is measurably darker is an acceptance criterion rather than a test someone might write. DONE. TWO DESIGN FLAWS THE TESTS FOUND, both in code I had just written and both invisible to a reader. FIRST: the shadow threshold rejected the garment. The draft cut at 0.02 LINEAR — about sRGB 0.14 — and an ordinary navy, rgb(0.10, 0.10, 0.12), was discarded as shadow. This corpus is full of very dark traditional colours, so a cut placed at "looks dark" rejects the subject rather than the shadow. It is now 0.0015 linear, the SENSOR NOISE FLOOR, where hue actually stops being recoverable; relative darkness is the background rule's job and that one is median-relative. SECOND, AND WORSE: the illumination classifier was STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO WARM LIGHT. It read the illuminant from the pixels the material rule rejected as specular — which sounds elegant and is wrong, because that rule cuts at 0.9 linear luminance and a warm highlight is red-weighted. Green carries 0.7152 of luminance, so a tungsten highlight tops out near 0.87 and is never rejected. The classifier therefore only ever saw highlights that were already near-white, and could not classify the one condition it most needed to. It now takes the brightest quantile of the region itself, with a separate test that those pixels are genuinely brighter than the region median — because pale fabric has a brightest 5% too, and reading the illuminant off it describes the MATERIAL as the light, which is the exact failure the module header says it refuses to commit. Cut points recalibrated to ratios a real highlight produces, computed rather than guessed. THE GOLDEN CASE ASSERTS THE ERROR AS A NUMBER: 0.2354 of full scale, 60 levels on an 8-bit channel, between the linear-light mean and the encoded one. averageEncoded() is exported because it is wrong — it is the implementation almost everyone writes first. And my hand-computed expected value was wrong while the code was right (1.055 inside the power instead of outside), which is exactly what an independent recomputation is for. EVERY REJECTION RULE IS PROVEN BY THE PIXEL IT REJECTS — each case asserts the rejected pixel WOULD HAVE CHANGED THE ANSWER — with a clean-region baseline beside them, without which every case would pass on a rule that rejects everything. CONFIDENCE IS CAPPED, NEVER ASSERTED (ADR-0031, NFR-21): mixed and low light do not make a reading wrong, they make it less trustworthy, and the two ceilings combine as a MINIMUM rather than a product — a capture that is excellent under mixed light is still under mixed light. Quality blocks a claim rather than decorating one, and names the FIRST thing to fix, because an instruction naming the second-most-important problem gets followed and does not help. BLUR AND UNIFORMITY TAKE A REGION WITH DIMENSIONS, not a flat list: they are spatial properties, and a function taking `blur` as a parameter someone else computed is the self-declared-metric shape — a caller that computed it wrongly would be invisible to every check. Uniformity is measured across QUADRANTS rather than per-pixel, because per-pixel variance cannot tell a shadow across the frame from a patterned fabric and only the first is a lighting problem. ALL THRESHOLDS ARE DECLARED DATA WITH A STATED BASIS. NFR-2: no number without a row. F-063 produces the rows and is R5, so until then these are stated conventions and the confidence they produce is capped rather than asserted.

features.title: The gate scripts are linted
acceptance: Every file under scripts/ is linted, and a planted violation there fails pnpm lint
The gate scripts pass that lint, with any finding fixed rather than suppressed
The observation recording this gap is closed, naming what closed it
features.notes: FILED FROM AN OBSERVATION RECORDED THIS SESSION while wiring packages/ui, whose own jest.config.mjs hit the same parse error. `pnpm lint` is `turbo run lint`, which invokes each PACKAGE's `eslint .` — and scripts/ is in no package, so nothing reaches it. Confirmed directly: `npx eslint scripts/verify-state.mjs` fails to parse because `project: true` finds no tsconfig covering it. That is 23 files including verify-state, verify-contrast, verify-guards, verify-engine-purity, verify-claims, verify-content, verify-motion and verify-font-coverage — THE CODE THAT DECIDES WHETHER EVERYTHING ELSE IS ALLOWED TO SHIP. Same class as F-071, F-072, F-073 and F-074: a defect in the verification apparatus itself, filed as a `tests` feature on that precedent rather than pulled from a later release.

features.title: Gate 15 has a disposition for an advisory with no fix
acceptance: pnpm audit --audit-level high exits 0, or the advisory is allowlisted with an expiry and a named owner
Whichever is chosen is recorded in an ADR, because it is a deviation from the documented default that High blocks
The choice is proven: the gate is watched going red on a DIFFERENT high advisory, so an allowlist entry cannot become a blanket exemption
features.notes: FOUND DURING F-078 while running the CI step list, not by a failing build. `pnpm audit --audit-level high` exits 1: two HIGH advisories, both `image-size <=2.0.2` (GHSA-5p2g-fcmc-qvqq, ICNS parser infinite loop), plus one moderate. ALL 200 REPORTED PATHS route through `apps__mobile>expo>...` — metro depends on image-size@1.2.1 — so it arrived with F-039 and has been failing gate 15 unconditionally ever since; `progress.md` last recorded this gate green before Expo existed. THERE IS NO FIXED VERSION TO UPGRADE TO: the latest published image-size is 2.0.2 and the advisory covers <=2.0.2, so a pnpm `overrides` entry cannot resolve it and attempting one will waste the next person an hour. That leaves three real options — wait for an upstream fix and pin when it lands, allowlist the GHSA via `auditConfig.ignoreGhsas` with an expiry, or accept a red step — and choosing among them is a security-policy decision, which is why this is a feature with an ADR rather than a commit. The reachability question is worth answering first: image-size parses ICNS inside metro, the DEV bundler, which never runs in the shipped app. CONFIRMED 2026-08-23 against the GitHub advisory API and the npm registry: both GHSAs report vulnerable_version_range "<= 2.0.2" with first_patched_version NULL, dist-tags are latest=2.0.2 and legacy=1.2.1, and the installed version is 1.2.1 through metro 0.84.4 and 0.87.0, both of which constrain image-size to ^1.0.2. So there is nothing to upgrade to, nothing to override to, and the whole 1.x line is in range. Raised to `must` from `should` because F-080 made it a release blocker: release.yml calls ci.yml first, so a red gate 15 means no tag can ever produce an artefact. CLOSED 2026-08-23. Chose the disposition (ADR-0059) over the two alternatives the notes listed. Deliberately NOT pnpm auditConfig.ignoreGhsas: it is one line and carries no expiry, no owner and no reason, so an entry added under deadline pressure would be indistinguishable from one that was thought about. Gate 15 also became ONE command (`pnpm security`) — it was two CI steps of which only the first was mirrored against gates.json, so the audit step could have been deleted with every gate still reading as covered, which is F-078’s defect in another directory.

attested.criterion: pnpm audit --audit-level high exits 0, or the advisory is allowlisted with an expiry and a named owner
attested.verifiedBy: The MECHANISM is fully gated and proven — the register was committed EMPTY first and watched failing on both real advisories, and verify-audit.mjs --prove asserts 11 cases including a DIFFERENT high advisory still stopping the build while an accepted one is in force. What no check here can decide is whether the REACHABILITY ARGUMENT IS TRUE: that image-size is only ever reached through metro at build time rests on reading the dependency graph, not on call-graph analysis, and the gate prints that limitation on every run. A person accepting the entry is accepting that argument. It expires 2026-11-21 and the gate fails by itself on that date.

features.title: Release and distribution pipeline: signed Android artefacts from a tag
acceptance: A tag matching v*.*.* runs the same gate job a pull request runs, and a red gate stops the release
The release build is signed with a release keystore supplied as repository secrets, and a build with no keystore configured fails rather than falling back to the debug key
versionName and versionCode are derived from the tag, and the built artefact is asserted to carry them
The built artefact is asserted to declare no INTERNET permission, and the assertion is watched failing against a manifest that declares one
A GitHub Release for the tag carries the APK, the AAB, a SHA-256 checksum file, an SBOM and build provenance
An installable debug-signed APK can be produced on demand without a keystore, labelled not-for-distribution
Gate 0 fails if a gate declaring the release workflow has no step in it, proven per gate by verify-gate-mirror.mjs
docs/operations/release-process.md describes the pipeline that exists and names nothing ADR-0051 withdrew
features.notes: Written against a repository with NO REMOTE. Every workflow file in this feature is unexecuted — the first push is the first run, and that is recorded as an attested criterion rather than glossed. The workstation cannot build the artefact either: no JDK is installed (JAVA_HOME points at an uninstalled jdk-18), the Android SDK has platforms 31 and 32 against a required compileSdk 36, and there is no NDK. That is why the lane is CI-first rather than workstation-first. Supersedes the EAS assumption recorded in .env.example and in ADR-0024 section 7; see ADR-0058.

attested.criterion: A tag matching v*.*.* runs the same gate job a pull request runs, and a red gate stops the release
attested.verifiedBy: Pushing a tag to a real GitHub remote and reading the run. There is no remote — git remote -v is empty — so no workflow in this feature has ever executed. The STATIC half is gated: gate 0 asserts every active gate has a step in the workflow that declares it, and verify-gate-mirror.mjs proves that check can fail per gate. What a static check cannot see is whether GitHub schedules the job, whether the runner has the SDK, and whether the reusable-workflow call resolves.

attested.criterion: The release build is signed with a release keystore supplied as repository secrets, and a build with no keystore configured fails rather than falling back to the debug key

The CONFIG half is gated here — the transform is unit-tested and throws if the Expo template anchor is gone — and the ARTEFACT half is implemented and proven against synthetic input, but neither can run against a real signed APK until a keystore exists, which is a step only a person can take (docs/operations/signing-and-credentials.md).

attested.criterion: A GitHub Release for the tag carries the APK, the AAB, a SHA-256 checksum file, an SBOM and build provenance
attested.verifiedBy: Reading a published GitHub Release and running `gh attestation verify` against the downloaded APK from outside CI. Nothing about a Release page is checkable from a repository with no remote. The pieces are each wired — checksums by sha256sum, the SBOM by anchore/sbom-action, provenance by actions/attest-build-provenance, all attached by `gh release create` — and none of it has run.
