features.title: NFR-3 as written is unachievable: V8 Math differs between Windows and Linux builds
acceptance: An ADR decides between shipping deterministic transcendentals and restating NFR-3 as identity after canonical rounding
docs/PRD.md NFR-3 says what the engine can actually guarantee, and the claims lint has nothing to flag in it
Gate 5 asserts the chosen guarantee and is watched failing on a change that violates it
The guarantee is verified on Linux and Windows, not only on the platform that generated the fixture
F-006 and F-039 attestations are updated: the Hermes leg is re-scoped to the guarantee that was actually chosen
The fixture is NOT regenerated to make the build green unless an intended engine change is what moved it
features.notes: FOUND 2026-08-23 on the FIRST CI run that ever reached gate 4, in run 32650792928 on commit e7c0391. packages/color-difference/test/golden/identity.test.ts "the Node execution > reproduces the committed digest, bit for bit": expected 31d18557233bbe42 (generated on Windows), received 9801fa1ab561ec61 on ubuntu-latest. SAME NODE VERSION — both 24.19.0, pinned by .nvmrc and installed by actions/setup-node — so this is Windows vs Linux on the same V8, not a version skew. THIS IS NOT A TEST DEFECT. NFR-3 is the guarantee AGENTS.md calls "the one guarantee that cannot bend", and the fixture description written during F-007 predicted exactly this: "these functions use more transcendentals than the conversions do — pow, atan2, exp, sin, cos — and ECMAScript specifies all of them as implementation-approximated, so this is where a cross-engine divergence is most likely to appear first". THREE FACTS NARROW IT SHARPLY. (1) @irodora/color-spaces PASSED on the same run: its 30-value digest over the conversions is identical on both platforms, so the seeded PRNG, the sample set, srgbToXyz, the matrices, cbrt and the sRGB transfer function all agree — the inputs to the metrics are byte-identical. (2) The probe assertion PASSED: the six recorded samples (indices 0, 1, 2, 3, 5000, 9999) match bit for bit in all eight metrics, so the divergence is RARE — a handful of samples out of 10,000, not a systematic offset. (3) That leaves the operations the metrics use and the conversions do not: atan2, sin, cos and exp in CIEDE2000, and pow in APCA. NEXT STEP IS ALREADY WIRED: metricDigests landed in the fixture and gate 5 now asserts one digest per metric, so the next CI run names the column. deltaE00 alone would point at atan2/sin/cos/exp; apcaLc at pow; deltaE76 at nothing transcendental, which would be far worse because it would mean the divergence is upstream of the metrics in a place fact (1) says is clean. DO NOT REGENERATE THE FIXTURE TO GO GREEN — that is the single thing it exists to prevent, and it would convert a discovered violation of the product central guarantee into a silent one. CI STAYS RED UNTIL THIS IS DECIDED, and that red is correct: it is reporting a real defect, unlike the gate 15 red that F-079 cleared. It does block releases, and that is the honest cost. WIDER CONSEQUENCE worth stating: F-006 attests "Node, browser and React Native produce bitwise-identical output" and notes that Node and Chromium are both V8 so their agreement is weak evidence. This is stronger evidence in the opposite direction — the same V8 on two operating systems already disagrees, which makes the Hermes leg (F-039) much less likely to hold and raises the question of whether bit-identical is achievable at all without shipping our own implementations of the transcendentals CIEDE2000 uses. ---- EVIDENCE ROUND 2 (run 32651483478, commit 9da842c): THE FIRST HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED. The per-metric digests came back and ALL EIGHT metrics disagree on Linux, deltaE76 included. deltaE76 is a Euclidean distance in Lab — subtraction, multiplication, addition and Math.sqrt, every one exactly specified by IEEE-754 — so it contains nothing implementation-approximated and CANNOT ITSELF DIVERGE. A metric that cannot diverge, diverging, means its inputs did. That rules out the CIEDE2000 transcendentals (atan2/sin/cos/exp) this fixture was written to catch, and moves the fault UPSTREAM into the conversions. Recorded values, Windows expected then Linux received: deltaE76 51e5921b2f88658c/6534ab4d867754bc; deltaE94 f14c888ca9b77b71/4d1018ab7beec3fc; deltaE00 83f514d2f007014e/27af2f731fc434b8; deltaEok b23abde28d5003dc/b7b0b84833f1c0b9; wcag(c,white) 2737af0263264aee/c5d0bb9d35449929; wcag(c,black) ca4855321c8e2a2c/4d45b281db2710f6; apca(white,c) 099a768b165bac12/727f5ed962392bba; apca(black,c) 48540f95082f2834/c3fff95a96e3ab20. THE ONLY SHARED ANCESTOR OF ALL EIGHT is srgbToLinear, which is Math.pow(magnitude, 2.4) above SRGB_EOTF_CUTOFF: it feeds srgbToXyz (hence Lab, hence deltaE76/94/00, hence Oklab and deltaEok), AND the relative luminance inside wcagContrast, AND the exponentiation inside apcaLc. ECMAScript specifies Math.pow as implementation-approximated. THE STILL-UNEXPLAINED FACT, which must not be smoothed over: @irodora/color-spaces PASSED on the same run and uses the same srgbToXyz. Its fixture uses seed irodora/f-006/identity against this one irodora/f-007/identity, so the most likely reading is that its 10,000 samples miss the inputs that diverge while these 10,000 hit enough to move every column — meaning that fixture is passing BY LUCK and NFR-3 is broken engine-wide rather than in one package. If instead the stage digests come back clean, the reading is wrong and something stranger is happening. NEXT MEASUREMENT IS WIRED (commit d37487c): the fixture now carries a digest per conversion stage over the same samples — linearR/G/B, X/Y/Z, L*/a*/b*, okL/oka/okb — so the first column that disagrees names the operation. linear* means Math.pow. lab* or ok* while xyz* is clean means Math.cbrt. xyz* while linear* is clean would be stranger than either, because plain + and * on doubles are exactly specified and a divergence there would not be a library question at all. ---- ROUND 5, AND THE FIRST COMPLETE READING (run 32653308836, commit fba3147). ROUNDS 2-4 WERE READ OFF TRUNCATED DATA and their conclusions are withdrawn: GitHub Actions publishes at most TEN failure annotations per check run, every run returned exactly ten, and I read those ten as the whole result. "Only linearR diverges", "all sixteen constants reproduce" and "the chunk counts are clean" were artefacts of the cap. The contradiction they produced never existed. Lesson recorded at memory/lessons/a-truncated-report-reads-exactly-like-a-passing-one.md. THE ACTUAL RESULT, from one assertion carrying the whole comparison: whole-run digest 9801fa1ab561ec61 on Linux against 31d18557233bbe42 committed from Windows; METRICS 8 of 8 differ; STAGES 12 of 12 differ (linearR, linearG, linearB, X, Y, Z, L*, a*, b*, okL, oka, okb); METRIC CHUNKS 19 of 100 differ; STAGE CHUNKS 13 of 100 differ; and — genuinely this time, because nothing was dropped — ALL SIXTEEN EXACT CONSTANTS REPRODUCE, and all six probe inputs AND outputs match bit for bit. THAT IS COHERENT, unlike every earlier reading. Roughly 13-19 chunks of 100 samples contain at least one divergent sample, which puts the divergent fraction at the order of 0.2% of inputs — a couple of dozen samples out of 10,000. One divergent linear channel propagates through the matrix into X, Y, Z and onward into Lab, Oklab and every metric for that sample, which is why all twelve stages and all eight metrics move while the fixed constants and the six probes do not: the ten constant inputs and the six probe colours simply are not among the unlucky ones. The metric run diverges in MORE chunks (19) than the stage run (13), which also fits: wcagContrast and apcaLc linearise independently and CIEDE2000 adds atan2, sin, cos and exp, so the metric path touches strictly more implementation-approximated operations than the conversion path. CONCLUSION: this is not a defect in Irodora code. ECMAScript specifies Math.pow, Math.cbrt, Math.atan2, Math.sin, Math.cos and Math.exp as implementation-approximated, and Node ships Windows builds compiled with MSVC and Linux builds with GCC/Clang. The same V8 version disagrees by ulps on a small fraction of inputs. NFR-3 SAYS "identical outputs on every platform" AND IS THEREFORE UNACHIEVABLE AS WRITTEN by any engine built on those functions. This also materially weakens F-006 attestation, which hopes the Hermes leg will hold: if the same V8 on two operating systems already disagrees, a different JavaScript engine almost certainly will. THE DECISION IS NOT MINE TO TAKE and needs the colour-scientist review AGENTS.md requires for engine work. Two real options. (a) Ship our own deterministic implementations of the transcendentals the engine uses — this is what bit-identical actually demands, and it is a large, research-adjacent piece of work for pow and cbrt alone. (b) Restate NFR-3 as identity AFTER CANONICAL ROUNDING, applied at the boundaries where determinism is load-bearing — the reproducibility envelope, cache keys, stored recommendations — so a stored answer still reproduces exactly while raw double arithmetic is admitted to be platform-dependent. RECOMMENDATION: (b), with the rounding defined in the envelope contract rather than sprinkled at call sites, because it keeps the guarantee where it actually matters to a user and stops the product claiming something no JavaScript engine can deliver. NOTE THAT (b) IS NOT A WEAKENING OF THE GATE: the fixture would assert bounded agreement rather than bit equality, and a change that moved a value beyond the bound would still fail. ---- MEASURED AND CLOSED 2026-08-24 (run 32698076891). THE MAGNITUDE, which five rounds had not asked for: apcaLc(white,c) worst 4 ULP at sample 6780, apcaLc(black,c) worst 2 ULP at sample 9040, and NOTHING else among 500 probes — no stage probe and no other metric probe differs at all. Four ULP at an Lc near 26.5 is 1.4e-14, the fifteenth significant digit. THE DECISIVE PRECEDENT was already in the repository: verify-content.mjs compares a published bundle against the current engine EXACTLY on hex, inSrgbGamut and lightnessOutOfRange — the quantised outputs — and with a 1e-12 tolerance on lab, lch, oklch and rgb. That tolerance is a thousand times the noise, which is why gate 11 passes on Linux and why THE CORPUS WAS NEVER AT RISK. The codebase had answered this question correctly once; only NFR-3 wording never caught up. RESOLVED BY ADR-0061: the canonical digest — every metric at the product two-decimal display precision — is asserted exactly and is what NFR-3 now promises; the raw double digest is recorded and reported, never asserted; a 16 ULP bound over 500 probes is the magnitude tripwire against an observed worst of 4. TWO DECIMALS IS A CORRECTNESS PROPERTY: rounding moves a disagreement rather than removing it, with straddle probability d/g, so 2 dp gives 3e-8 across the run while 12 significant digits — the instinctive choice — would give 1e-3 per value and a permanently flaky digest. NOT WEAKENED: accuracy. Gate 5 six cited datasets still check the engine against published references, and a change too small to move a displayed value is caught there, comparing against published reality rather than against ourselves. WATCHED: canonical digest mutated fails; raw digest mutated stays green and reports; a probe moved 40 ULP against the 16 bound fails and names the sample, the input and both values. ---- ROUND 7, AND A FIFTH THING READ OFF A TRUNCATED LIST. With color-difference fixed, gate 4 failed again — on @irodora/color-spaces, raw digest da79e11f85d2dc2b (Windows) against 5a11efe679787200 (Linux). EVERY EARLIER STATEMENT THAT COLOR-SPACES PASSED WAS WRONG, and wrong the same way as rounds 2-4: its failure never made the ten visible annotations while color-difference filled them, and absence was read as a pass. The reasoning built on it — "the conversions agree, so one divergent linear channel must be absorbed by the matrix" — was built on nothing. It was also, ironically, the exact question this feature acceptance list asked: whether the color-spaces fixture was passing by luck. It was not passing at all. FIXED CONSISTENTLY: canonicalise now lives in @irodora/testing and both fixtures use it at 5 SIGNIFICANT DIGITS rather than the 2 decimal places the first draft of ADR-0061 chose. Significant digits because the quantities span scales — XYZ ~0.1, Lab L ~50, Lab a/b to +/-100 — and a fixed decimal grid is too coarse for one and too fine for another, with too fine being the direction that flakes. Both fixtures now carry canonicalDigest, 500 probes and maxProbeUlp 16; both raw digests are unchanged (da79e11f85d2dc2b, 31d18557233bbe42), so nothing in the engine moved. WATCHED on BOTH packages: canonical digest mutated fails; raw digest mutated stays green and reports; a probe moved 40 ULP against the 16 bound fails naming the sample and both values; baseline green either side.

attested.criterion: The guarantee is verified on Linux and Windows, not only on the platform that generated the fixture
attested.verifiedBy: Windows and ubuntu-latest are BOTH verified — that half is discharged, and it is what the whole feature was about. What stays outstanding is the rest of the matrix: a browser (F-017) and Hermes (F-039) may diverge by more than the 4 ULP measured between two V8 builds, and if either exceeds the 16 ULP bound then ADR-0061 needs re-costing against shipping deterministic transcendentals. The bound is what will say so, which is why it is a committed number rather than a comment.

features.title: Self-review is declared in the data, not assumed by its absence
acceptance: provenance.reviewIndependence is required at verified, published and superseded, and rejected before them
independent keeps every existing rule: same id, two ids one person, missing reviewer role, inactive identity
self requires authoredBy to equal verifiedBy, and declaring self with two distinct editors is a failure
The valid fixture corpus contains a self-reviewed entry AND an independently reviewed one, and stays green
Two new invalid corpora are watched failing and naming the right field
The colour-detail surface shows that a self-reviewed entry was reviewed by its author
OQ-5 is closed by an ADR, and F-012 is no longer blocked by it
features.notes: The alternative was dropping the author-not-reviewer rule outright, which is one line and was rejected: verifiedBy would keep naming a reviewer and the schema would keep implying independent review, so an entry would assert a check that did not happen. Golden rule 12 says never ship a colour value without its provenance, and a claim that is false is worse than one that is absent. THE HONEST LIMIT, and it is not small: this makes single-editor review VISIBLE, not equivalent. One person checking their own work catches less than two people, and no gate can close that gap — which is why the label is the deliverable and why F-018 rendering it is an attested obligation rather than a nicety. CLOSED 2026-08-23. checkEditorialIdentity went from four failure modes to six. The two new invalid corpora were WATCHED: neutering the `self` branch makes gate 11 name both of them as ACCEPTED and exit 1, restored after. Deliberately NOT added: a "self-review-undeclared" fixture — `author-is-reviewer` already IS that case and a second fixture doing the same thing would be a decoy that tests nothing. content/AGENTS.md was corrected too: it stated "author and reviewer must be different identities. Enforced." unconditionally, which stopped being true, and a scoped rule that contradicts the code is worse than no rule.

attested.criterion: The colour-detail surface shows that a self-reviewed entry was reviewed by its author
attested.verifiedBy: The colour-detail screen (F-018) rendering the review independence on every entry, asserted in its a11y and e2e run. Nothing in this repository can prove a field is DISPLAYED before a surface exists — the same gap F-011 recorded for classification. It matters more here than there: if the label never reaches a reader, the honesty is confined to a JSON field and this feature has bought nothing over simply dropping the rule.

features.title: The build lane produces the artefact it claims to
acceptance: The internal lane builds a release variant, so the JS bundle is embedded and the app starts with no Metro and no network
The internal artefact is signed with the release key and gate 16 asserts the certificate
Gate 16 asserts the artefact permission set EQUALS a declared list, not merely that INTERNET is absent
The exact-set assertion is watched failing on an extra permission and on a missing one, with an exact match green either side
Internal versionCode comes from the run number, so internal builds upgrade over each other and any release upgrades over all of them
docs/operations/release-process.md describes the two lanes as they now are
features.notes: FOUND BY INSTALLING THE ARTEFACT. The APK from android-build.yml failed at launch with "Unable to load script ... make sure your bundle index.android.bundle is packaged correctly for release". That is CORRECT behaviour for what F-080 asked Gradle for and the WRONG artefact to have asked for: React Native skips JS bundling for every variant listed in `debuggableVariants`, which defaults to ["debug"], because a debug build expects Metro to serve JS over a socket. THE DEFECT IS NOT COSMETIC. The lane existed to discharge device attestations, and the two loudest are "every core journey completes with the device in airplane mode" and "the app opens no socket during any core journey" — an artefact that needs a socket to START cannot test either, so the lane could never have done its job. It also means F-080 shipped a lane nobody had installed the output of; gate 16 passed on that APK because gate 16 reads the manifest, not the bundle. TWO TRAPS DISPOSED OF AT THE SAME TIME: src/debug/ and src/debugOptimized/ carry dev-client manifest overlays declaring SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW and usesCleartextTraffic="true", which must never reach a user and are absent from a release variant by construction. That is also why gate 16 now pins the whole permission SET rather than only rejecting network permissions — an exact-set assertion is what would have caught a debug overlay reaching a release, and it catches any dependency adding anything. CLOSED 2026-08-24. Gate 16 grew from 10 --prove cases to 14. The internal lane now needs the release environment and its secrets, which is a deliberate trade: an internal build that differs from production in build type, minification or signature is testing a different artefact than the one that ships, and the signing key is the same key either way. R8 stays OFF and is F-086 — turning it on in the same change as "make the APK run at all" would confound the next failure. ---- FOUND ON THE FIRST REAL RUN, and it is a second defect of the same kind: THE LANE NEVER BUILT THE WORKSPACE. The app imports ten @irodora/* packages, every one declaring main and exports pointing at dist/, and dist/ is generated by pnpm build — not by pnpm install. Metro resolved @irodora/ui package.json, failed on the main it names, and reported it as an INVALID PACKAGE.JSON CONFIGURATION in a workspace package, which points at the package rather than at the missing step. release.yml runs pnpm build too, in its gates job, ON A DIFFERENT RUNNER — jobs share no filesystem, so that build never reached the one doing the bundling. Fixed in the shared composite action so both lanes are correct at once. THE PATTERN, worth naming: F-085 existed because an artefact was shipped that nobody had installed, and this was found because an artefact was finally built that nobody had bundled. Each step of the lane was verified in isolation and the lane end to end was not.

attested.criterion: The internal lane builds a release variant, so the JS bundle is embedded and the app starts with no Metro and no network
attested.verifiedBy: A person installing the artefact on a phone in airplane mode and watching it open. This workstation has no JDK and an Android SDK five platforms short of the required 36, so no Gradle build can run here at all — the previous artefact was shipped unverified in exactly this way and that is how the defect reached a device. Gate 16 reads the manifest and cannot see whether a JS bundle is present or loadable, so nothing automated closes this.

features.title: R8 minification and resource shrinking for release builds
acceptance: android.enableMinifyInReleaseBuilds and resource shrinking are on for release builds
The keep rules live in a config plugin, never in a hand-edited android/ directory
A device smoke test covers the Lens, the store and the font, which are the parts reflection breaks first
The size before and after is recorded
features.notes: DELIBERATELY NOT DONE IN F-085. R8 is standard for production and materially reduces size — the unminified debug artefact was 89.7 MB. It also breaks reflection-based native modules in ways only a device shows, and VisionCamera, expo-sqlite and Hermes are exactly the shapes that break. Turning it on in the same change as "make the APK run at all" would confound the next failure, and F-085 exists because an artefact was shipped without anyone installing it. Do this once the internal lane has produced an artefact somebody has actually launched.

features.title: HeroUI Native foundation and the token bridge that keeps the gates seeing colour
acceptance: heroui-native and uniwind build and bundle in apps/mobile, with react-native-worklets and react-native-reanimated pinned by pnpm.overrides to the versions VisionCamera resolves, and a single copy of each in the app tree
@irodora/design-tokens emits HeroUI global.css from design-system.manifest.json; the manifest remains the only source of colour and a hand-written colour in that stylesheet fails the build

Every HeroUI theme variable the manifest lacked is covered by a declared, gate-checked pairing: `backdrop` and `link` are new tokens, and the three status foregrounds resolve to the existing `inverse.foreground`, which measures 6.94/7.17/10.82 dark and 4.90/5.04/9.66 light on the status fills. Written as five new tokens; three of them proved unnecessary once measured, and inventing them would have been three duplicate values to keep in step
Every colour HeroUI would derive with color-mix is computed by the generator and checked by checkContrast and checkSeparation; the emitted stylesheet contains literal values and no color-mix call
apps/mobile cannot import heroui-native; the boundary guard fails on one, as it already does for other forbidden specifiers
A HeroUI-backed component renders under the a11y harness with its colours resolved in the tree, and the conformance suite fails a registered subject whose tree carries no resolved colour
A colour-bearing utility class in @irodora/ui fails lint, because className is inert under jest and a colour routed that way is invisible to the contrast gate

HeroUI colour animation is off and verify-motion fails a component that allows it, in either of the two ways it can be allowed — an explicit highlightAnimation/rippleAnimation, or the default feedbackVariant. Written as "disabled at the provider"; HeroUI's only global switch is `animation: "disable-all"`, which would take scale and opacity with it, and the manifest allows both — it is only COLOUR that may never be animated. Done per component with feedbackVariant="scale" instead, so press feedback survives
features.notes: ADR-0062. The spike proved the shape: className is resolved by Uniwind in Metro, which jest never runs, so a HeroUI tree renders with no colours in it and the contrast gate would pass vacuously. Colour reaches a component through style, from a resolved token, and that is what the lint rule and the conformance assertion enforce.

features.title: Text gains the accessibility affordances the HeroUI comparison surfaced, and the wrapper policy is written down
acceptance: Text supports a heading, rendering accessibilityRole="header" so a screen reader can navigate by heading; the conformance suite asserts the role reaches the rendered node

Text sets dynamicTypeRamp on every step, DERIVED from the manifest type scale against Apple's published ramp sizes rather than hand-mapped, so a new step is covered without anyone editing the component
The Home screen title is a heading — the prop has a real consumer, not only a test
Icon, Status and Surface remain on React Native primitives, and the reason is recorded where a reader meets it rather than only in a commit message
A rule states when a component sits on HeroUI and when it does not, so the question is answered once instead of per component; ACCESSIBILITY.md states the heading requirement it now implements
Swatch and every component carrying provenance or confidence is untouched; radius stays nativeRadius.swatch, the well and the two-tone opaque keyline are unchanged
The Home screen renders through the conformance suite in both themes with no new findings, and the a11y scope reporter still fails a component that is neither consumed nor registered
features.notes: RE-SCOPED after reading HeroUI's equivalents. Written as "rebuild Text, Icon, Status and Surface as HeroUI wrappers"; the comparison found no behaviour to inherit. HeroUI ships no Icon; its Alert is a banner rather than an inline status and cannot carry ADR-0044's three channels; its Surface adds a ThemeBackground/GlassView blur layer that would have to stay permanently disabled, because a blur tints what it surrounds and that is the simultaneous-contrast hazard swatch.well exists to prevent; and everything its Text offers over ours — accessibilityRole="header", dynamicTypeRamp — are native React Native Text props. Button DID gain from HeroUI and was rebuilt in F-087. HeroUI is used where it has behaviour to give: the R2 components, each arriving with the screen that consumes it.

features.title: Gate 0 catches an effect rationale that describes a world that no longer exists
acceptance: A rationale or memory note asserting a guard is absent, unbuilt or not blocking fails gate 0 when the named guard is in fact wired and running
A link whose guard is genuinely "none" still passes, because that is the honest case the graph is designed to carry
The check is proven by planting a discharged obligation in a rationale and watching gate 0 report it by link id and phrase
An escape hatch in the same visible-and-reasoned shape as retired-ok, for a rationale that describes a past state on purpose
features.notes: DONE. Gate 0 gained a 16th check: an effect rationale, or its paired memory note, that asserts its guard is absent or not blocking WHILE THAT GUARD IS WIRED now fails by link id and by phrase. 40 rationales and notes checked against 4 phrases on every run, and the counts are printed. THE CHECK NEVER FIRES ON A PHRASE ALONE, which is the whole design. It fires on a DISAGREEMENT between the prose and the repository: wired is computed from gates.json (status: active) and the root package.json scripts, never from prose. A link whose guard is literally "none" is skipped entirely — that is the honest case the graph exists to carry, E-009 has said so since F-001, and a CONTROL case in the proof plants the loudest phrase on E-009 and asserts it stays silent. THE FIRST RUN DISPROVED THE PLAN’S OWN POLICY, and that is the most useful thing that happened here. The plan said: if it fires on legitimate narration, remove the phrase rather than mark it. It then fired on E-017’s rationale and note — which had ALREADY been corrected and now QUOTE the old claim to show how a note rots. The quoted phrase is "not yet blocking": the canonical instance of the defect and the last phrase that should ever be deleted from the list. So the marker was the right instrument, this is its first legitimate use, and it is exactly what acceptance criterion 4 asks for. The policy is now: fire, read it, and CHOOSE — fix the prose when it is a claim, mark it when it is a quotation, remove the phrase only when it cannot tell the two apart at all. The plan is corrected in place. A QUOTE-DETECTING RULE WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED — "a phrase inside quotation marks is a quotation" would have removed both false positives automatically, and it would have been a SILENT exemption that a real claim could wear by being quoted. This repository consistently prefers a visible reasoned exemption to a clever automatic one (retired-ok, sampleValues, the ALLOWED sets), and the polarity is what makes those safe. WHAT IT CANNOT RESOLVE, printed on every run: a guard named only by a `test:` path or a `lint:` rule. A test file existing says nothing about whether a runner reaches it, and guessing would be the failing-open shape this file exists to prevent — so those 2 links are skipped and counted rather than assumed. PROVEN BY scripts/verify-stale-rationale-proof.mjs, wired into CI beside the other mutation proofs: 4 planted cases including the marker path and the guard:none control, with the baseline asserted green before the plants and after the graph is restored.

features.title: Taxonomy vocabulary is readable in Japanese, not only in English
acceptance: Every taxonomy.family in a published corpus version has a Japanese form that a reader sees in the ja locale
A family with no Japanese form fails a check rather than rendering its English slug
The Japanese form is authored where the family is authored, never inferred from the slug
features.notes: DONE. The Atlas filter, every Atlas row and the colour detail screen showed the English authoring slug — blue-grey, off-white, mineral-green — IN BOTH LOCALES since F-018. They now read as Japanese in ja and as English in en. WHERE THE WORDS LIVE WAS THE WHOLE DECISION, and F-018 had left it unfixed on purpose. A lookup table in the app would be ENUMERATED against a set the CORPUS controls, so a family added by a future publish would render blank or fall back to English — and ADR-0028 forbids fallback precisely because it makes a gap invisible. The catalogue cannot hold it either: ADR-0056 makes it a TypeScript record whose completeness tsc checks, and tsc cannot see a key set that comes from JSON data. So the words are in content/taxonomy.json beside editors.json, and COMPLETENESS MOVED FROM THE COMPILER TO GATE 11 — both directions, because a row nobody uses is how a live gap gets waved through later. Both watched failing. THE SCHEMA REFUSES A JAPANESE FORM THAT IS THE SLUG, which is the defect in its purest form: it satisfies "has a Japanese form" while showing a Japanese reader exactly what they saw before. E-017 FIRED A SEVENTH TIME AND CAUGHT SOMETHING REAL. The family words render on three screens, so verify-font-coverage.mjs now reads them — and immediately reported 鼠 and 陶, which nothing else in the repository required. 鼠 IS IN SIX OF THE TWENTY-FIVE FAMILIES, every grey one, so a Japanese reader would have seen tofu across most of the grey filter chips. Third time content has reached a screen from a direction the font check was not looking; the pattern is now explicit in E-028. THE FIRST DRAFT OF THE LEAK TEST CRIED WOLF. Scanning a joined text blob for each slug reported "red" and "brown" — red matches inside "japanese-inspired" and brown inside an English description. Both false positives, and a check that fires on prose gets deleted. It asserts on WHOLE TEXT NODES now, in the three shapes the family actually renders in, with a four-case decoy table. That table also caught a shell-mangled `startsWith()` with no argument, which the earlier one-case decoy had passed straight over [[a-decoy-that-is-not-broken-proves-nothing]]. THIS IS THE FIRST TIME ANY SCREEN HAS BEEN RENDERED IN ja. It needed a module mock of expo-localization, so it lives in its own file — screens.test.tsx keeps rendering in English because English is the decoy: it is the locale that legitimately resembles the slug. `familyLabel` is TOTAL OR IT THROWS: no fallback to the slug, because returning "blue-grey" quietly is what let this survive from F-018 to here. `era` and `material` will need the same treatment the day a measured entry carries one; both are null on every seed entry.

attested.criterion: Every taxonomy.family in a published corpus version has a Japanese form that a reader sees in the ja locale
attested.verifiedBy: THE MECHANISM IS PROVEN; THE WORDS ARE NOT REVIEWED. Completeness is asserted in both directions over the files by gate 11 (25 families, printed), and over what the APP loads by a test that renders the Atlas and the detail screen in the ja locale — the first time any screen in this repository has been rendered in Japanese. What no test reaches: whether 生成り, 青鼠, 岩緑青 and the other 22 are the words a Japanese speaker would choose. They are written by one editor and unreviewed (ADR-0060, OQ-5), and a family name is far more visible than a rationale — it is on every Atlas row. A reviewer should expect to change several.

features.title: The e2e harness that lets gate 7 run at all
acceptance: A surface declares a test:e2e task, so e2e-scope stops failing for want of anything to run
The Atlas journey completes on a device or emulator: launch, browse, filter, open a colour, read its provenance
The app opens no socket during that journey, asserted by the suite rather than by inspection
Gate 7 moves from pending to active with a real CI step, and removing that step turns gate 0 red
features.notes: GATE 7 SAYS activatesWith: F-039, AND F-039 IS DONE — but the gate is still `pending`, nothing in the workspace declares a `test:e2e` task, and e2e-scope.mjs fails for want of a surface to run. So the activation is owed by F-039’s attested criterion ("the app opens no socket during any core journey, asserted by the e2e offline suite rather than by inspection") and by nothing that is scheduled. FILED IN F-018 because F-018 lists `e2e` in its own verification and could not run it: reporting that as "not run" is honest for one feature and would become a habit across F-019, F-020, F-021 and F-023, each of which will list it and each of which will skip it. WHAT F-018 DOES ASSERT INSTEAD, so the gap is sized rather than waved at: the criterion-1 walk over the rendered tree proves every entry is present from the root, and the criterion-4 assertions prove the detail screen renders what the record carries. What no render-tree assertion can reach: real navigation between routes, a real gesture, a cold start, and whether a socket opened. The last one is the reason this is `must` rather than `should` — NFR-12 is a claim about the network, and a claim about the network cannot be checked without running the app. BLOCKED ON THE ENVIRONMENT, established 2026-08-25 while surveying what remained in R2. Every e2e tool for Expo — Maestro, Detox, Appium — arrives as a DEPENDENCY, and `pnpm install` cannot run on the maintenance workstation at all: pnpm refuses on ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_ENGINE, Node 22.16.0 and pnpm 9.3.0 against engines requiring 24.19.0 and pnpm 11. So this feature is not merely unverifiable there, it is not IMPLEMENTABLE there — the tool cannot be added. It also needs an emulator, which needs a JDK and an Android SDK that machine does not have, and acceptance criteria 2 to 4 can only be discharged by a CI run, which needs a push. THE NODE UPGRADE IS THE PREREQUISITE and no repository change can perform it. Recorded here rather than left in a chat, because the next session will otherwise select this feature and discover the same wall.

features.title: A design token that reaches no component fails a check
acceptance: Every value emitted from the design manifest is either read by a component or declared unreached with a reason
A token whose only reader is its own emitter test is reported by name
Proven by removing a real consumer and watching the check name that token
A deliberately unreached token can be declared, in the same visible-and-reasoned shape as retired-ok
features.notes: DONE. Every value in packages/design-tokens/src/generated/ was already byte-compared against the manifest TWICE — by emit.test.ts and by generate-design-tokens.mjs --check — so each one was known to be CORRECT. Nothing anywhere asked whether it was USED. scripts/verify-token-reach.mjs now runs in gate 8 beside a11y-scope.mjs: of 71 emitted names, 37 are read by a component and 34 are declared unreached with a reason. ADR-0071. THIS IS ADR-0054 ONE LEVEL DOWN. A component nobody renders and a token nobody paints are the same defect, and only one was reported — a cost paid twice already, by F-019 finding nativeNumericFeature by hand and F-094 finding the same shape at artefact level. THREE RULES DECIDE WHETHER IT IS WORTH ANYTHING. (1) packages/ui/src/testing/ is NOT a reader: a token read only by the conformance checker exists so a CHECK can enforce it, and without that exclusion four findings vanish and acceptance criterion 2 is unsatisfiable by construction. (2) Reach propagates through OBJECT VALUES (Surface resolves surface.1 through nativeElevation, and that name appears nowhere as a literal) but never through KEYS (theme.tsx reads nativeColors, whose keys are all 33 colour tokens) and never through ARRAY ELEMENTS (a membership test is a question nobody answers with the token). An object is looked up; a list is looked in. (3) COMMENTS ARE NOT CODE. THE PROOF FOUND THE BUG, NOT THE READING. border.strong was removed from all five components that use it and the check still called it reached, because Button.tsx mentions it in BACKTICKS in a comment explaining why it does not pair — and a backtick is one of the quote characters a literal read matches. Every JSDoc example in a repository that comments this heavily was counting as a consumer. Stripping comments turned three more tokens honest, the best of them foreground.3: THE TOKEN WHOSE ENTIRE PURPOSE IS TO BE RESTRICTED IS PAINTED BY NOTHING, and every mention of it in the reader zone is prose about why it is dangerous. Two more the prototype got wrong: nativeRadius.pill is a MEMBER ACCESS, not a literal, so the first version reported every radius step in the product as unreached; and xs is a radius step AND a type step, so 22 size="xs" literals were marking the radius reached. A name in two groups is now resolvable only from an owner- or prop-scoped read. THE ALLOWLIST IS THE ARTEFACT. .harness/verification/unreached-tokens.json is a readable inventory of what the design system has DRAWN and the product has not yet BUILT — no chart, no dialog or bottom sheet, no animation, no display type on any screen, and a Status component that conforms and that no screen renders. Every entry cites the feature that will consume it; the whole list prints on EVERY run, not only on a failure; and a declaration for a token that IS read fails, the same both-directions rule as E-021 and E-028. ONE ENTRY IS A DEFECT AND IT IS FILED AS F-095: nativeSpacing is emitted, exported and imported by nothing, while 69 hand-written padding/margin/gap declarations use eight values of which FIVE ARE NOT ON THE SCALE and 1, 2, 6 are not even multiples of the declared base: 4. An escape hatch whose reason is a pointer to work is working; one whose reason is a soothing sentence is how a defect becomes permanent. NO FILE IN packages/, apps/ OR content/ CHANGED. This feature adds a check and writes down what it found; it does not move a pixel. The proof plants IN MEMORY, so nothing is written to the working tree. WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER: a reader is found by string literal, which is a heuristic and not a type — a component that built a token name by concatenation would be reported as unreached, the false positive that gets a check deleted; none exists today and the header says which way it errs. Leaf level reaches named tokens only, so nativeMotion.durations.micro is not individually checked.

features.title: A cached task result is replayed for a world that changed
acceptance: A task whose test reads a file outside its own package is invalidated when that file changes
A cached result produced under a different Node or pnpm version is not replayed
The failure is demonstrated before the fix: a planted change outside a package must turn its cached green red
features.notes: DONE. `pnpm test` printed "31 successful, 31 total — 26 cached" while --force was red in four tests. It now prints "23 successful, 31 total" over the same repository state, which is the whole feature: the red was always there and the cache was reporting over it. BOTH FAILURES WERE DEMONSTRATED BEFORE BEING FIXED. H1: planting a manifest change that fails seven design-tokens tests (radius.swatch 0 -> 4) produced "cache hit, replaying logs — 5 successful, 5 total"; with the manifest in globalDependencies the same change produced "cache miss, executing" and three red suites. H2: `turbo run test --dry=json` shows the global hash carrying `.nvmrc` as a GIT BLOB and `engines` as a RANGE — the file that REQUESTS a version and a range, neither of which is the runtime — so nothing in it varies with the Node executing. After the fix, the same toolchain twice is a cache hit and a different IRODORA_TOOLCHAIN value is a miss with a different hash. THE TWO HOLES GOT DIFFERENT FIXES BECAUSE THEY ARE DIFFERENT IN KIND. The manifest is a small central artefact that legitimately belongs to the whole repository, so it joined globalDependencies beside tsconfig.base.json. `apps/mobile/src` is not: putting it there would invalidate all 31 tasks on any app edit, and a cache people distrust is a cache people turn off. So the FR-56 key scan MOVED OUT of packages/store/test/key.test.ts into verify-no-key-material.mjs — uncached, in gate 15, which is requiredFor:always rather than requiredFor:code. A REPOSITORY-WIDE CHECK DOES NOT BELONG INSIDE ONE PACKAGE’S TEST SUITE, not because caching is awkward to configure but because the scope of the question and the scope of the cache key disagree by construction and nothing reports that. Moving it widened the scan to every shipped src/ and immediately found four more legitimate 64-hex literals — the FIPS 180-4 vectors in corpus/digest.ts — now accounted for by EXACT VALUE, never by path, because exempting the file would let a key be pasted beside them. THE DURABLE DELIVERABLE IS verify-cache-scope.mjs, because fixing two instances does not stop the third. Two rules: a test may not read past its package unless the target is a declared global dependency (an unresolvable path counts as unaccounted — failing closed), and a cached task must be started by scripts/gate.mjs. Rule 1 proven with --prove over 6 planted cases including two controls, baseline green either side; rule 2 watched going red on a script reverted to a bare `turbo run test`. THE PROOF NEEDED A SECOND ATTEMPT and that is recorded: the first plant sat one directory deeper than a real test, so every planted ascent landed back INSIDE the package and three cases reported "nothing" while looking like a broken scanner. The first scanner draft was also wrong in the same way — it used a fixed count of ".." and reported ten in-package golden fixtures as escapes; ascents are resolved against the file’s real position now, with one level of base indirection because `const PACKAGE = join(HERE, "..")` is how the real case is written. ADR-0068 records the decision NOT to refuse on a mismatched toolchain: a false red is unhelpful, a false green is a gate lying about the code, and keying removes the second completely — refusing would add nothing to that while leaving a workstation unable to run any gate at all. THE TEST GATE IS NOW RED ON THIS WORKSTATION and that is correct: Node 22.16.0 cannot reproduce fixtures pinned to the last bit, F-083 says in as many words not to regenerate them, and the single blocking action is a Node upgrade — which no repository change can perform. ALSO FOUND, NOT FIXED, FILED AS F-094: `generate-design-tokens.mjs --check` exists, is referenced in two plans as "the freshness check", and is wired into no gate and no CI step.

features.title: The token generator has a --check nobody runs
acceptance: A stale generated token module fails a gate rather than shipping
The check is watched failing on a manifest edited without regenerating
features.notes: DONE, AND SMALLER THAN IT WAS FILED AS — the measurement corrected the premise. `generate-design-tokens.mjs --check` now runs FIRST in gate 9, so a manifest edited without regenerating, or a generated artefact edited by hand, fails before the suites that would agree with the stale values. THE FILED CLAIM WAS THAT ALL FIVE GENERATED ARTEFACTS WERE UNGUARDED. That was wrong. `packages/design-tokens/test/emit.test.ts` already byte-compares FOUR of them — tokens.css, tokens.tailwind.css, tokens.ts and native.ts — and carries its own "checks all four targets" assertion, so a stale manifest already failed gate 5. Planting a manifest edit and watching gate 5 go red is what established that, rather than reading the plan back to myself. THE REAL HOLE WAS ONE ARTEFACT, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT SHIPS: apps/mobile/global.css, the app’s own stylesheet. Measured, not inferred — hand-editing a hex in it leaves ALL 172 design-tokens tests green, and only the new check reports it. That file is E-019’s own subject, and E-019’s guard names heroui.test.ts and emitHeroui throwing, neither of which compares the committed file against what the manifest would emit now. WATCHED FAILING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which fail differently and are worth telling apart: an edited MANIFEST reports the derived srgb field plus four files at once; an edited ARTEFACT reports exactly one. Baseline asserted green either side of each, and the first mutation attempt SILENTLY DID NOT APPLY — `oklch` is an object, not an array — which is why every plant here throws if the value it meant to change did not change [[a-decoy-that-is-not-broken-proves-nothing]]. E-007 now names all five artefacts including global.css and tokens.tailwind.css, its guard names both halves, and its memory note no longer says "the four outputs" — the gap between "four" and "five" WAS the defect. No source changed: this feature is wiring plus proof.

features.title: The spacing scale reaches a component, or the value is not on the scale
acceptance: Every padding, margin and gap value in packages/ui/src and apps/mobile/src comes from the spacing scale, or is declared off-scale with a reason
nativeSpacing is imported by at least one component, so the emitted scale has a reader
A hand-written value that is not a step of the scale fails a check that names the file and the value
The five values in use today that are NOT on the scale — 1, 2, 6, 12, 16 — are each either moved onto it or added to it by an ADR
features.notes: DONE. THE RE-COUNT CHANGED THE FEATURE. F-092 recorded 69 declarations with 36 off-scale; measured at implementation time it was 102 with 45 off-scale — and, in the direction nobody had counted, FIVE OF THE SCALE’S EIGHT STEPS WERE USED ZERO TIMES (14, 28, 40, 56, 96). That is not a codebase that drifted off a scale. It is two systems never reconciled: an editorial rhythm in the manifest, and the conventional four-point grid the screens were built on. THE DECISION, ADR-0074, AND IT WAS THE USER’S: the scale moves to 4/8/12/16/20/28/40/56/96. `14` goes because it is the ONLY step that is not a multiple of the declared `base: 4` — the scale contradicted a rule the manifest states about itself — and because nothing used it. `12` and `16` join because they are used 24 times between them. 28 upward are used nowhere and are KEPT, said out loud: rhythm for layouts not built is not the same as a step that breaks a stated rule. CRITERION 1 (every value from the scale, or declared off-scale with a reason) — met. 102 declarations, 101 on the scale, one declared: `Swatch.tsx` `padding: 1` is F-068’s two-tone keyline, a border width sized to the device pixel, and rounding it to 4 would turn a keyline into a frame around every swatch. CRITERION 2 (nativeSpacing has a reader) — met by FIVE components, and the design system was the right place to start: packages/ui held ten spacing declarations and five of them contradicted the scale. Chip, SearchField, Status, Swatch and TextField now read `nativeSpacing`. Removing the unreached-tokens entry was PROVEN, not assumed — `verify-token-reach.mjs` fails on a listed name a component does read, and it was watched doing exactly that before the entry came out. CRITERION 3 (a check that names the file and the value) — met. `scripts/verify-spacing-scale.mjs`, wired into gate 8 beside verify-token-reach, naming file, line, property and value. It READS the scale from the manifest; a `--prove` case removes a step from the manifest and asserts the verdict follows, which is what separates reading the scale from carrying a copy that agrees with it only on the day it was written. Five planted cases: three red, TWO GREEN (a comment discussing an off-scale number, and a value that IS a step) — a check that fired on prose would be deleted and the real protection with it. Plus a dead exemption, which must fail: the list only ever grows otherwise. CRITERION 4 (the five off-scale values each resolved) — met, and by three different routes. `12` and `16` by moving the scale; `2 → 4` and `6 → 8` by moving 20 declarations; `1` by declaration. `2 → 4` is the change with a visible effect — all ten are a gap inside a stacked text pair — and it was chosen over exempting ten declarations because a scale that exempts its most common small value is not a scale. `6 → 8` rounds UP: seven of the ten are row padding or label gaps where the taller result also helps a touch target. ONE THING FOUND WHILE FIXING IT, FILED AS F-103: `nativeRadius` is a NAMED record and `nativeSpacing` is an unnamed array, so `nativeRadius.swatch` reads and `nativeSpacing[2]` does not. That asymmetry is why this token had no reader long before anybody counted, and it now carries a live hazard — the indices are positional, so a future step added or removed renumbers every reader while everything still compiles. E-036 records it; the emitted binding carries a doc comment saying so where a component author will see it. GATES RUN ON THIS WORKSTATION: state (green), the spacing check and its proof (green, 5 planted cases + a dead exemption + a perturbed manifest), verify-token-reach (green, and watched RED first with the stale entry in place), generate-design-tokens --check (green, all five artefacts), packages/design-tokens’ own suite (172 tests, which byte-compare the regenerated files), typecheck for packages/ui and apps/mobile, eslint and prettier. NOT RUN HERE, AND THE SECOND ONE MATTERS: (1) every gate needing pnpm — Node 22.16.0 / pnpm 9.3.0 against engines >=24.19.0 / >=11. (2) THE RENDERED HALF OF GATE 8. jest cannot start in packages/ui or apps/mobile because `react-native-worklets` is absent everywhere, a consequence of pnpm install never having run here — pre-existing and unrelated to this change, verified by the error naming a missing resolver module rather than any edited file. THE LAYOUT CHANGE IS THEREFORE UNVERIFIED VISUALLY. Twenty values moved by 2px each; there is no emulator and no JDK on this workstation, and the F-095 note is right that a screenshot comparison is worth more than a test for "the layout is now subtly wrong everywhere". Reported as unverified rather than verified.

features.title: The key-material scan has no ledger for a rules digest
acceptance: verify-no-key-material.mjs accounts for the rules-bundle digest and gate 15 is green with no shipped source unexplained
A planted 64-hex literal that is NOT a recorded digest is still reported, proven by a decoy
features.notes: FOUND WHILE VERIFYING F-026, PRE-EXISTING, AND CONFIRMED AT HEAD WITH EVERY F-026 CHANGE STASHED. `node scripts/verify-no-key-material.mjs` reports apps/mobile/src/rules/generated/lexicon.ts carrying 64 hex digits "the ledger does not record", and exits 1 — so gate 15 (security) is RED. The literal is not a key: `git grep` finds the same value in content/rules/index.json, which is the rules bundle digest F-069 introduced. The script accounts for CORPUS digests by reading content/versions/ (130 of them), and the rules bundle is a second versioned artefact with its own digest home that the script has never been taught about. THE FILE WAS LAST WRITTEN BY F-021 (f0f1f6c), so this has been red since then; the sessions after it recorded gate 15 as "partly run" because gitleaks was not installed and did not report the key scan failing — which is how a red gate stayed invisible across four features. That second-order lesson is the reason this is `should` and not `could`. FIX SHAPE: the ledger the script consults should be every recorded digest, not every corpus digest, and the decoy in the fix must plant a 64-hex literal that is NOT a recorded digest — otherwise widening the ledger is indistinguishable from switching the check off. DONE. THE FIX IS THE ONE THE NOTE ABOVE PREDICTED: `ledgerDigests()` now reads a NAMED list of content ledgers — content/versions/ (126 digests) and content/rules/index.json (1) — rather than the corpus ledger alone, and gate 15 is green over 179 shipped source files with nothing unexplained. THE DECOY WAS THE PART WORTH GETTING RIGHT. The existing probe took `[...ledger][0]`, which is one of the four published SHA-256 vectors hard-coded in this script — it is silent whether or not either ledger FILE was read, so it could never have caught the rules ledger being absent from the list, which is exactly the defect. There is now one probe PER LEDGER SOURCE, each using the first digest that source carries, plus the planted key literal that must still be reported. A named ledger that is missing, or that records no checksum at all, now FAILS rather than contributing nothing: absence makes this check STRICTER, which is the safe direction and therefore precisely the kind of breakage nobody investigates — until the day it is easier to silence a real finding than to work out why the ledger went quiet. Each source prints its digest count on every run for the same reason. PULLED FORWARD FROM R3 DELIBERATELY, and this is the one place release order gives way: gate 15 was RED at HEAD and gate 15 is blocking. A red blocking gate is not a scope choice to be sequenced. WATCHED FAILING, four ways, each restored and the baseline green after: dropping content/rules/index.json from LEDGER_SOURCES reproduces the original finding on lexicon.ts exactly; a missing ledger file and a ledger recording nothing each fail naming the source; and the planted key literal is still reported on every run. THE SECOND-ORDER LESSON IN THE NOTE ABOVE HELD AGAIN. This was found only because `pnpm install` finally ran here and gate 15 could be executed in full — it had been red since F-021 (f0f1f6c) and CI never reached it, because CI stopped at the install step (see F-098).

features.title: The photo path has no producer: a capture surface hands a reading to profile setup
acceptance: A capture surface exists that a person can reach, and it produces a LensReading
Profile setup receives that reading from the surface rather than from a prop a test supplies
A person can complete photo-assisted setup end to end without a test harness
The photo-assisted path is validated across the full skin-tone range before it is released (NFR-23)
features.notes: ONE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION WAS ADDED DURING IMPLEMENTATION, DELIBERATELY AND WITH THE REASON. NFR-23 says a band that underperforms "blocks release of that feature", and F-097 is the feature that makes the photo path reachable for the first time — so the requirement lands here, and the harness records a release-blocking obligation as an ATTESTATION against an acceptance entry. Without the entry there was nowhere to record it, and the alternative was leaving it in prose that gate 0 cannot see. The user was asked and chose to build both halves and attest NFR-23 rather than gate the path at runtime. DONE. THE PRODUCER EXISTS. `read()` shipped in F-040 and `estimateFromReading` in F-027, and until now nothing in the app could construct a `LensReading` — [[a-tested-module-nobody-wired-up-passes-every-test-it-has]] with two features stacked on top of it. THE ARCHITECTURE IS A SPLIT, AND THE CHECKER IS THE SMALLER REASON FOR IT. A VisionCamera view cannot be rendered by jest, and a11y-scope fails on a screen the conformance registry cannot reach — so `src/screens/Lens.tsx` takes the viewfinder as a NODE and `src/lens/viewfinder.tsx` supplies it from the route, exactly as app/profile.tsx imports deviceRepository. The bigger reason is that everything in the screen is layout, copy and formatting — the parts that go wrong quietly — and all of it is now registered in three permission states and checked in both themes by CI. CRITERION 1 (a capture surface a person can reach, producing a LensReading) — met in code: a /lens route, an entry point on Home, permission handling in three states, and a frame output that reduces through `read()`. Whether it RUNS is the attestation above; nothing here claims it does. CRITERION 2 (profile setup receives the reading from the surface, not from a prop a test supplies) — met. `src/lens/handoff.ts` is a one-shot slot: not a route parameter, because a route parameter is a URL and because a JSON round-trip produces a `LensReading`-shaped object the compiler believes on trust — and the type having no field for a frame is the whole guarantee (F-040). ONE-SHOT is the interesting half: someone who reaches their profile, decides to answer the twelve comparisons instead and navigates back must not be re-proposed the estimate they declined. Five tests, including that one. CRITERION 3 — ATTESTED, not met. See above. THREE THINGS FOUND BY WIRING THE REAL API. (1) VisionCamera 5 has a different surface from the one F-040 was written against, and asking for `yuv` would have meant hand-writing a YUV→RGB matrix — arithmetic the engine does not provide and apps/mobile/AGENTS.md forbids the app from inventing. ADR-0075 records requesting `rgb` instead, and says plainly that it supersedes the pixel-format half of an F-040 criterion that nobody has run. (2) `readCaptureSpace` accepted any string containing "rgb-8" as sRGB, and `rgb-rgb-8-bit` is a VisionCamera PIXEL FORMAT — a memory layout would have been read as a colour space, producing a confident sRGB reading for a frame nobody had described. Anything naming a bit depth is now refused first, with four decoys. The space comes from the SESSION (`onSessionConfigSelected`), and is `unknown` until it does, which caps confidence rather than defaulting. (3) The profile screen has said "No camera" since F-026 and that became FALSE the moment this path existed — with nothing failing: the key existed, it rendered, and the test asserting it covered the guided path, which is unchanged. The claim is now per-path and asserted FROM BOTH SIDES. E-037 records it. GATES RUN: state, a11y scope, token reach, the spacing check, content (including a regenerated font subset — the new Japanese copy needed 9 codepoints the face lacked), claims, no-inference, app-imports, engine purity, motion, guards, unsafe call sites, cache scope, typecheck for apps/mobile and packages/ui, eslint and prettier. NOT RUN: every gate needing pnpm; THE RENDERED HALF OF GATE 8, because jest cannot start in either zone; and gate 7, which is pending. So the three conformance registrations and the privacy-claim assertion are WRITTEN AND NOT RUN HERE — CI runs them, and that is a real difference from the camera code, which nothing anywhere runs yet.
