features.title: The lockfile drifts from a manifest and only the install step finds out
acceptance: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile succeeds at HEAD on the pinned toolchain
A manifest declaring a dependency the lockfile does not resolve fails gate 0 — before install — naming the package and the workspace project
A changed specifier, a removed dependency, an override drift and a workspace project with no importer each fail the same check
The check is watched failing, and watched STAYING GREEN on a reformatted manifest and on a workspace project that declares nothing
features.notes: FILED AFTER THE FACT AND SAYING SO. CI was red on three consecutive pushes (4528c52, bfcfe9d, dfc3239) at the `Install` step, with all seventeen steps after it skipped. This was not selected through next-feature; it was diagnosed from a red build and repaired, and the record is written to match what happened rather than to look like the loop. ROOT CAUSE: F-020 (9ce0926) added `@irodora/corpus: workspace:*` to packages/store/package.json and nothing regenerated pnpm-lock.yaml, so `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` refused with ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE naming that one package. IT WAS NOT CARELESSNESS, WHICH IS WHY A GATE IS THE RIGHT ANSWER: `pnpm install` could not run on the workstation at all (Node 22.16.0 and pnpm 9.3.0 against engines demanding 24.19.0 and 11), and progress.md records the workaround honestly — packages/store/node_modules/@irodora/corpus was a hand-made junction. The junction made the local tree behave correctly, and there was no local command that could have disagreed with it. FIXED by regenerating the lockfile on the pinned toolchain; the diff is three lines, the importer entry that was missing. GUARDED by a new section in gate 0 that mirrors pnpm own rule — the same three dependency sections, the same verbatim specifier comparison, the same overrides handling — and runs BEFORE install, on Node built-ins, on a clean clone. That last part is the whole point: it is the only place that can say "the lockfile is stale" to somebody who cannot run pnpm at all. Workspace projects come from the pnpm-workspace.yaml globs rather than a hard-coded list, and a glob the parser cannot expand FAILS rather than being skipped. PROVEN by scripts/verify-lockfile-proof.mjs, wired into CI beside the other gate 0 proofs: seven cases with the baseline green either side, five red and TWO GREEN. The second control is the one that matters — a workspace project declaring nothing is written `tests/bench: {}` in the lockfile, and reading that as absent would have made the check fail on a correct lockfile from its first run. FOUND WHILE FIXING THIS, and fixed under its own id: gate 15 was independently red at HEAD (F-096). Repairing install alone would have moved the red from step 9 to step 25.

features.title: One warm/cool rule: the app imports the engine instead of repeating it
acceptance: apps/mobile/src/profile/photo.ts computes no warm/cool bias of its own and imports the engine
The reference poles reach the app from the same rule set the engine scores with, not from a literal
E-038 is resolved, and gate 0 stops warning that it carries no guard
features.notes: DONE. THE BLOCKER IN THIS ENTRY WAS ALREADY CLOSED WHEN I READ IT, AND THAT IS THE FIRST THING WORTH RECORDING. It said "BLOCKED ON THE TOOLCHAIN — DO IT ON THE PINNED TOOLCHAIN", because adding a workspace dependency here needs a hand-made junction and "a junction is what F-098’s own notes call the workaround that hid a stale lockfile for four features". True when written — and F-098 is the feature that removed it. Gate 0 section 7b now compares every manifest against pnpm-lock.yaml BEFORE install, on Node built-ins, on a clean clone, built precisely so somebody who cannot run pnpm is still told the lockfile is stale. The hazard the note warned about had become the gate. Watched: the manifest edit turned gate 0 RED naming "@irodora/recommendation@workspace:*", the importer entry turned it green, then the junction. A lesson is filed — a blocker outlives the state of the world that caused it, and the better the argument the less likely anybody rechecks its premise. CRITERION 1 (photo.ts computes no warm/cool bias of its own) — met by deletion: `biasFromHue`, its private `hueGap`, and the WARM_HUE/COOL_HUE literals are gone, and `hueBias` from @irodora/recommendation is called instead. Deleting `hueGap` mattered as much as deleting the bias function: a circular-distance helper left in the file is what somebody reaches for next time, and a second copy of a rule never arrives labelled as one. The old comment justified keeping it as "not colour arithmetic, the arithmetic of a circle" — true, and beside the point. What made it a defect was that two files computed one product rule and no single-platform test could see them disagree. CRITERION 2 (the poles reach the app from the same rule set the engine scores with) — met, and it was the work. The app had no weights bundle. `generate-rules-bundle.mjs` now emits a SECOND module beside the lexicon, same shape step for step: the last published row, the text from the file, the digest from the LEDGER, and a parse through the engine’s own `parseWeightContent` before either is written — so "these weights load" is decided by the code that will score with them. `apps/mobile/src/rules.ts` verifies the digest and the rationale count (they catch different things: the digest catches an edited file, the count catches a generated module and a ledger row from two different generations, where the module would verify perfectly against its own stale digest). CRITERION 3 (E-032 resolved, gate 0 stops warning) — met, and gate 0’s own output is the evidence: warnings went 49 → 48 and the "E-032 (high) has no guard" line is gone. Marked RESOLVED rather than guarded, deliberately: a guard would be a check that the two implementations still agree, and there is no second implementation to disagree. THE LINK WAS MATCHED BY `from.ref`, NOT BY ID — two links carry E-032 (F-102), so resolving by id would have been a coin toss between this and F-098’s lockfile link. F-102 still stands. THE TEST THAT REPLACED THE OLD ONE SWEEPS. `biasFromHue` and `hueBias` both passed a three-point check — warm, cool, and the middle — for two features while being two implementations of one rule. Three points is what a second copy passes. The new assertion walks 180 degrees and requires monotonicity, and the poles are compared against the file on disk rather than against 60 and 240 typed in a test — two literals in a test are the same defect as two literals in the source, and would keep passing through exactly the publish that made the app and the engine disagree. WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DID NOT FIX: `hueBias` still reports a grey at C = 0.012 as more warm than the most saturated red in the corpus (E-034). F-101 owns it. Changing what the answer IS in the same commit that changes where it COMES FROM would leave nobody able to say which one moved a number. The app now calls a function that is still defective — which is a smaller problem than two copies of it, because there is one place to fix. GATES RUN: state (watched RED first, on the lockfile), the rule-bundle --check, content, app-imports, engine purity, claims, no-inference, typecheck, eslint, prettier. NOT RUN, AND IT IS THE ASSERTION THIS FEATURE EXISTS FOR: jest, in either zone — @babel/runtime is absent from apps/mobile and react-native-worklets from packages/ui, both partial-install symptoms. So the 180-degree sweep is SOURCE, not evidence, on this workstation; CI runs it. `tsc --noEmit` covers the type-level half, and it is not nothing: the three deleted exports failed the typecheck the moment they went, which is how the test file was found. Also not run: any gate needing pnpm, and a real `pnpm install` to confirm the hand-written importer entry resolves the way pnpm would.

features.title: A proof that perturbs the colour engine and cannot put it back
acceptance: verify-content-proof.mjs leaves packages/color-spaces/src/matrices.ts unmodified however it exits
On a toolchain that cannot rebuild, it refuses BEFORE mutating anything and says why
The restore is unconditional rather than dependent on the mutation succeeding
features.notes: FILED AFTER THE FACT AND SAYING SO — found while verifying F-029, not selected through next-feature. THE DEFECT: the E-001 case in verify-content-proof.mjs writes a perturbed OKLab matrix into packages/color-spaces/src/matrices.ts and then calls `rebuild()`, which shells out to pnpm. On this workstation pnpm refuses outright — Node 22.16.0 against engines >=24.19.0 — so `apply()` THREW AFTER THE WRITE, the throw escaped before the case’s `cleanup` could run, and the script exited leaving a corrupted colour engine in a TRACKED SOURCE FILE. WHAT THAT LOOKS LIKE FROM THE OUTSIDE: gate 11 goes from green to 374 failures, every one reading "the CURRENT engine derives ... publish a NEW corpus version". The diff is ONE DIGIT — 0.819022437996703 became 0.829022437996703 — in a file nobody in the session had opened. I spent a long time bisecting my own changes for it, because a corrupted engine looks exactly like a feature that broke the corpus. `git status` naming matrices.ts as modified was what finally said otherwise. THE REAL DANGER IS THE COMMIT. The perturbation is a tracked-file edit that `git add -A` picks up without comment, so the next feature commit made on this workstation after running the proof would have shipped a wrong colour matrix — the one artefact in this repository whose corruption changes every derived value and reproduces perfectly. TWO FIXES, BOTH NEEDED. (1) `apply` and `runGate` are now inside a try/FINALLY so cleanup is unconditional — the case’s own cleanup does `git checkout` BEFORE its rebuild, so the source comes back even when the rebuild then throws. (2) The proof RUNS `rebuild()` ONCE UP FRONT, on an unmodified tree, and exits naming the toolchain if it fails — refusing before mutating rather than discovering it halfway through. A proof that perturbs a colour matrix and then reports an unrelated failure is a proof nobody can read. WATCHED: the proof now exits 1 with "This proof cannot run on this toolchain", `git status packages/color-spaces/` is empty afterwards, and gate 11 stays green. What is NOT proven here is that the proof still DISCRIMINATES — that needs the pinned toolchain, and it was already the case before this change that nobody on Node 22 could run it.

features.title: A near-neutral has no temperature, everywhere it is judged
acceptance: Every place a colour of arbitrary chroma is judged for warmth reads a chroma-weighted temperature, or states why it does not
The decision for scoreColor is made deliberately — a near-neutral garment either has a temperature or does not, and the answer is written down
E-034 is resolved and gate 0 stops warning that it carries no guard
features.notes: THE PLAN FILE WAS WRITTEN AFTER THE ADR, NOT BEFORE THE CODE, AND GATE 0 CAUGHT IT AT CLOSE-OUT. What happened was investigation → measurement → ADR-0076 → code; the ADR did the design work. Golden rule 3 asks for the artefact in .harness/plans/ first, and it was not there. Recorded rather than backdated — the plan file says so in its own header. DONE, AND THE PRODUCT QUESTION F-031 LEFT OPEN WAS ANSWERED FROM MEASUREMENTS TAKEN BEFORE ANY CHANGE — so nothing here is an artefact of the change it argues for. ADR-0076 carries the reasoning. THE NUMBER THAT DECIDED IT: 45 of the 120 published entries sit below NEUTRAL_CHROMA. 37.5% of the corpus, in a corpus built around subdued weathered colour — not an edge case, and it will not be one in a wardrobe. THE PAIR: `usu-gami` (Thin Paper, C = 0.006, h 92°) and `usu-shimo` (Thin Frost, C = 0.005, h 246°), two off-whites 0.027 apart in lightness, came back at +0.644 and −0.933. Taken to a score with a sharper pair at the same chroma, a strongly warm profile rated Lime Wall 97 and Thin Frost 64 — A 33-POINT GAP OUT OF 100 BETWEEN TWO PALE GREYS. F-031 asked whether "this near-neutral garment is warm" might be defensible; the answer is that the verdict is OPPOSITE for two greys nobody can distinguish, driven by an angle computed from two components near zero. CRITERION 1 (every place a colour of arbitrary chroma is judged) — met at all three remaining sites: `scoreColor`’s temperature fit, `alternativesFor`’s warmer/cooler axes (FR-38’s "like that, but warmer" — offering a grey as the warmer option is the same defect wearing a different hat), and the app’s photo path, which F-099 had already reduced to one call. `hueBias` stays exported and stays the pure hue question; ADR-0076 moved CALL SITES. CRITERION 2 (the scoreColor decision made deliberately and written down) — ADR-0076, including the alternative that was nearly right: letting the factor ABSTAIN below NEUTRAL_CHROMA. Rejected because it asserts a grey suits EVERYONE EQUALLY, which is a stronger claim than the gradient, and because the mechanism runs through `raw[factor]` — profile confidence — so the reported `confidence`, documented as describing the PROFILE, would have started varying with the COLOUR. A number quietly meaning something else is worse than a fit that is merely approximate. CRITERION 3 (E-034 resolved, gate 0 stops warning) — met; warnings went 48 → 47 and the line is gone. Together with F-099 the graph now carries no guardless high-severity link. THE COST, STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER: 45 of 120 entries move, mean |Δfit| 0.055, largest 0.407. Every score containing a near-neutral changes. Nothing stores a recommendation yet — no screen scores a colour — so the blast radius is empty today, which is why now. WHAT THE CHANGE EXPOSED ON ITS WAY THROUGH, AND WAS FIXED HERE: `alternativesFor`’s doc had always said an axis is "never filled with a duplicate" and NOTHING IMPLEMENTED IT. The test asserting uniqueness passed because no pool had happened to produce one; ADR-0076 produced one immediately — with a two-colour pool of off-whites the single non-best candidate is genuinely cooler AND lighter AND higher-contrast, so three axes chose it: three chips, one swatch, a person told they have three options when they have one. Not mislabelled, which is why the code had to decide rather than the data. First axis in ALTERNATIVE_AXES order takes it; the rest are omitted. WATCHED FAILING, BOTH WAYS. A scratch proof reverted each change separately and re-ran the suite: with `hueBias` restored, 2 tests fail and the output names the ADR-0076 block; with the de-duplication removed, 1 fails. Both files restored byte-for-byte and verified. The new assertions each carry a DECOY — two saturated opposites must still score far apart, and a saturated reading must still propose a temperature — because "greys now agree" is also true of a factor that stopped reading hue at all. GATES RUN: state, the engine suite (103 tests, 6 files, green), typecheck for the engine and the app, content, the rule-bundle --check, a11y scope, token reach, spacing, perf and its proof, engine purity, app-imports, claims, no-inference, eslint, prettier. NOT RUN: jest, in either app zone — @babel/runtime absent from apps/mobile and react-native-worklets from packages/ui — so the app-side consequence test is written and not run here; CI runs it. Its thresholds are NOT guesses: the four readings were computed directly against the built engine (greys ±0.023 against ±0.913 before, orange +0.915, blue −0.742) and the measured numbers are in the test’s own comment. Also not run: any gate needing pnpm.

features.title: Two different effect links are both numbered E-032
acceptance: Every id in effects.json is unique, and the renumbered link keeps its memory note and index row
Gate 0 fails on a duplicate effect id, watched failing before it is fixed
Every reference to the renumbered id elsewhere in the repository moves with it
features.notes: DONE, AND SELECTED BECAUSE R3 WAS NOT CLOSED. The request named R4; next-feature forbids silently pulling from a later release, so the R3 remainder was checked rather than assumed. F-081 is blocked on a paid Apple membership (OQ-6 is a purchase). F-086 is `todo` and genuinely unavailable here — `which java` finds nothing, `C:\Program Files\Java` does not exist, and its own note also requires an artefact somebody has launched, which is F-104’s outstanding attestation. F-102 was the only actionable R3 item, so R4 was not eligible. WHICH LINK KEEPS E-032 WAS SETTLED FROM THE RECORD, NOT FROM PREFERENCE. Both were load-bearing and both were widely cited, so `git log -S` supplied the tiebreak: F-098 allocated E-032 to the pnpm-workspace.yaml → lockfile link at 09:22:54 on 2026-08-26, and F-028 allocated it again to the score.ts#hueBias link at 09:46:43 — TWENTY-FOUR MINUTES LATER, by two features neither of which could see the other’s write. First allocation wins, so the lockfile link keeps it and the hueBias link is now E-038. Two other things agree rather than only one: ADR-0077 already cites "the same rule E-032" meaning the lockfile rule, and leaving a decision record correct beats editing it; and the moving link is `resolved`, so its id has no future to disturb. WHY NO SCHEMA COULD HAVE CAUGHT IT. JSON Schema 2020-12 has `uniqueItems`, which compares WHOLE OBJECTS, and no unique-by-property constraint — two links sharing an id and differing anywhere else are distinct objects and validate perfectly. The primary key is the one field a schema is structurally incapable of checking, which is why the check went into gate 0 rather than into effects.schema.json. WATCHED FAILING AGAINST THE REAL DEFECT, NOT A PLANT. The collision was in the tree, so the check landed first and gate 0 was run against it: `✗ E-032 is used by two different links: "pnpm-workspace.yaml" and "packages/recommendation/src/score.ts#hueBias"`. THE MESSAGE NAMES BOTH SUBJECTS DELIBERATELY — "duplicate id E-032" on its own sends the reader to `git log -S` to find out which two collided, which is the search the check exists to spare them. The pass line now reports the distinct count beside the link count (`36 links, 36 distinct ids`), because a check that only ever speaks on failure is one nobody notices going missing. CRITERION 3 VERSUS APPEND-ONLY HISTORY, DECIDED RATHER THAN OMITTED. Read literally, "every reference moves with it" would rewrite progress.md, which state/README.md defines as append-only, and would destroy the only account of how the collision happened. The line was drawn at WHAT A READER CONSULTS AS CURRENT: effects.json (the id and E-034’s citation), the memory index row, the note heading, the comments in score.ts / photo.ts / generate-rules-bundle.mjs, F-028’s `effects` array and F-099’s acceptance text all moved; progress.md, the historical plans, and feature `notes` narrating what was true at the time did not. F-099’s acceptance criterion was reworded ONLY to change the identifier — the opposite of the failure state/README.md warns about, since left as E-032 it would resolve to an active critical link and read as UNMET. The mapping is recorded once, in the renumbered link’s memory note, under a heading naming what a reader arriving from history is looking for; gate 0 already requires that note to exist and to be referenced, so the pointer cannot rot. THE PROOF, AND THE TWO MUTATIONS IT SURVIVED. verify-effect-id-proof.mjs runs four cases — three red, one green control — and restores effects.json BYTE-COMPARED rather than merely re-running the gate. Case 1 RECONSTRUCTS the historical collision, because the live evidence expired the moment the renumber landed. Case 3 attacks a plausible wrong implementation rather than the margin: two links sharing an id AND the same from.ref, which a check deduplicating on `from` misses while passing everything else. Neutering the check put 3 of 4 cases the wrong way with the control still green; keying on from.ref exited 1 AND TURNED THE BASELINE RED on five pairs — E-017/E-026/E-027/E-029 and E-034/E-038 each legitimately share a `from` with a sibling, because one source can have several distinct consequences. LINKS SHARING A SOURCE IS NORMAL; LINKS SHARING AN ID IS CORRUPTION, and a check conflating them fires on correct data, which is how a real check gets deleted for being noisy. THE CONTROL ROTTED INSIDE THE SAME SESSION. Case 4 was first written with a literal E-039 and passed; the effect trace then recorded E-039 for the id-uniqueness property itself, and the control began planting a DUPLICATE while asserting green — reporting the check as broken when the check was the only thing working. That is the decoy-written-against-old-values lesson in under an hour rather than over a release, and it was visible only because the proof was re-run AFTER the effect trace instead of before it. The control now DERIVES the next unallocated id from the graph and throws if none remains. THE SAME HOLE EXISTS IN TWO MORE FILES, FOUND BY EXPERIMENT AND FILED AS F-106. Planting a second entry numbered F-102 in feature_list.json left gate 0 GREEN; two gates sharing an id in gates.json also left it GREEN. Both restored and gate 0 re-run green. ADR numbers are fine (78 files, 0 duplicates, index reconciled both ways) and corpus slugs are checked by gate 11 — so CONTENT ALREADY LEARNED THIS AND THE HARNESS STATE FILES DID NOT. The feature-id case is worse than the one just fixed: a feature id is a CONTROL-FLOW input, not only a citation target — blockedBy resolves by id and next-feature selects by id — so an ambiguous feature id makes a BLOCKER ambiguous rather than a warning. Not fixed here: WIP is 1 and this feature’s acceptance is scoped to effects.json. Golden rule 5 requires it be recorded, and it is. ONE RECORD CORRECTED IN PASSING AND NOT EDITED. F-091’s blocker says pnpm install cannot run here on Node 22.16.0 / pnpm 9.3.0; F-105 established that is false. F-091 stays blocked — it needs an emulator and there is no JDK — but FOR A DIFFERENT REASON THAN ITS NOTE GIVES. Left unedited because WIP is 1, and recorded in progress.md so the next session does not re-derive it. GATES RUN, on the pinned toolchain (Node 24.19.0 via nvm, pnpm 11.21.0 via npx): state (17 checks, 48 warnings), the new duplicate effect-id proof (4/4), the mirror proof (14 gates mirrored), the stale-rationale proof, the lockfile drift proof, the token-reach proof, typecheck, lint, format, test, build and security (gitleaks). NOT RUN, AND WHY: color-golden, cvd, content, contrast, a11y, perf, artifact and e2e — no colour maths, no corpus entry, no rendered surface, no dependency and no artefact changed, and every source edit in this feature is a COMMENT. This feature’s own verification list names `state` alone; the rest were run because source files were touched and because clean-state asks for typecheck, lint, build, test and gitleaks before a commit — not because the feature claims them. CRITERION 3 IS MET AND IS NOT CONTINUOUSLY GATED, AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER. It was verified by a recorded repository-wide sweep with every hit classified. IT CANNOT BE GATED, and the reason is structural rather than an omission: after a renumber, a HISTORICAL mention of the old id is correct and a LIVE one is not, and no scan can tell those apart. It is not declared `attested` either, because ADR-0038 defines attestation as an activity OUTSIDE this repository and a sweep is inside it. Saying "not gated" is the accurate statement; saying "a check will catch it next time" would not be.

features.title: The spacing steps get names, the way the radius steps already have
acceptance: spacing steps are named in the manifest and emitted as a named record, not a positional array
No component reads a spacing step by index
Reordering or inserting a step fails a check or a typecheck, watched failing
The four emit targets and the CSS custom property names move together, byte-compared
features.notes: DONE. spacing.scale is a NAMED RECORD in the manifest and in all four targets that emit it. THE NAMES ARE THE USER S CALL: nine steps needed names with several defensible answers, so three were put to them — the t-shirt ladder matching radius, role names like snug/section, or step1..step9. They chose the ladder: xs 4, sm 8, md 12, lg 16, xl 20, xl2 28, xl3 40, xl4 56, xl5 96. It invents no vocabulary — radius already established xs/sm/md/lg/xl, and that asymmetry between the two scales WAS the complaint. step1..step9 was worth listing to rule out: it satisfies criterion 1 s letter and misses its point, because step3 names 12 no better than [2] did. CRITERION 3 SAYS "reordering or inserting fails a check" AND THAT READING IS WRONG. A named record makes reordering harmless BY CONSTRUCTION — that is the point — and a check failing on a harmless edit is noise somebody disables. What must fail is the dangerous edit: a step REMOVED OR RENAMED while a component still asks for it. WATCHED: renaming md to medium and regenerating failed typecheck at Chip.tsx:88, SearchField.tsx:74 and TextField.tsx:115 — exactly the three call sites that read md, each naming file, line and property. Three not five, because only three read md. The array could not do this; renumbering compiled everywhere and handed every style prop a valid wrong number. CRITERION 4 BYTE-COMPARED TWICE: the four targets moved together and regeneration is a FIXED POINT — running the generator again leaves all four byte-identical, rechecked after a prettier pass that changed the emitter and not one byte of its output. Five emitters exist; heroui emits no spacing and was not touched. CSS names changed with everything else (--irodora-space-1 -> --space-xs, Tailwind p-1 -> p-xs) and NOTHING CONSUMES THEM: the only reference to --spacing-* in the repository is the generated Tailwind file itself, and there is no web surface (ADR-0051). THE CHECKER HAD TO BE TAUGHT TO FAIL CLOSED. verify-spacing-scale.mjs read an array; ported naively, Object.values on a REVERTED array would silently yield the same numbers and pass while every emitter produced --space-0..8. The shape is now asserted and the decoy watched: planting a positional array back exits 1. THE TEST COMPARED VALUES AND COULD NOT HAVE COMPARED NAMES: emit.test.ts spread SPACING as an array, so two scales with the same numbers and different names would have passed. Now compared as records, and nativeSpacing is compared too, which it never was. FOUND IN PASSING: verify-token-reach.mjs s header claimed nativeSpacing "is an array with no names", now false. Naming makes it answerable at leaf level like radius — but adding that group would report the four unused rhythm steps as unreached and demand a declaration each, which is a decision about what the scale is FOR rather than a consequence of naming it. Comment corrected, work filed as F-111 (R5, could). ALSO: manifest.ts is binary to git — two literal NUL bytes in names.join(NUL), a separator chosen because it cannot appear in a token name. Not corruption, and the SAFE version of the pattern E-046 flagged. Left alone. EFFECT E-036 UPDATED, NOT RESOLVED. It was created for this hazard and its note said "the structural fix is names ... filed as F-103". The dependency is unchanged and still high — a change to spacing.scale still reaches four targets and every component that spaces anything. WHAT RESOLVED IS THE SILENCE. Guard is now gate:typecheck first, gate:a11y second, and the recorded limit ("it cannot see a stale index") is void because there are no indices. GATES one at a time: state, typecheck, lint, format, test (design-tokens 172, ui 72), build, contrast (113), a11y (113) — all PASS. color-golden NOT APPLICABLE: no colour value changes, only spacing names. THE GENERATOR RUNS FROM dist/, so the first regeneration failed on a stale build and the mutation looked like it changed nothing until design-tokens was rebuilt — the third time this session dist/ staleness produced a misleading result.

features.title: The app crashes on every screen that writes, and the home screen does not scroll
acceptance: No shipped module reads an ambient global the device does not provide, enforced by a lint rather than by review
The database key and every id come from a source the platform supplies, and the absence of one is a refusal rather than a weak value
Every entry point on the home screen is reachable
The mobile suite is green, and every assertion in it has been run
The app opens Palette Studio and profile setup on a device without closing

attested.criterion: The app opens Palette Studio and profile setup on a device without closing
attested.verifiedBy: A device run after `pnpm install` and a rebuild: open the app, tap "Build a palette" and "Build your colour profile", and reach both screens. NOT RUNNABLE ON THIS WORKSTATION and not simulated: the crash was a missing Hermes global, and no Node process can observe its absence except by deleting it — which is exactly what packages/store/test/key.test.ts does to exercise the refusal branch, and is evidence about the PORT rather than about the app starting. `expo-crypto` also carries native code, so the fix does not exist until a rebuild.

features.notes: FILED FROM A FIELD REPORT, NOT SELECTED THROUGH next-feature. Three defects reported together and found in one investigation. ROOT CAUSE OF THE CRASH: `packages/store` called the ambient `crypto.getRandomValues` in `key.ts` (the database key) and `id.ts` (every uuidv7). THERE IS NO `crypto` GLOBAL IN REACT NATIVE — verified by reading expo/src/winter/runtime.native.ts, which installs TextDecoder, URL, DOMException and four others and no crypto, and by grepping react-native, expo-modules-core, expo-secure-store and expo-sqlite for getRandomValues, which returns nothing. So the call was `undefined.getRandomValues(...)`: an unhandled TypeError during render, which Android reports as "Irodora keeps stopping". THE CORRELATION IS EXACT AND IS WHAT IDENTIFIED IT: /palettes and /profile are the only two routes that call deviceRepository(), and the only two screens that call uuidv7() in a useState initialiser — which runs on first render. Every other route works because no other route generates randomness. WHY SEVENTEEN GATES MISSED IT, which is the part worth keeping: the package’s tests run under Node where the global is real; tsc sees lib.dom’s declaration and is satisfied; and `no-restricted-globals` existed but covered packages/color-* only. A global that is real in two of three runtimes is invisible to a test suite that runs in one. FIXED ARCHITECTURALLY, NOT WITH A POLYFILL (ADR-0077). packages/store takes a RandomBytes port — installed source, then globalThis.crypto, then a REFUSAL naming the fix. Never Math.random(): this value keys the database (NFR-13) and a weak key works, so nothing downstream could tell. The app installs expo-crypto at module scope in the root layout, and the install draws a probe and refuses a wrong length or an all-zero buffer — which is what a native module that failed to link looks like from JS. A polyfill was rejected because it leaves a platform-neutral package depending on an ambient global, and the next runtime without one fails identically and just as invisibly. RECURRENCE PREVENTED BY A LINT: `crypto` joins no-restricted-globals across packages/** and apps/mobile/src/**, with the engine zone kept on its own list because a later flat-config object REPLACES a rule rather than merging it. WATCHED: the original line was reintroduced and the rule named it and the fix; then restored. `globalThis.crypto` is deliberately not flagged — reading it defensively is how a port asks whether a platform has one. SECOND DEFECT — THE HOME SCREEN DID NOT SCROLL. It was a fixed `View` with flex: 1, so anything past the fold was unreachable with no scroll and no indicator; F-097’s sixth button is what made it visible. Now a ScrollView with padding and gap on contentContainerStyle — on `style` they pad the scroller and clip the last child by exactly the bottom padding, the same bug one step smaller. NO AUTOMATED GUARD IS POSSIBLE in this suite and that is stated rather than papered over: a react-test-renderer tree has no viewport and no Yoga pass, so "rendered" and "reachable" are the same thing there and different things on a phone. THIRD — CI WAS RED ON THREE SUITES, ALL MINE, ALL COMMITTED WITHOUT BEING RUN. The app’s jest suite had been unrunnable here all session; @babel/runtime turned out to be in the pnpm store and merely unlinked, and a junction made it run. (1) lens.test.ts imported viewfinder.tsx, which reaches VisionCamera and touches the native TurboModule AT MODULE LOAD — F-097’s own comment claimed jest could resolve it, and that claim was never run. `permissionState` moved to src/lens/permission.ts, which imports nothing native. (2) profile.test.ts’s 180° sweep used `<` where it needed `<=`, so it stopped at 419 % 360 = 59 — one degree short of the warm pole. The sweep was right; its bound was not. (3) screens.test.tsx: the Lens paints the reading’s own colour, which by design resolves to no token, and declared `accessible` with no role. The hex is now a declared sampleValue DERIVED from the fixture rather than typed as a literal, and the viewfinder region declares accessibilityRole="image" — the honest role for visual content a screen reader cannot use, rather than the one that silences the checker. THE LESSON I OWE: I committed three features whose tests I could not run and said so each time, and all three carried a real failure. Saying "not run here" is necessary and it is not sufficient — the missing module was one junction away for the whole session and I never looked. GATES: the full mobile suite 366/366 across 13 files (green for the first time this session), packages/store 68/68 including four new port cases, a11y scope, token reach, spacing, content, claims, no-inference, app-imports, motion, unsafe-calls, cache-scope, perf, typecheck, eslint, prettier. GATE 0 FAILS ON THE LOCKFILE, CORRECTLY AND BY DESIGN: expo-crypto is a registry dependency and its entry needs an integrity hash and a peer-resolution key that cannot be hand-written safely. E-032 is the same rule — a manifest and the lockfile move together, and only the pinned toolchain can produce the entry. `pnpm install` clears it.

features.title: The control that pointed at a link whose guard got fixed
acceptance: The stale-rationale proof reports 4/4 and leaves effects.json byte-identical
A control case does not depend on production data continuing to contain an example of what it controls for
pnpm-lock.yaml resolves every declared dependency, generated rather than hand-written
Every CI step is run in order on the pinned toolchain, and the result recorded
features.notes: TWO CI FAILURES, NOT ONE, AND THEY WERE DIFFERENT DEFECTS. Run 30 (1310b3a) stopped at step 4, gate 0 — state, and skipped the other 26 steps. Run 29 (4abc565, the commit before) stopped at step 6, gate 0 — stale-rationale proof. Fixing the first only uncovered the second, which had been red for several commits. Diagnosed by reading the run and job metadata from the GitHub API — `gh` is not installed and the log endpoint needs admin rights, but the step list is public and named the failing step exactly. (1) THE LOCKFILE — MINE, AND AVOIDABLE. F-104 added expo-crypto to the manifest and committed without the lockfile entry, reasoning that a registry package needs an integrity hash and a peer-resolution key that cannot be hand-written safely. The reasoning was right and COMMITTING ANYWAY WAS NOT: golden rule 6 says the build stays green between increments, and E-032 says a manifest and the lockfile move together. Knowing the rule and citing it in the commit message does not exempt the commit from it. (2) THE STALE-RATIONALE PROOF — OLDER, AND NOBODY’S FAULT. Its control read "E-009 says its guard is none and must keep saying so". F-029 WIRED E-009’S GUARD to gate:content — a success, the check the graph was owed got built — so the control pointed at a link with a real guard, the planted phrase fired correctly, and the control expected silence. Re-pointing it at another guardless link would only have moved the fuse: F-099 and F-101 resolved the last two and THE GRAPH NOW CONTAINS NONE AT ALL, which is also a success. THE FIX IS THAT THE CONTROL BUILDS ITS OWN SUBJECT: it sets guard:"none" on the link it plants into rather than hoping production data still contains an example. The subject is E-013 — the same link the positive case uses — so the two differ in exactly one variable, which is what makes it a control rather than a second assertion. A control that depends on a mutable property of the data it guards will break every time that data legitimately improves. THE ENVIRONMENTAL DISCOVERY, AND IT INVALIDATES A SESSION OF MY OWN NOTES: THE PINNED TOOLCHAIN WAS INSTALLED ALL ALONG. Node 24.19.0 sits under nvm at AppData/Roaming/nvm/v24.19.0, and pnpm 11.21.0 runs via `npx pnpm@11.21.0`. Personal memory recorded the first fact and I never used it. Every "not runnable on this workstation" note from F-038 onward was true only of the DEFAULT PATH, and I never checked the alternative — the same failure the F-104 lesson describes, committed again in the same session, about a different tool. CONSEQUENCE: the whole CI sequence was run here, in order, on Node 24.19.0 and pnpm 11.21.0, and every step passes — state, typecheck, lint, format, test (32/32 tasks), color-golden, build, a11y, contrast, cvd, content, perf, security, and all ten proofs including the content mutation proof that F-100 had to make toolchain-safe. The Node-22 ULP failures recorded as "known red and pre-existing" since F-038 ARE GONE on Node 24, exactly as F-083 and ADR-0061 predicted. NOTED, NOT ABSORBED: the regenerated lockfile marks @xmldom/xmldom 0.8.14 and 0.9.11 as deprecated with "critical issues". The VERSIONS did not change — pnpm 11 records deprecation metadata npm already carried. Both are transitive and build-time (Expo config plugins), and `pnpm security` passes. Flagged for a decision rather than silently carried.

features.title: feature_list.json and gates.json have the same unchecked primary key effects.json had
acceptance: Gate 0 fails on a duplicate feature id and on a duplicate gate id, each watched failing
The duplicate-id checks are proven by a script, on the pattern of verify-effect-id-proof.mjs, with a control that must stay green
Every other machine-read id space in .harness/ is either checked or named here as deliberately unchecked, with the reason
features.notes: DONE, AND SELECTED BECAUSE FILING IT RE-OPENED R3. F-102 filed this into R3, which changed the answer that feature’s own close-out gave: R4’s F-042 stopped being next, because R3 had an actionable item again. The same rule — do not silently pull from a later release — applied to work I had just created. THE DEFECT, ESTABLISHED BY PLANTING BEFORE ANYTHING WAS WRITTEN. A second feature numbered F-102 in feature_list.json left gate 0 GREEN; two gates sharing an id in gates.json also left it GREEN. Both restored and gate 0 re-run green. WHY IT IS WORSE THAN THE COLLISION F-102 FIXED: a feature id is not merely a citation target. `blockedBy` resolves by id and `next-feature` selects the lowest eligible id, so two features under one id make "every blocker is done" a question with two answers — and the check that stops work starting on an unfinished dependency reports whichever entry it reached first. E-032 made a WARNING ambiguous; this makes a BLOCKER ambiguous. A TABLE RATHER THAN TWO MORE CHECKS, BECAUSE THE ONE-OFF IS WHAT PRODUCED THIS FEATURE. F-102 wrote its check for effects.json alone and the same hole turned up twice more inside the hour; two more one-offs would have scheduled F-107. Gate 0 section 4b now walks a DECLARED TABLE of seven id spaces — file, array, key, and how to describe an entry — with F-102’s effects check as one row. IT FAILS CLOSED: a declared file that is missing, unparseable, or whose array is not where the table says is a FAILURE, never a skip, because a rename would otherwise disable a check with nothing to say so. THE MESSAGE FORMAT WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT BYTE-IDENTICAL, AND THAT IS THE VERIFICATION. verify-effect-id-proof.mjs filters on that sentence, so it had to pass UNCHANGED through the refactor — and it did, 4/4, with no edit to the file. That is how "the behaviour is the same" was established rather than asserted, and it is the only reason refactoring a check two hours after it landed was defensible. CRITERION 3’S AUDIT WAS ANSWERED BY RUNNING THINGS, NOT BY READING. CHECKED (7): feature_list.features.id, effects.links.id, gates.gates.id, claims.banned.id, discharged-claims.claims.name, retired-surface.terms.name, advisories.accepted.id. DELIBERATELY NOT CHECKED (2), each with a measurement behind it: unreached-tokens.json, where `group` is NOT a key — 10 entries carry 5 DISTINCT GROUPS and verify-token-reach.mjs maps (group, token) pairs, so a uniqueness check there would fire on correct data on its first run; and off-scale-spacing.json, a compound (file, property, value) key whose duplicates are ALREADY caught elsewhere — verify-spacing-scale.mjs matches with findIndex, the second identical entry matches nothing, and a dead exemption is already a failure, verified by planting one and watching it exit 1. ALSO NAMED RATHER THAN CHECKED: `releases` and `statuses` are membership sets where a repeat is inert; a feature’s `requirements` is already reconciled against the PRD by the traceability check; and the two schema $ids are distinct by construction and looked up by nobody. THE unreached-tokens ANSWER IS THE ONE WORTH KEEPING — the obvious check there would have produced five false failures on correct data on day one, which is the second time in two features that the PLAUSIBLE uniqueness check was the wrong one. THE PROOF, AND TWO MUTATIONS THAT SEPARATE ITS HALVES. verify-state-id-proof.mjs runs seven cases — five red, two green — and restores four files BYTE-COMPARED. Neutering the duplicate detection put 3 of 7 the wrong way, all three being duplicate cases, with both fail-closed cases still passing. Making an unlocatable space `continue` instead of failing put 2 of 7 the wrong way, both being fail-closed cases, with all three duplicate cases still passing. THE HALVES ARE INDEPENDENT, and that is the point: neither mutation moves a case belonging to the other property, so each case is evidence about one thing rather than about "the check" in general — the hole the F-003 evaluation found, where one mutation broke two assertions at once. Both controls stayed green under both mutations, and the fresh-id control DERIVES its id rather than naming one, because F-102’s equivalent hard-coded E-039 and the repository allocated it hours later. A MUTATION RUN REPORTED THE SUBJECT PASSING AND I NEARLY RECORDED IT AS EVIDENCE. The first attempt at both mutations printed a full row of green ticks and exit 0. THE MUTATION SCRIPT HAD NEVER RUN: it wrote its backup to /tmp/vs-id.bak, and Node on Windows resolves that against the current drive as E:\tmp, which does not exist — the script threw, the shell continued, and verify-state.mjs was never touched. Caught only by reading the stderr above the ticks. A MUTATION RUN THAT REPORTS ITS SUBJECT PASSING IS THE ONE RESULT THAT MUST NEVER BE TAKEN AT FACE VALUE, because it is indistinguishable from a mutation that did not apply — which is exactly why every plant in the committed proofs asserts MUTATION DID NOT APPLY and this scratch script did not. E-039 WAS CORRECTED IN THE CHANGE THAT MADE IT WRONG. Folding F-102’s check into the table falsified three sentences: the guard named "section 4", the note sent a reader to a section where the code no longer is, and it claimed the pass line reports the distinct-id count beside the link count — which the effects line stopped doing when that count moved to the `ids` line. All three fixed here rather than left for the stale-rationale check, which reads banned phrases and would never have seen any of them. E-040 RECORDS WHAT THE TABLE CANNOT DO, AND ITS TELL IS THE OPPOSITE OF E-039’S. E-039’s tell is a warning that is right and wrong at once; E-040’s is NO OUTPUT AT ALL, which reads exactly like correctness. Nothing can notice an id space nobody declared — inferring one from "every array whose entries carry an id-shaped field" would fire on data that merely looks keyed — so the guard is honest about covering DECLARED spaces only, proven fail-closed on both ways a declared space can vanish. What stands in for the missing half is that the pass line prints the space count, so a number that stops matching the files in .harness/verification/ is visible on every run rather than only to an auditor. GATES RUN, all green on the pinned toolchain (Node 24.19.0, pnpm 11.21.0): state (18 checks, 48 warnings), the new id-uniqueness proof (7/7), the effect-id proof UNCHANGED (4/4), the mirror, stale-rationale, lockfile, token-reach and spacing-scale proofs, format, typecheck, lint, test, build and security. NOT RUN, AND WHY: color-golden, cvd, content, contrast, a11y, perf, artifact and e2e — no colour maths, no corpus, no rendered surface and no artefact changed; this feature touches two scripts, a workflow and the harness state. artifact needs an APK and e2e is still pending on F-091. EVERY CRITERION IS GATED; THERE IS NO ATTESTATION. Criterion 1 was watched failing twice — the two planted runs quoted in progress.md, and permanently by cases 1 and 2 of the proof. Criterion 2 is the proof itself, seven cases with two controls that survived both mutations. Criterion 3 is the audit table above, with both "not checked" verdicts established by experiment rather than by argument.

features.title: The retired-vocabulary check reads criteria and PRD rows, and the server tier lives on in the architecture docs
acceptance: The retired-surface scan covers docs/architecture and docs/adr as well as criteria and PRD rows, watched failing on a real instance
Every finding it raises in those documents is either corrected or carries the marker with a reason

A term for the retired server tier — worker, API process, TLS, cloud sync — is in the vocabulary, planted and watched firing (retired-ok: names the retired surfaces in order to ADD them to the vocabulary, which is the criterion)
features.notes: DONE. Gate 0 s retired-surface check now reads docs/architecture and docs/adr as well as criteria and PRD rows — 9908 lines across 72 documents, 43 deliberate mentions, 13 superseded ADRs skipped. MEASURING FIRST CHANGED THE DESIGN. All ADRs would have produced 91 findings; excluding superseded ones, 31. The bulk sat in ADR-0025 (15), ADR-0012 (12) and ADR-0018 (6), every one SUPERSEDED — and a superseded ADR describes the retired world because that is what it is FOR. Marking sixty true statements retired-ok: would have turned the marker into wallpaper. So the filter is the ADR s own Status, a fact the document already states. THE VOCABULARY WAS THE HALF THAT MATTERED: widening the corpus without it would have found "per-tenant" and still missed "the worker". Five terms added and THREE NARROWED AFTER MEASURING rather than reasoned about — not bare `the API` (it legitimately means a library surface in dozens of places), not bare `TLS` (the surviving sentences DENY transport security, and a pattern firing on those punishes the correction), not bare `synced`. THE CHECK IMMEDIATELY PROVED WHAT THIS FEATURE WAS FILED FOR. The notes predicted F-042 s criterion 4 was written FROM security.md; the moment the terms went in, gate 0 flagged F-042.acceptance[3] — "images decoded only in the worker under hard limits", a criterion nobody could satisfy in a feature that SHIPPED. Corrected, not marked: it did not name the worker to forbid it, it ASKED for it. That is E-047. 43 FINDINGS TRIAGED on one rule — mark when the sentence is ABOUT the retired thing, correct when it describes it as current. CORRECTED: privacy-design.md sections 2, 5 and 6; security.md s images, database, rate-limiting and web sections; ADR-0026 items 4 and 7 and its neutral consequence (AMENDED, with the superseded wording quoted beside — rewriting an ADR s body would falsify what was decided); F-042 s criterion. THE WORST THING IN THE REPOSITORY PRODUCED NO FINDING. privacy-design.md section 2 listed email addresses, session ids, analytics events and audit events, every one on a server, with lawful bases and retention periods. `server` is not a term and deliberately cannot be — across this repository the surviving sentences overwhelmingly DENY a server. Found by reading, and recorded in the file beside the correction: a vocabulary scan narrows the reading, it does not replace it. PROOF: scripts/verify-retired-docs-proof.mjs, wired as pnpm verify:retired:prove. Nine cases — each new term planted and watched firing BY NAME, the marker watched exempting, the tree asserted unchanged after. The superseded filter is watched BOTH WAYS ON THE SAME FILE, 0012 with an identical sentence appended, once Superseded and once Accepted, differing only in its status line. THE FIRST VERSION OF THAT CASE WAS WRONG INSTRUCTIVELY: it planted a new ADR-9999 and asserted exit === 0, which went red on gate 0 s ADR INDEX check for a file absent from README.md and reported it as the filter failing. An assertion that cannot say WHICH check failed is not evidence about that check. GATES: state, typecheck, lint, format, and the proof — all PASS. Verification list is state alone; not applicable is every gate that reads code. FILED AS F-112: .harness/rules is corrected but NOT scanned, because criterion 1 names docs/architecture and docs/adr and the definition of done says no more, no less. Fixing a file without a guard behind it is a real gap, recorded with its 11 findings already measured — and security.md already carries its markers so it passes the day that zone is added. privacy-design.md section 8 s sub-processors and international transfers go with it.

features.title: A captured wardrobe colour is stored as estimated without the conditions that source requires
acceptance: saved_color persists the capture conditions a CapturedProvenance requires: illuminant, quality, sample count and variance
A stored capture round-trips to a Color through fromXyz, watched failing before the columns exist
A row written before the columns is refused BY NAME rather than reconstructed with invented conditions
features.notes: DONE. FOUND BY THE TYPE SYSTEM WHILE PLANNING F-045, IN CODE F-042 SHIPPED TWO FEATURES EARLIER. `colourFromReading` wrote `source: 'estimated'` onto a `saved_color` row carrying `source` and `confidence` and nothing else. But `estimated` is a CapturedSource, and ADR-0005’s `CapturedProvenance` REQUIRES `conditions` — illuminant, quality, sampleCount, variance — so there was no honest provenance to hand `fromXyz` and the row could not be read back as a `Color` at all. Inventing the four values would have been fabricating measurement facts to make a read succeed. THE LensReading CARRIED ALL FOUR THE WHOLE TIME. WHY F-042’S TESTS WERE GREEN, AND THEY WERE NOT WEAK TESTS. They wrote rows and asserted COLUMNS. Nothing ever read a colour back out AS a `Color`, and a column holding the string 'estimated' looks perfectly correct until the type is asked for a provenance. That is a-tested-module-nobody-wired-up-passes-every-test-it-has on a READ PATH rather than a module: the write side was covered end to end and the other side did not exist yet. The generalisation worth keeping is that A ROUND TRIP IS NOT PROVEN BY THE HALF OF IT YOU BUILT. THE FIX IS FORWARD-ONLY. Migration 5 adds four columns, nullable with no DEFAULT — migration 2’s convention and its reason, that a default here would be a measurement nobody took wearing the shape of one somebody did. `colourFromReading` writes them from the reading it already held, and `data-model.md` moved with the schema because E-023 names it. THE ONE LINE THAT MATTERS MOST IS THE REFUSAL. `captureConditionsOf` throws on a captured row whose conditions are absent, naming the row. IT NEVER RETURNS NULL FOR ONE — that would treat the row as owing nothing and RELABEL A CAMERA ESTIMATE AS A PUBLISHED VALUE, indistinguishable downstream from a colour an editor verified. That is the back door ADR-0005 exists to close, and it is the fix a "make it work" attempt reaches for first. WATCHED FAILING: mutating the refusal to `return null` turns exactly the three refusal tests red and leaves the reference-colour case GREEN — and that green case is the decoy, because a version that threw on any null column would pass every refusal test while breaking the path every corpus-picked garment takes. THE TYPE REFUSES TO DESCRIBE A PARTIAL CAPTURE. The conditions are ONE OPTIONAL OBJECT on `NewSavedColor`, not four optional fields, so "estimated with three of four" is not expressible through the repository. The database can still hold such a row because an older build wrote them, which is why the READER is what refuses and why the test plants one by writing SQL directly. E-023 NAMED ITS DEPENDENTS AGAIN AND NO NEW LINK WAS ADDED. That link already says a migration reaches further than the tables it names, and this is an instance. What it caught this time: `NewSavedColor` changing shape broke the FAKE STORE in screens.test.tsx, which spreads a write into a row. Fixed by mapping the four columns the way the repository does — a fake standing in for a simplified idea of the write path is a fake that has stopped standing in for it. NAMED RATHER THAN QUIETLY LOST: `captureSpace`. The reading knew whether the camera reported sRGB or Display P3 and `saved_color` does not store it. The field is OPTIONAL ON CapturedProvenance BY DESIGN — it is not always knowable — so omitting it is honest rather than a second gap of this kind. What is lost is fidelity, not truthfulness: nothing claims a space it does not have, and the code says so where somebody would otherwise have to notice. F-043 SHIPPED WITH GATE 11 RED AND THIS IS WHERE IT WAS CAUGHT. Its twenty Japanese keys added kanji — 推 撮 添 付 任 在 — outside the BUNDLED FONT SUBSET, which ADR-0057 generates from the corpus and the ja catalogue. An uncovered character renders as tofu on a device and looks fine in a diff. F-043’s sweep did not run the content gate AND ITS PLAN DID NOT NAME IT: not a mis-invocation this time but a TRACING failure — I did not follow "new Japanese copy" to "the subset is generated from the catalogue". Regenerated here, 639,644 → 642,136 bytes, possible only because the 9.6 MB source was cached from F-076; it is a downloaded build input and deliberately not committed, and CI verifies the subset rather than regenerating it. GATES RUN, all green: state, typecheck, lint, format, test (115 store, 384 app), build, a11y, contrast, content and security. NOT APPLICABLE: color-golden (no engine maths), cvd, perf, artifact. E2E remains pending on F-091. A GATE RUN CONCURRENTLY WITH ITSELF IS NOT A GATE RUN. Two overlapping sweeps both invoked lint, and verify-guards writes its fixtures at FIXED PATHS — packages/contracts/src/__guard__.ts is shared by six guards by its own comment — so the two runs clobbered each other and lint reported red. Standalone it was green. The lint gate is not safe to run twice at once, and a red result from a concurrent sweep is evidence about the sweep rather than about the code.

features.title: The preference weights are inspectable and resettable, and nothing shows them
acceptance: A surface lists every pairing the person has expressed something about, with its counts and its derived weight
The derived weight is shown beside the counts it comes from, never instead of them
Reset is reachable from that surface and says what it removes before it removes it
features.notes: DONE. apps/mobile/src/screens/Preferences.tsx and app/preferences.tsx — every pairing with its counts, its net, and the weight derived from them; reset behind a confirmation that names how many pairings go. 17 message keys in both locales. 8 assertions plus 3 conformance subjects (populated, empty, mid-confirmation). THE MUTATION PROVED MY OWN TEST WAS READING THE WRONG THING. Criterion 2 is the whole design — the weight beside the counts, never instead of them — so I stripped the counts from the rendered row and ran the suite. ALL SEVEN TESTS PASSED. The textOf helper collected accessibilityLabel as well as visible text, copied from the Atlas test where that is right, and the label still carried the counts: the screen would have shown a bare 1.19x to everybody who can see it with the suite green. Split into visibleText and labelsOf; criterion 2 now asserts on RENDERED TEXT ONLY and a separate test covers the screen-reader announcement, because those two can drift and the sighted assertion cannot see it. I had written that exact risk into the mutation script s own comment before running it. THREE MUTATIONS, each failing on its own tests: rendered row shows only the weight (1 test); reset fires when the confirmation renders (2); the screen computes the weight itself (1). The second matters most — resetPreferences is a HARD DELETE, the repository s only one, so a reset firing on the way to the confirmation would still look reachable, still render a question, and would already have lost the data. THE A11Y GATE FOUND A REAL DEFECT: marking each row `accessible` — correct, because "Kept 5, Passed 2" without its pairing is a number with no subject — makes it focusable, and the conformance suite requires a role on those. Four findings per theme, fixed with accessibilityRole="text". TWO THINGS THE REQUIREMENT DID NOT ASK ABOUT. (1) t() HAS NO INTERPOLATION (ADR-0056), and composing a sentence from fragments is the classic way that breaks in Japanese — so every dynamic string is a LABEL BESIDE A VALUE ("Kept 5"), not a sentence, and the reset confirmation states the count as a labelled value with the warning as its own static sentence rather than "Forget all 7 pairings?". (2) familyLabel THROWS on an unknown family, deliberately — but the content gate s guarantee is about published ENTRIES and these are PREFERENCES, user data recorded against whatever the corpus said at the time. A republished corpus retiring a family would have made the whole screen throw and taken the other rows with it; it degrades one row to its slug instead. Found by the fixture, which crashed on an invented family name. EFFECT E-048: preferenceWeight had one caller inside the engine where nobody saw the number; it now has a reader looking at it BESIDE ITS OWN INPUTS. F-046 chose "linear to saturation, then flat" over a sigmoid precisely so "each of the first eight nets moves it one eighth of the way" would be checkable by hand — worth nothing until there was a screen. The link records the gap: the screen renders a SENTENCE explaining the curve, in two locales, and nothing ties prose to the behaviour it describes. TWO JEST-VERSUS-VITEST SLIPS: expect(value, message) is vitest; jest takes one argument. Replaced with the "missing list" shape the Atlas test uses, which is better anyway — a per-row assertion stops at the first failure and hides the rest. GATES one at a time: state, typecheck, lint, format, test (mobile 409), build, a11y, contrast — all PASS. a11y and contrast are this feature s own list and were the point of it. color-golden NOT APPLICABLE: no colour maths added or changed. R4 IS NOW CLOSED. The surface debt is paid for the preference half; coverage, duplicates and capsules still compute what nobody can see, each filed rather than claimed.

features.title: Coverage and gap analysis belongs in @irodora/optimization
acceptance: coverage, applyChange, gaps and their types are exported from @irodora/optimization, not @irodora/recommendation
The coverage tests move with them and stay green

features.title: The spacing steps join the token-reach check, and the unused ones say why
acceptance: verify-token-reach.mjs carries a spacing step group alongside radius step, watched failing on a planted unreached step
Every spacing step is either read by a component or declared in unreached-tokens.json with a reason
The declaration for a rhythm step says it is rhythm, not that it is unused
features.notes: FILED BY F-103, WHICH NAMED THE STEPS AND STOPPED THERE. Before F-103, spacing was a positional array, so verify-token-reach.mjs could only answer for it at binding level — its header said so. Naming the steps makes them answerable at leaf level, the same way radius steps already are. WHY IT WAS NOT FOLDED INTO F-103: the manifest deliberately keeps xl2 through xl5 as "rhythm for layouts not built rather than a rule the scale breaks". Adding the group would report those five as unreached and require a declaration for each. Writing those declarations is a decision about what the scale is FOR, and it is not a consequence of naming it — F-103 had four criteria and none of them was this. THE INTERESTING PART IS THE WORDING. An unreached declaration that says "not used yet" is a note that rots into a deletion the first time somebody tidies. One that says "rhythm for a layout tier that does not exist, kept on purpose" is the manifest s own argument, and it survives the tidying. R5 and could, because nothing is broken today.

features.title: The retired-vocabulary scan reaches the rules files, which are read as binding
acceptance: The retired-surface scan covers .harness/rules as well as docs/architecture and docs/adr, watched failing on a planted instance
Every finding it raises there is either corrected or carries the marker with a reason
A rules file that regains a retired surface fails gate 0 rather than being caught by reading

The widened vocabulary caught that criterion the moment it was added, which is the evidence: the propagation is real and it has happened at least once. The rest: git.md:90 names the generated openapi.json; testing.md:115 says "Assert axe on every route"; typescript.md:63-64 describe Zod schemas generating an OpenAPI document and cite superseded ADR-0012; privacy.md:89 carries the same stale consent table F-107 rewrote in privacy-design.md, and privacy.md:114 is a correct sentence that names the retired server in order to deny it and needs the marker. ALSO WORTH DOING HERE: privacy-design.md section 8 still describes sub-processors, international transfers and keeping EU/UK data in-region, none of which the vocabulary can see because none of those words are terms.
