features.title: Three red gates from three of my own features, and the habit that hid all three
acceptance: The spacing-scale proof works against the named-record shape F-103 introduced, watched passing
The Japanese copy F-109 added is inside the bundled font subset, and gate 11 is green
The shipped artefact declares no RECORD_AUDIO, and the reason it appeared is fixed at source rather than by widening the expectation
Every single-line run: command in ci.yml is run locally before this closes, not a chosen subset
features.notes: DONE. THREE RED GATES, ALL THREE FROM FEATURES I HAD CLOSED AS GREEN, surfaced when the user pushed this session s work. (1) CI Verification gates — F-103 turned spacing.scale into a named record, updated verify-spacing-scale.mjs INCLUDING a branch that rejects the array shape, and left that script s own --prove doing .filter(...) on it. TypeError. The proof was written against a shape its own check no longer accepts. (2) gate 11 content — F-109 s Japanese copy introduced twelve kanji outside the bundled font subset, the SAME failure F-043 had, which F-108 fixed and F-045 made a tracing step. (3) gate 16 artefact — F-043 s expo-image-picker adds RECORD_AUDIO by default (`if (microphonePermission !== false)`), for callers who capture video; this app passes mediaTypes: [images] and records no audio. THE COMMON CAUSE IS NOT THREE SLIPS. I chose which gates to run from each feature s verification list plus a habitual set, and CI does not choose. All three were reachable from this workstation before the push. FIXES. The spacing proof removes the step BY VALUE and rebuilds the object rather than deleting a computed key (no-dynamic-delete, learned on the second round). The font subset was regenerated. RECORD_AUDIO is fixed AT THE SOURCE, never at the expectation: adding it to EXPECTED_PERMISSIONS would have made gate 16 green and shipped a microphone permission on a colour tool, which is the outcome the gate exists to prevent reached by editing the thing that objected. The plugin is listed with microphonePermission: false (the only way to pass an option, since Expo autolinks it either way) AND blockedPermissions carries it as a backstop. VERIFIED AS FAR AS THIS MACHINE ALLOWS: the prebuilt manifest carries RECORD_AUDIO with tools:node="remove", the mechanism that already provably keeps INTERNET out, and only CAMERA and VIBRATE survive from that file. The MERGE is Gradle s and needs a JDK that is not here, so what is proven is that the manifest asks for removal, not that the merged APK lacks it. TWO THINGS I BROKE WHILE FIXING THIS. I killed my own CI sweep mid-proof, and TaskStop does not run a finally — bench:prove left budgets.json mutated, and format:check then failed on a missing trailing newline. A red gate caused entirely by how I was running gates. And the sweep script buffered its own stdout, so a 110-minute run showed nothing and I could not tell which step it was on; a tool that cannot report progress is not one you can wait on. CRITERION 4 — EVERY runnable ci.yml step run individually, not a chosen subset: state, gate-mirror, stale-rationale, effect-id, state-id, lockfile proofs, token-reach --prove, typecheck, lint, claims proof, format, test, golden, build, a11y, spacing proof, contrast, contrast proof, cvd, content, content proof, bench, bench proof, security, no-inference proof, audit --prove — ALL PASS. The one step this workstation cannot run is `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`; the lockfile was checked by hand instead and every workspace dependency this session added is present. GATE 16 CANNOT RUN HERE and is not claimed. EFFECT E-049 (high): a dependency can ship an Android permission that no import and no config file mentions — its own AndroidManifest folded in by the merger, or an autolinked Expo config plugin calling withPermissions. Twice now: expo-file-system with INTERNET and two storage permissions, expo-image-picker with RECORD_AUDIO. F-114 filed to check the PREBUILT manifest on every pull request, with its own criterion stating the limit — the prebuilt manifest is not the merged one, so it catches the plugin half and not the library half.

features.title: The permission set is checked on every pull request, not only at a tag
acceptance: A check reads the PREBUILT AndroidManifest.xml and asserts the permission set it will merge from, watched failing on a planted permission
It runs in ci.yml, so a dependency that adds a permission fails the pull request that adds it
It states plainly that it is not gate 16 — it reads a manifest, not an artefact, and cannot see what library manifests merge in
features.notes: FILED BY F-113. Gate 16 reads the built APK and is the only thing that catches a dependency shipping a permission (E-049). It runs in release.yml because there is no APK on a pull request — which is correct, and means the delay between introducing a permission and learning about it is a TAG. F-043 added expo-image-picker and RECORD_AUDIO; five features closed before a signed artefact said so. WHAT WOULD CLOSE MOST OF THAT GAP CHEAPLY: `expo prebuild` already runs in the build gate on every CI run, and it writes apps/mobile/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml. That file shows exactly what app.config.ts contributes — including which permissions carry tools:node="remove" — so a plugin that adds one is visible there, on a pull request, with no Gradle and no JDK. THE HONEST LIMIT, and criterion 3 exists so it is stated rather than discovered: the prebuilt manifest is NOT the merged manifest. USE_BIOMETRIC, USE_FINGERPRINT and DYNAMIC_RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED_PERMISSION are in the shipped APK and in NO file this check would read — they come from library manifests and from AndroidX at Gradle time. So this catches the config-plugin half of E-049 and not the library-manifest half, and a check that let anybody believe otherwise would be worse than no check. Gate 16 stays exactly as it is.

features.title: The Lens crashed on its first frame: a worklet called a function that was not one
acceptance: Every function a worklet calls carries the worklet directive itself, checked across the whole app rather than at the one site that crashed
The reason it is marked is in the source, so removing the directive reads as a change rather than as tidying
The record states plainly that no gate here can catch this class, and why
features.notes: DONE. THE LENS CRASHED ON ITS FIRST FRAME AND THE CAUSE WAS THREE WORDS. `sampleFrame` in viewfinder.tsx runs on VisionCamera s frame-processor thread and carries 'worklet'; it called `sampleStride` in camera.ts, which carried nothing. A worklet may only call other worklets — the Worklets babel plugin captures an unmarked import as an ordinary JS-thread function and invoking it from the frame thread throws the moment a frame arrives, which is the moment the Lens opens. I GOT THE FIRST HYPOTHESIS WRONG AND THE RECORD SAYS SO. I thought it was react-native-vision-camera@5 s peer dependencies — nitro-modules and nitro-image are not declared by the app and under pnpm are linked ONLY inside VisionCamera s own node_modules. Good mechanism, real evidence for the placement, and FALSE: React Native s autolinker walks the dependency TREE rather than the app s node_modules, and expo-modules-autolinking react-native-config reports all four resolved. That is also why the APK builds. Reverted the dependency change and its lockfile edit. THE TELL I IGNORED TOO LONG: the APK builds and installs — an unlinked native module fails earlier and louder than one screen closing. CHECKED BEFORE BELIEVING THE SECOND ANSWER: sampleFrame marked; onFrame marked and calling only sampleFrame and scheduleOnRN; sampleStride the ONE cross-module call in a worklet and unmarked; everything else Math.*, Uint8Array, array literals and frame.*; readCaptureSpace correctly unmarked because it runs on the JS thread; pixelFormat rgb valid per TargetVideoPixelFormat. THREE WORKLETS EXIST IN THE WHOLE REPOSITORY and after this change every function they reach is marked — a complete statement, not a spot fix. THE HARNESS ALREADY SAID THIS WAS UNPROVEN. F-040 s first attestation — "VisionCamera frame processors run on a worklet thread and the UI thread never blocks on colour maths" — is OUTSTANDING, and gate 0 has printed it on every run since F-040 closed. The feature shipped with the one claim that would have caught this explicitly unproven. An outstanding attestation is not paperwork; it is the list of things nobody has run. E-050 (critical): nothing here can catch this class. Jest has ONE runtime and no worklet boundary, so the missing directive is an ordinary function the lens tests call and pass; typecheck sees a normal call; lint sees a resolving import. And 'worklet' does not change JS-thread behaviour, so the tests pass IDENTICALLY either side of the bug — a green suite was never evidence. Same shape as the crypto-in-Hermes lesson. GATES: state, typecheck, format, test (mobile 409), a11y — all PASS. Those passes are evidence for ONE narrow thing: the directive changed nothing for JS-thread callers. THEY ARE NOT EVIDENCE THAT THE LENS WORKS. I cannot verify the fix; it needs a device with a camera. If it still crashes the next candidates are the frame-output configuration and the device s reported bytesPerRow, neither of which would crash BEFORE the first frame. F-116 FILED: a static check that every function reachable from a worklet carries the directive, following calls across modules — the defect was an import, so a same-file check would have passed. Its third criterion is the limit: source analysis cannot follow a function reached through a variable or passed as a callback.

features.title: Every function a worklet reaches must say so itself, checked statically
acceptance: A check walks every function reachable from a worklet directive and fails when one of them lacks it, watched failing on the exact defect F-115 fixed
It follows calls across module boundaries, since the defect was an import and a same-file check would have passed
It states what it cannot see — a function reached through a variable, a callback passed in, or a dynamic property
features.notes: FILED BY F-115, WHICH FIXED THE INSTANCE AND LEFT NO GUARD. `sampleFrame` was a worklet and called `sampleStride`, which was not one; the Lens crashed on its first frame. NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY CAN SEE THAT — jest has one runtime and no worklet boundary, typecheck sees an ordinary call, lint sees an import that resolves, and the directive does not change JS-thread behaviour so the tests pass identically either side of the bug. WHY A STATIC CHECK IS THE RIGHT SHAPE HERE: this is a boundary the type system cannot express, which is the same category as verify-engine-purity (no node:* in the engine) and verify-app-imports (Metro resolution). Those are the precedents to follow, including their habit of printing what they cannot see. THE SURFACE IS TINY TODAY — three worklets, all in src/lens — which is exactly when to write the check, because the cost of walking it by hand is about to stop being small. THE LIMIT TO STATE (criterion 3): source analysis cannot follow a function reached through a variable, passed in as a callback, or looked up on an object. A check that let anybody believe it covered those would be worse than none, and the honest version narrows the reading rather than replacing it.

features.title: A screen whose native module will not load must not close the app
acceptance: The camera module is loaded lazily, so a failure to load is a caught rejection rather than a module-evaluation throw the app cannot survive
The Lens shows what actually failed, in text a person can read out, and says the rest of the app still works
Pressing the button on a build where the camera cannot start leaves the app running
features.notes: DONE. THE APP CLOSED BECAUSE THE THROW HAPPENED BEFORE REACT EXISTED. react-native-vision-camera builds its native binding at MODULE SCOPE — NitroModules.createHybridObject('CameraFactory') — so IMPORTING it throws when the HybridObject is not registered. This repository already recorded that exact error in src/lens/permission.ts: "Failed to get NitroModules: The native NitroModules Turbo/Native-Module could not be found." app/lens.tsx imported the camera STATICALLY, so the throw happened while the ROUTE MODULE WAS BEING EVALUATED, before React rendered anything — no error boundary can catch that, and the process went down. F-115 FIXED A REAL DEFECT AND IT WAS NOT THIS ONE. A worklet calling an unmarked function crashes on the first FRAME; this crashes on the BUTTON PRESS, before a camera exists. The distinction was in the first report — "after we click on the button" — and I did not weigh it before shipping. WHAT THIS FIXES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT: it fixes the app closing, which is a defect on its own terms and the one thing addressable without the device — one screen s native dependency must never kill the process. It does NOT make the camera work; why the HybridObject is unregistered in that build is still open, and this deliberately does not guess. THREE HYPOTHESES ELIMINATED WITH EVIDENCE, recorded so nobody re-runs them: (1) the Nitro peers are not autolinked — false, expo-modules-autolinking react-native-config, the exact command settings.gradle runs via expoAutolinking.rnConfigCommand, reports all four resolved, and the dependency change was reverted; (2) the worklets babel plugin is missing so worklet is inert — false, babel-preset-expo@57 auto-adds it when it resolves and it resolves from apps/mobile; (3) autolinking shows no Android platform data for the camera stack — not a signal, it shows none for react-native-screens or gesture-handler either and both work. THE TELL I UNDER-WEIGHTED: the APK builds, installs and runs; a module missing from the build fails earlier and louder than one screen closing. THE FIX: React.lazy around the camera inside an error boundary. CameraLens.tsx holds everything needing the native module and is only loaded lazily; CameraUnavailable.tsx shows the error TEXT on purpose, because the failure is structural rather than transient, no retry helps, and "something went wrong" would delete the one fact that makes a report actionable; app/lens.tsx uses lazy + Suspense + a small class boundary (a class because componentDidCatch has no hook equivalent, and expo-router s ErrorBoundary is for render errors rather than a module that will not load). Lens.tsx is untouched, so gates 8 and 9 still assert what they did. TWO LINT ERRORS WORTH KEEPING: `unknown | null` is meaningless because unknown absorbs null — replaced with a `caught` flag, which is also more correct since what was thrown may BE null; and JSON.stringify is typed as returning string but returns undefined for undefined, a function or a symbol, so the result is checked rather than trusted. THE FONT SUBSET WAS REGENERATED IN THIS CHANGE rather than after gate 11 went red — F-113 recorded two features ago that forgetting it is this repository s most-repeated mistake. Ten new codepoints, green on the first run. GATES: state, typecheck, lint, format, test (mobile 409), a11y, contrast, content — all PASS. NONE OF THEM CAN CONFIRM THE CAMERA WORKS; they confirm the failure mode changed. STILL NEEDED: the crash log from the device — adb logcat --pid=$(adb shell pidof -s com.irodora.app). The line naming the missing HybridObject is the answer, and it is the one thing this workstation cannot produce. F-040 s attestation that frame processors run on a worklet thread remains OUTSTANDING for exactly this reason.

features.title: Frame processors need a package nobody had installed
acceptance: react-native-vision-camera-worklets is a declared dependency of the app, at the same version as react-native-vision-camera
The two are pinned exactly, so they cannot drift apart in a future resolution
The lockfile moves with package.json, so CI installs what this machine resolved
features.notes: DONE. THE ANSWER CAME FROM THE SCREEN F-117 PUT IN PLACE OF THE CRASH: "Cannot use Frame Processors - react-native-vision-camera-worklets is not installed!" It is a SEPARATE COMPANION PACKAGE and it was installed nowhere in this repository. It is NOT react-native-worklets, which has been installed all along — that one is Reanimated s worklet runtime; this one is VisionCamera s bridge onto it. The Lens uses useFrameOutput, so it is required rather than optional. Thrown by VisionCameraWorkletsProxy.ts from a bare require inside a try/catch. WHY NOTHING FOUND IT BEFORE A DEVICE DID: VisionCamera declares it in NO dependency field — not dependencies, not peerDependencies, not optionalDependencies. So pnpm install had nothing to warn about, the lockfile was complete and correct without it, typecheck never saw it because nothing in our source imports it, and THE APK BUILDS, because the missing piece is a JS module resolved at runtime. A dependency that exists only inside a try block is invisible to every tool that reads dependency metadata; the only thing that finds it is running the feature — which is what F-040 s four outstanding attestations have been saying since it closed. THE FIX AND WHAT IT TAUGHT ABOUT PINNING: declared at the same version as VisionCamera, PINNED EXACTLY. The first resolution took the bridge to 5.2.3 while the camera stayed at 5.2.2 — allowed by the caret I wrote, and exactly the drift that would reintroduce a mismatch nothing here could catch. react-native-worklets and react-native-reanimated were already pinned exactly in this file; VisionCamera s ^5.2.2 was the outlier. Both camera packages are now 5.2.2 with no range, because they are generated together and must move together. Lockfile regenerated with --lockfile-only: 22 lines, camera resolution unchanged. THREE FIXES, ONE BUG. F-115 (a worklet calling an unmarked function) was a real defect and NOT this crash — it fires on the first frame, not on the button. F-117 (the static import that made the throw uncatchable) was not the cause either, BUT IT IS WHAT PRODUCED THE DIAGNOSIS. F-118 is the cause. F-115 was shipped on a hypothesis I had not tested against the TIMING in the report, and the report said "after we click on the button" from the start. The lesson is not "guess better" — it is that the first move should have been to MAKE THE FAILURE SPEAK. F-117 did that and the answer arrived in one screenshot. GATES: state, lockfile proof, typecheck, lint, format, test, a11y, contrast, content — all PASS. NONE OF THEM CAN CONFIRM THE LENS OPENS, for the same reason nothing found the bug here: pnpm install has never run on this workstation, so the new package cannot be in apps/mobile/node_modules. CI installs from the lockfile; the device proves it. E-049 APPLIES: a new native dependency can bring its own manifest permissions. A worklet bridge should not — but "should not" is the assumption that let RECORD_AUDIO ship two features ago, so gate 16 on the release lane is where that is checked. THE CameraUnavailable SCREEN STAYS. If there is another missing piece it will name itself rather than closing the app.

features.title: The Lens says why there is no reading, instead of waiting forever
acceptance: A frame the processor cannot sample produces a reason, not silence, and the reason names which of the four refusals it was
The case no frame can report — no frames at all — is reported too
The reason appears only in the empty state, never beside a reading and never when access was refused
features.notes: DONE. THE ANSWER TO "IS IT EVEN WIRED UP" IS YES. F-040 built the whole chain and every link is present: useFrameOutput with an rgb pixel format, an onFrame worklet, sampleFrame walking the centre region, scheduleOnRN handing the sample across, read() reducing it through @irodora/color-sampling, and Lens rendering the result. Every prop and API was checked against the installed VisionCamera 5.2.2 — outputs, onSessionConfigSelected, hasPixelBuffer, bytesPerRow, pixelFormat rgb — and all are real and correctly used. So something in the chain produces nothing AND SAYS NOTHING ABOUT IT. THE REFUSAL WAS RIGHT; THE SILENCE WAS NOT. sampleFrame returned null when the region was empty, the buffer was GPU-only, or the format was planar. Refusing is correct — reading a planar buffer would produce a plausible colour from the wrong bytes, which is worse than reading nothing, and that discipline stays. But FOUR DIFFERENT FAILURES ALL PRESENTED IDENTICALLY as a live preview that never produces a reading. A frame processor that declines every frame and reports nothing is indistinguishable from one that is not running, which is exactly the ambiguity the report was stuck in. WHAT CHANGED: sampleFrame returns a discriminated outcome instead of null — the sample, or the reason it refused — and onFrame schedules whichever it got. PLUS THE FAILURE NO FRAME CAN REPORT: no frames at all. If the output never starts, onFrame never runs, so neither path is reached; a two-second JS-side timer covers it. The reason reaches the SCREEN, not a log — a log on a phone is not something the person holding it can read, and they are the only one who can see this happen. Same principle as F-117 s CameraUnavailable, which produced the last diagnosis in one screenshot. WHERE IT IS SHOWN: only in the empty state. Never beside a reading (structural — that branch only exists where the reading is null) and NEVER WHEN ACCESS WAS REFUSED. That last is a real sequence: grant, frames fail, a diagnostic lands in state, somebody revokes the permission in Settings and comes back; the screen must explain the refusal, not a frame problem from a camera that is no longer running. THE FIRST VERSION OF THE SUITE DID NOT CATCH THAT. Removing the permission guard passed every F-119 test. The revoked-permission case was added, and the same mutation now fails on exactly that test and nothing else. GATES: state, typecheck, lint, format, test (mobile 414), a11y, contrast — all PASS. A conformance subject was added for granted-with-a-diagnostic, because that line still has to meet the same contrast and type rules as everything else. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it does not make the Lens read a colour. It makes the Lens say which of four things is stopping it. IF FRAMES ARE ARRIVING AND BEING SAMPLED, the failure is downstream in read() or the display derivation and this will show nothing new — that is the real limit and the next place to look. The diagnostic is sent per refused frame: a worklet cannot hold state to throttle, and React drops a setState to an identical string without re-rendering, so a steady stream costs a bridge hop per frame and no renders.

features.title: The Lens listens to the camera error channel it had always ignored
acceptance: A camera session error reaches the screen instead of a log nobody on a phone can read
A dropped frame is reported with its reason, because producing frames and discarding them is a different fault from producing none
The frame processor entry is counted on the frame thread, so a worklet that runs and throws is distinguishable from one never invoked
features.notes: DONE. THE DEVICE REPORTED "no frames reached the frame processor". The preview is live — the screenshot shows a wall through the viewfinder with the crosshair over it — so the session runs, the device is fine and permission is granted. onFrame simply is not delivering, which rules out every sampling failure: region size, GPU-only buffer, planar format. None is reached. MY OWN DIAGNOSTIC WAS AMBIGUOUS AND THAT CAME FIRST. seenFrame was set inside deliver and report, which run on the JS thread via scheduleOnRN — so a worklet that IS invoked and then throws produced exactly the same sentence as one never called at all. Two different faults, one message: the defect F-119 existed to remove, one level down, introduced by me in the fix. Now counted on the frame thread with a Synchronizable, incremented as the FIRST statement in the worklet before anything that can throw. A ref cannot be written from a worklet, and a per-frame scheduleOnRN ping would be bridge traffic at frame rate carrying a number nobody reads until something is wrong. The two cases now read differently. THE CHANNEL NOBODY WAS LISTENING TO: useCamera accepts onError, onStarted, onStopped and onInterruptionStarted, and this screen handled NONE of them; onError defaults to a handler that logs. So a session that starts a preview and then fails to configure the frame output reports it in exactly one place — a log on a phone, which is not something the person holding it can read. That is the entire reason "a working preview and no readings" was the whole symptom. onFrameDropped is the same story: useFrameOutput installs a console.warn when you do not supply one, and a camera producing frames and discarding every one is a DIFFERENT fault from one producing none. Both now reach the screen. WHAT IS NOT TESTED AND WHY: the viewfinder cannot be rendered by jest — it imports the native module, which is the whole reason Lens takes a node instead. There is no test that can exercise these callbacks, and adding one that appeared to would be the "registered with a render that never runs" failure Lens.tsx s own header warns about. What is checked is that nothing else broke. GATES: state, typecheck, lint, format, test (mobile 414), a11y, contrast — all PASS. WHAT THE NEXT SCREENSHOT DECIDES: an error message means the session is failing and now says how; a dropped-frame reason means frames exist and are discarded; "ran N times but nothing reached the app" means the worklet runs and something after it fails; "never called" with no error at all means the output is created and attached without complaint and still delivers nothing, which points at its configuration (targetResolution HD 16:9, pixelFormat rgb) rather than at our code. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: changing the pixel format or resolution to see if it helps. That is guessing with a rebuild per guess, and ADR-0075 chose rgb for a reason that still holds.

features.title: The frame thread can say what it threw, and deliver a reading without the push
acceptance: A throw inside the frame worklet reaches the screen as its own message, instead of the console.error that react-native-vision-camera-worklets swallows it into
A sample reaches the app through a path that does not depend on scheduleOnRN, so a reading arrives even if the push out of the frame runtime is what fails
A reading always beats an error on screen: the fallback reports a throw only when nothing was sampled and nothing was refused
Reading the pixel buffer is a refusal carrying its reason, not a throw that loses it
The fallback costs nothing once the push works — it is switched off by the push, never by itself
features.notes: DONE. THE DEVICE REPORTED "the frame processor ran 51 time(s) but nothing reached the app" — the most informative sentence the Lens has produced. In two seconds the worklet was entered 51 times (about 25 fps), onError fired NOT ONCE, onFrameDropped fired NOT ONCE, and neither deliver nor report ran. Execution dies between the first statement and the delivery. WHY IT WAS SILENT, WHICH HAD TO CHANGE FIRST: react-native-vision-camera-worklets installs our worklet inside its own try/catch (src/createRuntimeThreadProvider.ts) and sends whatever it catches to console.error. Every throw the frame worklet produced WAS reported — into a log on a phone. It had been naming the fault on all 51 frames somewhere nobody can read. WHAT I RULED OUT HERE RATHER THAN ASKING THE DEVICE: I ran the app s real Babel pipeline over camera.ts and viewfinder.tsx and read the output. There is NO babel.config.js in this repository at all, so Expo 57 s Metro transformer falls back to expo/internal/babel-preset (@expo/metro-config/build/loadBabelConfig.js), and babel-preset-expo adds react-native-worklets/plugin whenever it resolves — which it does, from apps/mobile, and it is NOT gated on isNodeModule. The transform shows sampleStride, sampleFrame and onFrame all carrying __workletHash. So F-115 s class of fault is NOT what this is; the worklet chain is intact. I also read scheduleOnRN in react-native-worklets@0.11.4: from a non-RN runtime it takes globalThis.__workletsModuleProxy.scheduleOnRN(fun, globalThis.__serializer(args)), both globals installed by the native runtime and by setupSerializer() inside createWorkletRuntime s initializer, which createWorkletRuntimeForThread uses; its helpers isWorkletFunction and RuntimeKind are a worklet and a plain enum, so neither is a remote function there. It is the documented path and it looks well-formed — a reason not to accuse it, not a reason to stake the feature on it. TWO CANDIDATES REMAIN and neither can be separated from a workstation: sampleFrame throwing (most likely at frame.getPixelBuffer(), which hasPixelBuffer promises a FORMAT about, not a successful call), or scheduleOnRN failing out of that runtime. THE CHANGE MAKES ONE BUILD SETTLE IT EITHER WAY. (1) A catch writing the message to a Synchronizable — a ref cannot be written from a worklet and scheduleOnRN is itself a suspect, so the message travels on the one mechanism PROVEN working on this runtime: entered is a Synchronizable and it is what produced the number 51. (2) A delivery path that does not depend on the push — the sample is written to a Synchronizable BEFORE scheduleOnRN is attempted and the JS side polls at 4 Hz, so if the push is the fault the Lens works on THIS build. (3) Reading the pixel buffer is a refusal, not a throw: FrameOutcome exists to carry a reason to the screen and a throw at getPixelBuffer() discarded one. THE FALLBACK COSTS NOTHING WHEN THE PUSH WORKS. It early-returns on a pushed ref that ONLY the scheduleOnRN callbacks set — deliberately not seenFrame, because a polled reading setting THAT flag would switch the poll off after one frame and freeze the viewfinder on a single colour. That failure looks like success, which is why it is E-051 and not a comment. And a reading beats an error on screen: if scheduleOnRN is the fault then every frame writes BOTH a good sample and a thrown message, so the poll reads latest, then refusal, then thrown. GATES: state (18 checks), typecheck, lint, format, test (mobile 414), a11y (129), contrast (129) — all PASS. NOT RUN: the device. Nothing in this repository can execute a worklet, a Synchronizable or a frame callback; jest has one runtime and no camera. F-040 s first attestation is still OUTSTANDING and is still the only thing that could cover any of this. The Babel transform is EVIDENCE, NOT A GATE — run by hand, and nothing in CI would notice a dropped directive tomorrow. F-116 closes that, already filed for R5. WHAT THE NEXT SCREENSHOT DECIDES: readings that follow the lens means scheduleOnRN was the fault and the fallback is carrying the Lens; "the frame processor threw: ..." means sampleFrame was, and names it exactly; "the pixel buffer could not be read" means getPixelBuffer() was, now degraded to a refusal; "N byte(s) per pixel — planar" means the negotiated format is not what ADR-0075 asked for. Every branch is a sentence. NONE of them is silence. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: changing pixelFormat or targetResolution to see if it helps — guessing at a rebuild per guess, and ADR-0075 chose rgb for a reason that holds. And promoting the poll to the primary path: 4 Hz against NFR-4 s 50 ms live-pick budget is a decision, and decisions take an ADR.

features.title: The wardrobe has no browse surface, and FR-41 is recorded as covered by a package
acceptance: A screen lists the wardrobe and groups it by colour using perceptual distance, not hex string sorting (FR-41)
A saved garment can be opened, and every progressively-enriched field on it can be edited — including the price, which today can only be set at creation
REQUIREMENTS-COVERAGE.md names a feature for FR-41 whose service can actually satisfy its e2e and a11y verification
features.notes: FOUND WHILE BUILDING F-051, AND FILED RATHER THAN FIXED. FR-41 (browse, filter and group the wardrobe) is mapped in REQUIREMENTS-COVERAGE.md to F-042 with verification `e2e, a11y` — but F-042 is a `packages` feature that built the schema and the repository, and neither of those gates can apply to a package. There is no wardrobe list screen: `apps/mobile/app/wardrobe/` contains exactly one route, `add.tsx`. THE CONSEQUENCE F-051 HIT. Cost per wear had nowhere to live. The line went into OutfitBuilder because that is the only screen where a garment a person owns is on screen, and a price can only be entered at creation because no surface opens a saved garment. Both are correct for F-051 and both are the wrong long-term home. NOT PULLED INTO F-051: a browse screen is a second feature, and building one under this id would be scope nobody reviewed against a requirement. Priority `should` rather than `must` because the app is usable without it; the coverage-map row is the part that is actually wrong today, because it reports a requirement as delivered by work that could not have delivered it.

features.title: The investment signal, once somebody has decided what it means
acceptance: An ADR defines what "investment signal" means, with the alternatives taken seriously and the number it rests on named
The signal is computed from data the person actually recorded, and says so — never from an assumed number of wears
The shopping check shows it beside the three answers F-052 built
features.notes: FILED BY F-052, WHICH BUILT THREE OF FR-52'S FOUR THINGS. The PRD row reads "outfits unlocked, personal compatibility, duplicate warning, investment signal"; F-052's acceptance list names only the first three, and the acceptance list is the contract. THE TERM IS USED ONCE IN THE PRD AND DEFINED NOWHERE — the only other occurrence in the repository is an archived brainstorm about "recommended size of wardrobe investment", which is a different idea. So building it means DECIDING what it means, and that is an ADR before it is code (golden rule 7). WHY THE OBVIOUS IMPLEMENTATION IS THE TRAP. Cost per wear exists as of F-051, so the tempting signal is a projection: "at 30 wears this would be £1.52 each". THE 30 IS INVENTED. FR-46's own sentence is "absent data yields unknown, never an invented estimate", and a projection whose denominator nobody chose is that estimate wearing a conditional. An honest version would rest on a number the person's own wardrobe produced — their median wears for that garment type, say — which is computable only once wear counts exist in quantity, and F-051 made the first one possible an hour ago. REQUIREMENTS-COVERAGE.md's FR-52 row names F-052 AND this feature, so the requirement is not recorded as delivered by work that did not deliver it.

features.title: The outfit component scores say what they mean, in the reader’s language
acceptance: Every key in OUTFIT_MESSAGE_KEYS has an entry in both catalogues, and the outfit builder renders the sentence rather than the raw component name
i18n.test.ts's declared gap for OUTFIT_MESSAGE_KEYS is deleted rather than shortened, so the E-053 assertion covers the engine's whole key set
features.notes: FOUND WHILE BUILDING F-052's E-053 GUARD. `scoreOutfit` emits a messageKey per component and NONE of them is in either catalogue; `OutfitBuilder` renders `${c.component}: ${score}` — the raw identifier, in English, in both locales. So a Japanese reader sees six English component names beside six numbers. THE GAP IS DECLARED RATHER THAN EXCLUDED. `i18n.test.ts` asserts the missing set EXACTLY, so this gap is visible and a NEW unrenderable key still fails; the alternative — filtering the outfit keys out of the assertion — would have made the test quietly stop covering them, which is how a check stops checking. NOT PULLED INTO F-052: rendering them is a change to F-045's screen against FR-32, not FR-52, and F-052 had no criterion that touching it would serve.

features.title: The Lens can hand a reading to the wardrobe, which has been able to receive one since F-043
acceptance: A reading taken in the Lens can be offered to the wardrobe, so AddGarment's "use the Lens reading" control is reachable on a device
A test asserts every ReadingDestination has at least one producer, so a third destination cannot be added without one
features.notes: FOUND WHILE BUILDING F-052, AND IT IS THE F-051 LESSON A SECOND TIME. `READING_DESTINATIONS` is ['profile', 'wardrobe'] and `offerReading` is called EXACTLY ONCE in the whole app — `CameraLens.tsx`, with 'profile'. So `takeReading('wardrobe')` in app/wardrobe/add.tsx can only ever return null, and AddGarment's `wardrobe.fromLens` button is unreachable on a device. F-043 built the receiver, E-042 records the addressed-mailbox design that made two consumers safe, and the SENDER for the second address was never added. A CONSUMER WITH NO PRODUCER — [[a-column-nothing-writes-makes-its-own-feature-unfalsifiable]] applied to a mailbox rather than a column, and invisible for the same reason: every test that exercises the wardrobe path supplies the reading itself, so the fixture is the missing sender. THE SECOND CRITERION IS THE POINT. Adding the offer fixes today; asserting that every destination has a producer is what stops the third one repeating this. NOT PULLED INTO F-052: the shopping check deliberately does not take a Lens reading — F-040's first attestation is still outstanding, so no reading has been observed reaching the app on a device, and building a third consumer of a path nobody has seen work would be two dead routes instead of one.

features.title: The outfit scanner reaches a camera, once the Lens is known to deliver a reading
acceptance: The frame processor can hand over a whole-frame sample set, not only the centre region, and the frame is still disposed on the worklet thread
A person can scan an outfit, see the proposed bands over the viewfinder, drag them, and read the per-garment colours and the score set
A refusal from proposeBands or from any slot reaches the screen as a sentence, never as an empty result
features.notes: BLOCKED ON F-040'S FIRST ATTESTATION, NOT ON F-054. The scanner's maths, its refusals and its score set landed in F-054 and are tested; what is missing is pixels. `sampleFrame` in viewfinder.tsx walks ONE CENTRE REGION, and widening it to a whole frame is a change to the exact code path F-117 through F-121 have been debugging — as of F-121 NO READING HAS BEEN OBSERVED REACHING THE APP ON A DEVICE, and the build that would settle why is still unrun. Putting a second unproven path on top of an unproven one would make the next device report ambiguous again, which is the specific failure F-120 was filed to remove. THIS IS F-031'S SHAPE AND IT IS DELIBERATE. That feature built six component scores and could not show them; its own note said so, and F-045 rendered them once there was a surface to render them on. Same here: the estimator exists and is checkable, and the surface waits for the input to be real. WHAT UNBLOCKS IT: F-040's attestation — frame processors run on a worklet thread and a reading reaches the app — discharged on a device. Not another commit here. THE THIRD CRITERION IS THE ONE THAT WILL BE TEMPTING TO DROP. `proposeBands` refuses a uniform frame, a frame too short, and a frame with no real boundary; `scanOutfit` refuses a band with no usable pixels. Every one of those is a sentence somebody needs to read, and a screen that renders an empty result for them would put back exactly the ambiguity F-119 removed from the Lens.

features.title: Two static scans read a string literal as a reference
acceptance: A file that names unsafeFromHex in a comment or a string is not reported as a call site by verify-unsafe-call-sites.mjs
A test containing a path-shaped string it does not open is not reported as a cross-package read by verify-cache-scope.mjs
Both still flag the real thing — proven by decoy files each check must accept and must reject
features.notes: FOUND BY F-055. `scripts/verify-unsafe-call-sites.mjs` decides a file is a call site with `readFileSync(file).includes('unsafeFromHex')` — a substring match over the whole file, comments included. So `apps/mobile/src/measure.ts` was reported as an UNREVIEWED CALL SITE for a doc comment that said the opposite: that a typed measurement is `reference` while the unchecked hex path stays `declared` and is NOT taken. THE WRONG FIX WAS AVAILABLE AND WAS NOT TAKEN. Adding the file to REVIEWED would have made lint green by declaring a call site that does not exist — and worse, it would have pre-approved a REAL call there, which is the one thing the census exists to prevent. The sentence was reworded to avoid the identifier instead, which is why the comment now describes the function rather than naming it. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE COMMENT: the check's whole argument is that a sentence about people is not a check. A check that cannot tell a call from a sentence teaches people to stop writing the sentences — and the documentation it suppresses is exactly the kind that says which boundary is being preserved and why. FAILING CLOSED IS RIGHT AND IS NOT THE ISSUE: an import or a call expression is what should trip it, and both are distinguishable from prose without a parser. THE SECOND CRITERION IS THE POINT. `verify-guards.mjs` already carries decoy files that its rules must ACCEPT and must REJECT; this needs the same, or a narrowed matcher will quietly stop matching anything. SECOND INSTANCE, FOUND BY F-056 AN HOUR LATER. `verify-cache-scope.mjs` reported `packages/export/test/export.test.ts` as reading `packages/etc/passwd` — because the test asserts that `slugify('../../etc/passwd')` cannot produce a traversal. A traversal LITERAL is indistinguishable from a read to a textual scan, exactly as a mention is indistinguishable from a call. The fixture was assembled from parts instead, with the reason written beside it, and the assertion is unchanged. TWO SCRIPTS, ONE DEFECT: both decide what a file DOES by matching text in it. Failing closed is right and is not the issue — what is missing in both is the distinction between a reference and a mention, which an import, a call expression or a read call makes visible without a full parser. THE COST IS THE SAME BOTH TIMES: the check pushes people to stop writing the literal that explains the thing, and the explanation is the part that was worth having.

features.title: The Lens needs minSdk 26, because the pixel buffer it reads is compiled out below it
acceptance: The Android build sets minSdkVersion 26, so Nitro compiles its AHardwareBuffer support in and Frame.getPixelBuffer() returns a buffer instead of throwing
The minimum is declared in app.config.ts, which is the only source CI prebuilds from — android/ is generated and untracked
The decision to leave Expo default 24 is recorded as an ADR, with what it costs
A check fails if the declared minimum drops below what the Lens needs, rather than the Lens failing on a device
features.notes: DONE. F-121 s instrumentation was built so one build would settle a two-way split. It did, and the answer was NEITHER candidate: "the pixel buffer could not be read: Frame.getPixelBuffer(...): java.lang.RuntimeException: ArrayBuffer(HardwareBuffer) requires NDK API 26 or above! (minSdk >= 26)". THIS WAS NEVER A JAVASCRIPT FAULT — thrown from C++, through Kotlin, into a worklet, and no amount of TypeScript could have found it. THE MECHANISM: react-native-nitro-modules guards its entire AHardwareBuffer implementation on a COMPILE-TIME constant, #if __ANDROID_API__ >= 26 ... #else throw std::runtime_error(...). __ANDROID_API__ is set by the NDK from Gradle s minSdkVersion and Nitro takes the app s value directly. This repository never set one; ExpoRootProjectPlugin.kt defaults it to 24, so the whole native tree compiled at 24 and the #else is what shipped. On the device, ImageProxy+getPixelBuffer.kt prefers a CPU-readable HardwareBuffer whenever SDK_INT >= P (28); a modern phone is, and ADR-0075 s pixelFormat rgb gives CameraX an RGBA_8888 ImageProxy that is exactly that. So the fast path is taken on every frame and the fast path is a throw. WHY hasPixelBuffer SAID YES: it asks the same question with only the RUNTIME half. One is a property of the DEVICE, the other of OUR BUILD. Nothing on the JavaScript side could ever have bridged that, which is precisely why F-121 s try/catch around getPixelBuffer() was worth having — it turned an invisible throw into a sentence, after four device round trips. E-054. THE CHANGE: expo-build-properties with android.minSdkVersion = ANDROID_MIN_SDK (26), exported from app.config.ts so a gate reads the number rather than greps for it. IN app.config.ts AND NOWHERE ELSE: apps/mobile/android/ is generated and untracked and both workflows run expo prebuild --clean, so a hand-written value works locally and vanishes on the next run. 26 NOT 28: 26 is the number in the #if; a device on 26-27 never reaches the HardwareBuffer path and falls to the single-plane branch, which works. There was NO JavaScript alternative — the fast path is chosen by SDK_INT and the buffer s own usage flags, neither reachable from our code, and the only remaining lever (pixelFormat yuv) is what ADR-0075 refused. THE CHAIN VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: prebuild was RUN and android/gradle.properties read back showing android.minSdkVersion=26; then android.minSdkVersion -> catalog key minSdk (ExpoAutolinkingSettingsExtension.kt:117) -> rootProject.ext.minSdkVersion (ExpoRootProjectPlugin.kt:53, default "24") -> Nitro s getExtOrIntegerDefault. THE GUARD: scripts/verify-android-min-sdk.mjs, wired into gate 2 and mirrored in CI. Seven cases, decoys watched failing. The ones that MATTER are the LOWERED values — 24 and 25 both rejected — because a check that only noticed a MISSING number would pass the edit that actually happens: somebody widening device support. Two more reject a plugin hard-coding the number instead of passing the constant, INCLUDING when the literal is 26, because two numbers that can disagree is the shape this regresses in. The real config stays green. WHAT IT COSTS: Android 7.0 and 7.1 can no longer install the app. Close to zero, because the app ALREADY did not work there and NFR-7 sets the bar at a four-year-old mid-range Android (API 31+ in 2026). Declaring 24 was a claim the binary could not honour. ADR-0079. GATES: state (18), typecheck, lint (incl. the new check), format, test (516), verify:minsdk:prove — all PASS. NOT RUN: the NDK compile and the APK. Gate 16 needs an Android toolchain this workstation does not have; that is F-039 s attestation, still OUTSTANDING. Everything verified here stops at the generated gradle.properties. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: touching apps/mobile/android/ (generated, erased by the next --clean prebuild); changing pixelFormat (ADR-0075 holds and this fault is not evidence against it); moving targetSdkVersion or compileSdkVersion (neither implicated, both their own decision).

features.title: The export formats reach a screen, and a CJK-capable PDF
acceptance: A person can export a palette or a batch-compare result in any of the six formats, to a file they chose
A PDF report can draw kanji, kana and the macron romaji — an embedded subset, with a ToUnicode map so the text is selectable
A palette exported as design tokens or JSON can be imported back, and the round-trip is asserted
features.notes: FILED BY F-056, WHICH BUILT THE FORMATS AND DELIBERATELY NOT THE SURFACE. `service` there is `packages` and its verification list is `state, test` — no a11y, no e2e — and F-035 already owns the export JOURNEY (writing to a file the person chose) with the attestation for it. Wiring six writers to a screen is a mobile feature. THE PDF HALF IS ADR-0080's RECORDED COST. The report is Latin-1 under base-14 Helvetica, so no kanji, no kana, and none of the nine corpus romaji carrying macrons can appear in one; a character it cannot draw is REFUSED BY NAME rather than dropped. Fixing that means a TrueType parser, a cmap walk, a subsetter and a ToUnicode CMap — a font pipeline, which inside an export-formats feature would have been scope nobody reviewed against a requirement. THE IMPORT HALF IS FR-28's SECOND CLAUSE, and it waited for this feature on purpose: an importer written before its exporter has no format to agree with. Now there is one, and the round-trip is assertable. NOT A REASON TO DELAY THE SURFACE: five of the six formats carry every character today, so a person can export a Japanese-titled palette as JSON, CSV, CSS or tokens the moment a screen offers it. FILED AS F-129 AND NOT F-128, which was already taken by a done R4 feature — the id was checked against the list rather than counted from the last one this session touched.
